TITLE: Minor RTA
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Location = M25 J25 4 lane roundabout above M25 from Enfield.

Parked up on inside lane of roundabout with handbrake on waiting for lights to change.

Observed odd activity from girl in car behind during queuing for a while to get to my parked position.

Watched her in rear view mirror engaging with a passenger in the back seat of her car – she turned around throwing a coat or something, and, I can only assume, let her foot off the clutch and drove into the back of me, so no handbrake on.

She immediately held her hands to her face in shock.

I gestured to acknowledge I had felt it!

My back felt the impact in 3 places – coccyx area, below shoulder and neck – all is OK for now, but my coccyx does still feel like it has been impacted. I will monitor to see if it doesn’t resolve itself.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
I got out of the car to indicate for her to follow me to a safer area, rather than hold traffic up and risk cars hitting us – the traffic lights began to change at this time so no time to get details or reg.

She then backed up and shot across the 3 additional lanes and left the roundabout in a lane she wasn’t positioned to take – prompting lots of horns and an annoyed driver to chase after her.

I exited on to the M25 because I could not get across to pursue.

Car drove (and still does) OK and on Inspection showed no damage from the impact.

TITLE: CDC Full Load Trip
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
At 16:40h the unit had a full load trip from 386MW/SO. ROMS was called at 16:51h. The unit was REMIT'ed out to 21:30h at 0MW. after investigation it was found that the trip was caused by aIP By-pass trip signal (10MAN51EZ001) which was instigated by a IP water injection flow protection (10MAN53EZ110). The IP by-pass spray water flow went below 0Kgs (-0.5kgs) on channels A and B, which has caused the unit trip. The IP by-pass was closed at the time and the IP Throttle valve was at 99% open. Paul Cockram and Will Hammond investigated the trip. A temporary simulation has been put in place whilst a Siemens recommend MOD is put in place.

Unit re-synchronised at 20:42 .
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The unit was made safe and put on turning and the unit SGC was turned around ready for a restart. ROMS and stuart Noble was called at 16:51h, and the ops shift started a investigation in to the trip.

waiting for a Siemens recommend MOD to be put in place

TITLE: U6 HP Bypass failed to operate correctly and boiler safety valves operated
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
When taking U6 off load the HP bypass spray wasn't controlling properly causing high after bypass temperatures and tripping the HP Bypass.This is a known issue so we were expecting this to happen. Due to the Bypass trip the HP header pressure rises as the steam has nowhere to go. When the bypass was reset it was noticed that the process value on the HP bypass was struggling to meet the set point and was lagging behind quite a bit. This caused the HP header to rise significantly and the safety valves lifted. At this point the unit was off load but it was noticed that the GT EV burners were still lit adding to the high steam pressure situation. We tried to put an 'OFF' on the GT sequencer but this didn't work so we used the emergency trip button located on the unit desk. Once the flames were out the pressure started to subside but the HP bypass was still clearly not controlling as it should.Due to the significance off the HP bypass the unit was MEL'd to 0MW until 12:00 01/10/24
There are x3 issues here:
1. HP Bypass spray water control not controlling well enough to stop the HP Bypass tripping on high temperatures
2. Hp Bypass process value not following the set point as it should.
3. The GT not shutting down correctly and taking the flames out when the Circuit breaker was opened.

TITLE: Commercial loss due delayed start.
CASE_DESCRIPTION: After suffering a GT trip during the start at 05:30 (separate synergie entered for this) the unit synchronised at 07:30. During the hold period it became evident that the Steam Turbine X5 criteria would not be achieved for a number of hours. GT load was held back at 60MW which is unusual as this load should be around the 90MW mark. GT exhaust temperature was 465 degrees C which seemed low for the required HP steam temperature to clear X5. Theory that some HOF settings may be interring with run up, so a decision was made to shut the unit down and start again. Second attempt HP bypass appeared to behave as expected i.e. in flow control vs pressure control on previous attempt and X5 criteria was clearing at a more accelerated rate. GT load was held the same causing a prolonged hold period of 1hr 10mins vs 40mins expected. Looking back at previous starts the GT load is being pegged back at 60MW vs 90MW expected.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Raised with ROMs

TITLE: Harness/fall arrest inspection by British Engineering Services - Harness found with the wrong safety markings
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During the Fall Arrest inspection yesterday, Integral delivered a new harness for inspection, which failed. The Inspector noted that some of the catches were the wrong way round and while this isn’t a failing in itself it would make the harness uncomfortable to wear, as the catches would rub on the chest of anyone wearing it.

Facilities don't keep their own inspection register.

IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Harness was destroyed at the inspection, discussions with Facilities to locate who and where this was purchased from.  
Facilities to set their own account with BES and a register of their harnesses.

TITLE: Failed Trip Test on control Transmitters of Fuel Gas Heater Stream A
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
While completing fuel gas stream A underperformance investigation and rectification, it was discovered that the fuel gas heater failed to trip when the transmitter is placed in open loop. 

This means that any failure of this nature would not be detected and the control room has no visibility  of the transmitter. Therefore, if the control transmitters (EKC20ZT006 or EKC20ZT008) were to open circuit it would drive the heaters to 100% output!
(The control and trip transmitters utilise the same cabling so have a massive common cause failure).

This could lead to disabling of the protection layer, as the control system drives energy into the heaters.

TITLE: BHC Incomer Monitoring Incorrect Fuse Ratings
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Engineering investigated a report from operations regarding BHC switchboard voltage monitoring reading 0V. Upon investigation, it was found that out of the three inline fuses feeding the switchboard monitoring equipment (one fuse per phase), two of the three had blown. It was also noted that the fuse ratings were incorrect and mismatched (2A on L1 phase, 4A on L2, and 16A on L3). The 16A fuse was still intact. The datasheet for the monitoring equipment specifies a maximum ampacity of 3A, suggesting that the 16A fuse was significantly over-rated, and this is likely why it did not blow at the same time as the other two fuses. Incorrect fuse ratings can lead to damage of downstream equipment and poses a potential fire risk in the event of an overcurrent fault.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: fuses replaced with correct rating and synergi raised

TITLE: East Building Lift - British Engineering Services Inspection - Lift taken out of service due to safety concern raised by the Inspector

TITLE: Water treatment plant  - Failure of effluent dosing pipework
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Whilst dealing with an analyser problem in the WTP it was noticed that there was water spraying from somewhere approximately 3 metres above ground level.  Further investigation identified that it was from the dosing pipework for effluent system 2 which was in service and in the process of neutralising the effluent tank.  I immediately went to local control room and stopped effluent system 2 and made it unavailable. The leak was from plastic pipework that travels over the top from the pumps to the ejector skid.  This pipework fails regularly as a result of movement when the pumps stop/start or a dose of either caustic or HCL is applied.  At the time of the leak the PH of the tank was 13 so it was dosing with HCL.  The leak would have been a mixture of HCL and motive water.  The area is always barriered off due to the regular failings off the plastic pipework used on this system. Notification raised for repair to be carried out.  Improvements to the plastic pipework need to be made as this is a regular occurrence.
HAZARD: Toxic substance or CMR substance (carcinogenic, mutagenic, reproduction toxic)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: System made unavailable.  Redesign of pipework to mitigate this issue happening again

TITLE:
STATION AUX TRANSFORMER  2 INCOMER
 3.3kV CB Closed in Remote when in Local.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Station Aux Transformer 2 Incomer was closed from the DCS with local mode still selected at the breaker. This should not have operated and is a danger to anyone locally operating or attempting to rack the breaker out with remote operation still active.
Following a trip on Station service board feeder 2 3.3Kv breaker, the Station Aux Transformer incomer 3.3kV breaker was opened to deaden the board while the tripped breaker was investigated/made safe. On entering the switch house the Station Aux Transformer incomer 3.3kV breaker was placed in local control to prevent livening the board whilst personnel were present in the switch room.
Once the tripped breaker had been removed from its cubicle and it was safe to re-energise the board, the remaining personnel left the switch room and Station Aux Transformer 2 Incomer 3.3Kv breaker was closed remotely; after confirmation the breaker was closed, personnel re-entered the switch room to ensure that the breaker and board looked healthy. It was then discovered that the breaker was still in local operation mode. The breaker was placed back into remote operation and the 415v boards normalised.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Defect raised, synergi raised. Electrical team investigating.

TITLE: Delays in meeting PN sync time and further imbalance on run-up
CASE_DESCRIPTION: The unit had a PN sync time of 16:00 after the return to service from the CW pipe repair . Unfortunately due to LP drum levels having a large split between each level transmitter the sync was delayed. The delay was remitted in half hour periods on 4 occasions until the decision was made to remit the sync time out to 20:00. Our trading colleagues pulled the PN and re-scheduled it for 20:00. Unit synchronised at 20:00 and ran up until a delay was incuured on the ST program, this was due to the seal steam pressure being at 2.9 bar as opposed to the required 3 bar in Step 8 of the ST program. The delay caused a temperature imbalance between the boiler and ST ESV/Control valves not usually present on a cold start holding the ESV's from opening as required.

•	Currently we are unaware of a specific mode of failure. General arrangements are understood from pipework build drawings. Any transition/dissimilar metal welds could be in question on the OTCs inlet and outlet pipework.

4)	We are considering an NDT inspection scope strategy for suitable opportunity .

5)	Based on further information from GE when it is received, and/or information obtained from an NDT strategy, we will review the PEM120 risk assessment controls and exclusion zone requirements. A further detailed specific risk assessment may also be required.

TITLE: NRW received an incident report from a member of public
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Contacted by NRW via phone with confirmation by email regarding complaint:

As discussed, at 13:30 on Friday 28th February NRW received an incident report from a member of public.

It states the following

Caller concerned about clouds of smoke/gas discharging from Connahs Quay power station noticed yesterday and is happening again today. Caller has tried contacting site direct, but the number given is not being answered. Caller says she doesn't want an excuse of "condensation", as she claims "condensation would evaporate, but these clouds are hanging about for 2 days".

Reply to NRW from Environmental Advisor:

Hello and many thanks for your email. 

We’re keen to ensure all environmental complaints / enquiries regarding the Power station are answered as quickly as possible. As you may be aware, last weekend (Feb 28th to March 2nd) has been a time of very low wind levels, bright sunshine, clear skies and generally cold atmospheric conditions. 

Shown below is a screen grab of the weather entry for Hawarden weather station for Feb 28th 2025

As a result we were called to run three CCGT Units for the majority of Friday and at times four units ran together over the weekend. 

I’ve checked with our operational staff and can state we were called to run three CCGT Units for the majority of Friday and at times four units ran together over the weekend,  on all these occasions the machines ran successfully, with no incident or issue and well within our emission monitoring limits as specified by the site’s Natural Resources Wales regulated Environmental Permit. As you may recall our Gas Treatment Plant closed in 2023 and is no longer operational. 

As a result, I can only conclude that the complainant is referring to the significant cooling tower plume which would be produced by active generational levels on a cold and crisp winter day. The uncommon environmental conditions are very likely to result in the large scale formation of such plume, made more visible by the cold clear winter skies. 

This emission of cooling tower vapour is permissible inline with current environmental legislation. Should you have the ability to contact the complainant then we would be interested to know which phone number was rung and failed to contact the power station. Clearly we’re keen to ensure there is always a clean means of communication in times of potential incident complaint and we can seek to correct any incorrect phone numbers which might exist anywhere. 

Please don’t hesitate to contact myself should you require any further information regarding this issue.

TITLE: HCl tanker leak developed in offloading point.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During pressurisation of a delivery tanker of HCl to the WTP, a loss of fluid was observed from the foot valve area on the underside of the Brentag delivery tanker.  The tanker was immediately depressurised to reduce leak to a low flow. The fluid produced some gassing which was damped down using a fine spray from a washdown hose. The area was immediately barriered off to avoid unprotected persons entering the area. All forwarding systems for wash down residues was stopped and site surface drains closed. HVAC systems for adjacent buildings was stopped. Security informed to block access to site. Brentag driver requested assistance from Brentag emergency response team as per company procedure. Decision by Emergency Controller, in consultation with exec team, to ask site personnel to leave in a staggered approach to minimize risk of mass egress of 200+ staff (station on outage), rather than initiate sitewide evacuation. All persons confirmed off site by 15:03. External pump used to transfer product from tanker to designated delivery point. Leak flow decreased during transfer period and finished upon full transfer to tank. Tanker off site 17:30. Boiler Clean Drains Tank contents monitored and measuring 1.8pH. Advice sought from site chemist who approved use of Sodium Bicarbonate to neutralise contents of site chemically contaminated drains tanks. Tanks neutralised and monitored – in compliance with discharge permit. Discharged in purge.
No harm to persons or risk of as all control measures for delivery being followed as per approved operational procedure.
Full report to follow.
HAZARD: Hazardous substance, which is non-toxic, non-CMR substance (carcinogenic, mutagenic, reproduction toxic)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Immediate actions are covered in case description. Awaiting investigation from Brentag.

TITLE: Electric fire pump newly fitted NRV 19SGA12AA002 gasket failed while charging the system.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Electric fire pump discharge side: New NRV (Non Return Valve) 19SGA12AA002 was fitted yesterday (20 Nov 2024). 

System was deisolated this evening & filled, then completed the system walkdown for leak checks, no leaks were found. system was at around 2.5 bar with raw water tank head pressure. 

Then while during the process of pressurising the the system back to it's normal working pressure using the Jockey pump; at around 6 bar ; the newly fitted NRV gasket joint failed & started spraying huge amounts of water everywhere inside electric fire pump house.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Immediately switched off the jockey pump to stop pressurising the fire system, isolated the leaking NRV 19SGA12AA002, by shutting the electric fire pump inlet & isolating valves, pump recirculation valve. monitored for the leak to die down and stop. 
barriered the area, put no access signs to prevent any access, cleared water with squeeze mop, made area safe.

TITLE: PEM 120 - Grain - Gas Ignition Block Overpressure Integrity Risk
CASE_DESCRIPTION: GT Ignition block gauge is being subject to gas pressure potentially beyond its design pressure. This synergi is captured as per PEM120 exclusion zone requirements. Please see GE Help case 20240222-0255 for further details and Depp Data.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
1) Exclude access to the auxiliary skid top of lube oil tank from unit ignition through to shut down as risk is present at many and uncertain running conditions particularly the TRIP risk. 

2) If integrity was breached the purge credit system would likely fail due to leakage in the system while it’s applied. 

Monitoring Action: Operations team to monitor purge credit system status across all units and if the system fails, the operations team should carry out a gas leak check in the area local to ignition block as soon as possible after shutdown. If the atmosphere is safe, then carry out a local leak check of the ignition block assembly with leak detection spray to see if any leak persists. Additionally the assembly should be visually inspected for any signs of damage or leakage. 

3) Plan to remove the gauge and replace with a plug to eliminate risk of leakage via the gauge until a full solution is developed to reinstate the gauge. GE recommended and confirmed with ignition block OEM. Once plugged the exclusion zone is no longer required.

TITLE: Unit 71 Brushgear, possibility of snapped carbon brush dropped into slipring box.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:

The brush holder was noticed to be tight on insertion, which is not uncommon, was removed and found to have a broken brush with part missing. The brush holder was checked by two experienced brush gear nominated CP's before it was returned to the brush box, the person carrying out the work was under training and the close supervision of the two experienced CP's.
The brushbox was then visually inspected by both experienced CP's but the broken off piece could not be found.
The area around the brush gear has also been checked and cleared.
This was Brush B12, it should be noted that the section missing is carbon only.

14/04/2024
Opportunity to visually inspect brush gear off load more thoroughly, no evidence of broken piece anywhere in brush box location, more confident that broken piece is not in brush box.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Control person and Unit operator notified, Site electrical Strategy engineer informed. At the first off load opportunity the brushgear will be re-inspected.

TITLE: MUW Strainer 2 Backwash Pump Overload Setting Too High
CASE_DESCRIPTION: During investigation of a tripping issue on Strainer 1 backwash pump, it was observed that the adjustable overload device for Strainer 2 backwash pump was set to the maximum of 25A, presumably during original commissioning. The motor's rated FLC is 14.2A at 415V, so setting the overload device to 25A effectively removes the overload protection from the motor in the event of a fault. This can result in serious damage of plant as well as the potential for fire which carries a risk to personnel.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Overload setting to be adjusted to correct level.

Overload settings of other adjacent equipment to be checked for correct settings.

TITLE: U7 Chimney Stack integrity failure (external RCA in progress - (EXTENDED 31/12/2022 Panel of Enquiry) 14/10
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
At 13.20 on Friday 18th February 2022 the integrity of Unit 7 Chimney Stack failed in high winds. The chimney stack collapsed and folded at a height of approx. 35-40m onto the corner of the HRSG roof, causing the top of the stack to collapse down the north side of the building in between Unit 7 and Unit 6.
Unit 7 GT Trip Push Button was initiated from the CCR at 13.21.
Unit was shut down as safely as possible with the GT & ST going On Barring. U61 was also shutdown in a controlled manner as a precaution, whilst U81 was already non operational due to Outage activities progressing.
A full site evacuation was ordered, with all site personnel and contractor workers being fully accounted for. There were no reported injuries or off site local impacts as a result of the collapse.

This incident occurred during storm Eunice, with a red weather warning Met Office alert having been issued earlier that day (having already been upgraded from an Amber alert issued the previous evening). Site had already implemented the high winds procedure which restricted any external work activities. This measure was agreed and communicated following the morning meeting performance dialogue. At approx. 12:00 hrs, as a further control measure all non essential works were ceased on site, with all contractor workers being stood down and returning to their respective office/messroom facilities.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Unit 7 was manually tripped and shut down safely - MEL'd to Zero until further notice pending investigation.
U61 was also shutdown in a controlled manner as a precaution, whilst U81 was already non operational due to Outage activities progressing.
A full site evacuation was ordered, with all site personnel and contractor workers being fully accounted for. There were no reported injuries or off site local impacts as a result of the collapse.

TITLE: U7 Safety Valves Lifted after ST trip (Ref A1 for further investigation No. 41001918)
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
At 10:20am the ST tripped without warning. This cascaded into a full GT trip and lifting of IP safety valves.
The trip was caused by maintenance testing a thrust bearing TC which had been BDQ for a while. During the testing, the temperature was simulated through the range and when the trip value was exceeded, the ST tripped.
The control person was not aware of the testing, although the unit operator had been informed.
During the trip, the IP Bypass function group was deactivated by the control system and prevented the bypass from opening when required. This led to the IP safety valves lifting.

TITLE: Excavation works
CASE_DESCRIPTION: An excavation was being completed to expose electrical cables as part of the decommissioning works. On inspection there were aspects of the excavation which could be improved such as the access into the excavation and the angle of response for the battering and stepping.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Work was stopped and a review was completed and an action plan implemented to allow the works to proceed.

Response to Excavation Inspection Findings:

During the excavation to expose electrical cables as part of the decommissioning works, several areas for improvement were identified, specifically regarding access into the excavation and the angle of response for the battering and stepping.

Access to the Excavation:
Safe access and egress from an excavation are critical for worker safety. The current access should be assessed to ensure compliance with safety regulations. 

Recommendations include:
Installing proper ladders or steps to provide stable and safe access points.
Ensuring that the access route is free from obstructions and is clearly marked.
Evaluating whether the current access meets the required slope and angle guidelines to prevent slips, trips, or falls.

Angle of Response for Battering and Stepping:
The angle of the batter (slope) should be reviewed to ensure that it is adequate to prevent soil collapse. If the excavation is too steep, it increases the risk of collapse and makes it more difficult for workers to move around safely. Suggestions include:

Adjusting the slope to meet the recommended safety angles based on the soil type, depth, and stability.

Implementing proper benching and stepping techniques to reduce the risk of soil failure.

Regularly inspecting the slope to account for any changes in ground conditions during the excavation process.

Recommendations include:
Risk Assessment: A thorough risk assessment should be conducted to identify and mitigate any additional hazards associated with the excavation, ensuring compliance with all relevant regulations and best practices.

Training: Ensure all personnel working in and around the excavation have received the necessary training on excavation safety, including proper access methods and the importance of maintaining correct angles for the battering and stepping.

By addressing these points, the excavation process can be made safer, reducing the risk of injury and ensuring a compliant work environment.

TITLE: Ops Loss - U2 Outlet dust high due to 'C' Precip pass performance.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Following U2 RTS on Tuesday 25th June, the unit had to be MEL'd to 350MW from approx 18:00 to 21:00 to recover the daily dust position.  The MEL was raised to 400MW from approx 21:00.  MEL has remained at 400MW due to 'C' Precip pass being shut away.

The Unit had several milling plant issues on RTS, and the inlet dust to FGD was high, especially on the 'B' side.  The FGD outlet dust (on unit desk back left overview) was however reading ~14mg, which is within daily limits and was not in alarm.  The cause of the high inlet dust was presumed to be combustion led, but the inlet dust remained high despite trying numerous mill configurations.  

It became apparent that the outlet dust reading on the unit back panel was incorrect (still reading ~14mg), and the actual outlet dust (CDAS) reading was 3x higher than displayed on the overview.  The Centre desk was receiving the correct data and the daily average was exceeding the 18mg limit.  On the unit desk Air CEMS screen the Outlet dust was reading 14mg with a magenta box around the reading.  The CDAS outlet dust was reading 30mg+.

C3 Precip zone will not go in service (keeps tripping), and on interrogating the data it became apparent that the C1 & C2 passes were working extremely hard.  The conclusion was that the high 'B' side inlet dust was due to 'C' Precip pass not coping with the dust burden.

The MEL was reduced to 350MW to allow the 'C' Precip inlet damper to be shut.  
As the damper closed the 'B' side dust immediately reduced.  The MEL was later increased to 400MW once the daily dust position was recovered.  The MEL will remain at 400MW due to only 4 Precip passes being I/S.

C Pass has been box rapped several times after the unit came off load.  On the next RTS of Unit 2, C pass should be introduced incrementally and dust burden monitored closely.

Defects have been raised for C3 precip - keeps tripping (21525966), C2 Negative rapping U/S (21525967) & for Unit 2 outlet dust displaying wrong reading on the unit overview panel.  Strangely once the dust burden reduced, the Outlet dust started to read the correct values again and matched the CDAS reading!
HAZARD: Dust (Inc. complaints, technical breaches or affecting ecosystems)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Load reduced to 350MW
'C' Precip inlet damper closed
Load kept at 350MW until Daily dust position recovered.
MEL increased to 400MW and proven OK with only 4 passes I/S.
'C' Precip pass boxed rapped several times overnight once unit was off load.

Refer C3 tripping issues to Elec team.  
Attempt to re-introduce 'C' pass on next run while monitoring inlet / outlet dust
Investigate Unit desk overview panel dust reading displaying incorrect value and not alerting the Unit operator to the high outlet dust.

TITLE: Main Water Treatment Plant Stream 1 Cation & Anion.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On the committed work program for Friday (1st March), there was a request to isolate both the Anion & Cation on Stream 1.  Stream 1 has not been in service for many years and the request was to unbox the vessels and pump out the resin in preparation for decommissioning the stream.  Stream 1 has sat isolated for at least 10 years.  Overnight the keys were retrieved from the CPO's key safe and all the isolation points were checked, and the old E-on caution labels were replaced with Uniper labels.  As the vessels had been isolated for so long, and there is no external indication of level, it was an unknown as to the level within the vessels.  The Anion and Cation drains to the effluent sump were opened, and a flow was heard immediately.  Also the tell tale drains and vents to atmosphere were opened.  I would estimate that the vessels were at least half full prior to starting draining.  As the vessels were draining there was a pungent smell noted,  we remained in the WTP as the vessels drained and continued to apply further isolations to the acid & caustic dilution tanks in preparation for future de-commissioning.  The smell appeared to us to dissipate fairly quickly, so once the vessels were fully drained, the drain valves were locked shut to complete the isolation.  We returned to the Permit office to prepare the PFW.  When passing through the control room there was several comments made about a foul strong smell, and it was quickly realised it was emanating from our skin, overalls and clothing.  I returned to the WTP to assess the odour, and on re-entering the WTP the smell was extremely strong.  But again within a few minutes I became accustomed to the smell. 

Due to the pungency of the odour, I stated (in the further precautions on the PFW) that a selected person should attend the unboxing of the vessels and carry out an atmosphere check prior to starting work.

I understand that prior to the unboxing, discussions between the selected person and duty control person resulted in the PFW being withdrawn until the source of the smell could be identified, and to ascertain if it was in anyway harmful to health.  I was asked to input a Synergy tonight (2nd March).
HAZARD: Exposure to gases, fumes and vapours
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Email was sent to Selected persons asking for assistance prior to unboxing of vessels.
effluent sumps were pumped out and flushed to dilute the effluent.
Selected person took samples of effluent.

Selected person to carry out investigation into the source of the odour.

TITLE: Steam Turbine delay to run up due to a ET200 power supply fault.
CASE_DESCRIPTION: ST Would not run up to warming speed. There was a standing ET200 power supply fault which would not clear activated the previous evening. Various boiler Temp And pressure signals had been lost, most appeared to be 2oo3 channels, and unit ran oK  with the fault the previous evening. However ST was missing the S/HTG RHT AHD TURB >30K criteria to  release the ST. This was due to signal 10LBB50CP004 being the only channel used to calculate the superheating and was currently a bad signal. This was simulated to replicate CP002/003 at 22 bar to release the ST.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: It was later found that thermocouple 10LBB50CT006 had suffered heat damage and was the cause of the ET200 trip. Once this was disconnected the ET200 reset OK.

TITLE: PSO - U2 tripped at 430MW on turbine trip
CASE_DESCRIPTION: U2 tripped at 430MW on turbine trip. This is believed to have been caused by the HSUs changing over & one of the oil supply pumps failing to cut in, however this has not proven yet.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The trip happened to the previous shift, they safely ran down the turbine / unit & changed over to station supplies. They contacted the turbine & electrical team
Around 18.30 our shift took over at this point the turbine was on barring with station electrical supplies established.
Ovation trends were analysed we concluded that for an unknown reason the HSUs had a changeover initiated & on this changeover the A side supply pump no2 failed to start, this caused a Non Urgent turbine trip.
After consultation with the turbine & electrical teams we decided to reset the turbine, run a number of HSU change overs & if successful put the unit back on.
We were unable to reset the turbine due to a ‘Valve combination trip’ standing after further help from the C&I team this was cleared & the turbine was reset. HSU change overs where initiated numerous times without fail & it was then decided to put the unit back on.  
The unit was back energised from the 400kV substation & whilst the unit was being prepare for a start-up, the control engineer out a start on No2 CW pump, as the pump started the Unit Transformer protection was initiated & the 400kV supply tripped thus losing unit supplies, this incident will be logged as a separate synergy.
text_features: PSO - U2 tripped at 430MW on turbine trip. U2 tripped at 430MW on turbine trip. This is believed to have been caused by the HSUs changing over & one of the oil supply pumps failing to cut in, however this has not proven yet.

TITLE: PSO: U2 - Unit transformer differential protection operated
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Unit 2 - Unit transformer differential protection operated
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
On attempting to return unit 2 from a turbine trip, unit was back energised from the 400kV sub station, the was being prepared for a start-up.  All the unit auxiliary plant was in service & a CW pump was required.
Prior to the control engineer putting a start on No2 CW pump, the unit brd volts were 11.7kV, as the CW pump started the Unit Transformer protection was initiated & the 400kV supply tripped thus losing unit supplies.
On further investigation the Unit Transformer differential protection had initiated. The unit transformer was visually inspected & all looked o.k.
The Electrical team was contacted & it was decided to MEL the unit to zero, until the cause for trip could be established.

TITLE: PSO - U2 Seal Oil System pipework swinging during test
CASE_DESCRIPTION: When carrying out the turbine lub and seal oil cut-in tests it was reported that the pipework was swinging and noisy
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Violent noise and knocking reported shortly after starting to conduct the routine Saturday turbine oil pump tests on Unit 2. DC seal oil pump had but run for approx 15 seconds before being armed and starting the tests. Aux POP was in service and the unit operator was unable to arm the AC seal oil pump without it cutting back into service. Pipework around the main lub oil tank was knocking loudly and seal oil pipework was shaking violently throughout the system (see attached video) although the H2 seal oil diff and seal oil pressure appeared steady. Running either the aux POP or AC seal oil pumps either in isolation or together made any difference. Knocking appeared most severe at either spill valve 367A or DC Seal oil pump discharge NRV 357B. Able to take turbine off barring and take o/s lub oil pumps, so eliminated knocking as being due to main oil system. As soon as the DC seal oil pump was started the distress in the system stopped. The DC pump was left in for a few minutes before being stopped. Once out of service the system remained 'normal'. Suspect the the cause of the distress was possibly 'hammer' from air in the section of seal oil pipework associated with the DC discharge pipework before teeing into the seal oil cooler to seal pipework? Or possibly the DC pump NRV 357B passing back (although it can be confirmed that no seal oil pumps were reverse rotating when out of service.

TITLE: PSNH - Station Mulsifyre Detection Air System
CASE_DESCRIPTION: The mulsifyre detection air systems depressurised resulting in the operation of most of road 4 mulsifyre water systems and very nearly all of road 3 generator transformer associated fire systems, however operation of those systems was averted in this incident. The incident occurred following the release of and isolation of station general service air compressor no.2 which had been supplying the back-up alternative air supply to all three main station mulsifyre systems. The standby general service air system had not been started and this resulted in the GS air system and in turn the mulsifyre air detection system depressurising which caused the operation of road 4 mulsifye systems. The root cause of the incident being that the three individual mulsifyre detection air top up compressors are all unavailable through breakdown. The top-up compressors run excessively due to detection air system leakage. We have consequently been reliant on the alternative air provided by the GS air system to maintain pressure in the mulsifyre detection air systems, however this is not the primary purpose of the GS air system.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
GS air system re-instated and mulsifyre detection air systems re-pressurised. Road 3 mulsifyre deluge water isolating valves shut off. Mulsifyre pressure tank taken off line on refilled. Report to station fire PA to reset road 3 fire systems.
Recommendations to reinstate the the three separate mulsifyre top-up compressors and identify and repair the most significant air detection system leaks across the site to minimise wear and tear on the top-up compressors. Return the air detection systems to normal stand alone operation and become less reliant on the alternative back-up GS air supply.

TITLE: Passing valve fills acid measuring tank - Linked SL # 46684
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
At 00:47 High and High High level alarms were received on the Sulphuric acid measuring tank.
Pulling up the trend showed that the level had risen gradually from 26% starting at  approx 21:00. 
The air isolation valve for the Suplhuric acid dosing system had been isolated at around this time.
Sited was attended immediately to try to work out what had happened, the acid measuring tank filling valves were checked first.... both valves found to be closed.
When looking around the Acid Measuring tank it was noticed that the tank was very hot and on inspection it was found the the Acid ejector motive water valve fails open when the air is isolated... this should not be a problem as there are other valves that remain closed in the system.
It is suspected that one of the Acid Ejector suction valves 90GCN30AA010 or 90GCN30AA012 is passing allowing motive water to leak back to the Acid measuring tank when the air was isolated and the Motive water valve failed open.
Acid Measuring tank was left boxed.
During the night the tank level started dropping.
On investigation the flanged joint on the lower inspection point was found to be leaking and the stainless inlet pipe at the bottom of the tank was also found to be holed.
All acid that leaked was contained within the bund and associated chemical waste sump.
HAZARD: Hazardous substance, which is non-toxic, non-CMR substance (carcinogenic, mutagenic, reproduction toxic)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Reason for tank filling investigated.
Motive water hand isolator 90GCN30AA013 shut to completely isolate the tank.
Acid dosing skid barriered off.

TITLE: Loss of power to U6 BFB board causing trip of condensate extract pump and other systems fed off BFB board.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
While carrying out fault investigation under MO - 1180967658 an unexpected operation of the BFA to BFB interconnector caused loss of power to the BFB board.

Breaker 61BFT20GT200 (BFB feeder) was placed in test position for the purposes of fault investigation.

Upon reaching step 5 of the MO "Operate breaker locally and observe operation." a peer check was carried out to ensure that the correct operation was being undertaken.

Once the ON(Test) button was depressed, breaker 61BFT20GT200 (BFB feeder) closed, this was the intended outcome. However with this, 61BFA15GS021 BFA to BFB interconnector opened, this caused loss of power on the BFB board. This caused condensate extract pump 2 to trip, fortunately pump 1 was available and swapped over without issue. Other systems impacted were as follows, MBH55 GT exhaust cooling fan, CMAS fan 2, vacuum breaker etc. The event list is attached.

In normal operation if the the BFA feeder was closed and the BFB feeder was to close the interconnector should open. However the collective understanding was that in the test position this logic would be void. 

Upon investigation of the logic it was found that this is not the case.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Immediate action - Shift team leader sent out email to all shift team leaders outlining what happened.

Recommended actions -  The logic be updated to take into account test position.

TITLE: NMR - Slip and Trip While Descending from the Large Borer Bed
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Individual slipped whilst stepping down from the big borer bed onto the shop floor using the step at the chuck end of the machine.
HAZARD: Slip / Trip / Fall (at the same floor level and on stairs)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The First Aider conducted a thorough check with the individual, confirming that the only injury sustained was a minor muscle strain resulting from the prevention of a fall. No additional symptoms were reported, and no further first aid was required.

Upon investigation, it was identified that the current step's tread is too narrow to ensure secure footing and exhibits a slippery surface, presenting a significant safety risk.

To mitigate this hazard, immediate action was taken to commission the fabrication of a replacement step, specifically designed to provide enhanced grip and safer foot placement. Furthermore, a comprehensive deep clean of the area was organised to remove any residual oil around the machine, further minimising the risk of slipping. These proactive measures aim to significantly improve the safety of the workspace and prevent similar incidents in the future.

TITLE: Unit 6 HP Bypass Water Injection Control Valve logic modification fault.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Unit 6 HP Bypass Water Injection Control Valve logic was requested to be changed to match Unit 7's, that has been on trial. 
The logic is designed in such a way there is a test facility (a switch to turn the modified logic on/off). This was in place so that the logic could be switched on when DCS engineers where on site, during a run up, to monitor it and tune it if required. 
With the test bit off, the new logic would not be active and the control would not be changed. 
The logic was copied, but an error was made and the test facility was accidently left on. During Unit 6's run up after its outage, the spray valve wasn't operating. This is when the 'test' logic was still realised to be on. The test facility was turned off and that allowed the spray to function, stopping the unit from tripping on high temperatures.

TITLE: GT Trip from PRS ESV’s closing
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
At 09.49:33.913 GT Tripped due to humming event caused by low gas pressure from the PRS.  Low gas pressure recorded at the PRS due to ESD system operation closing the inlet ESD valve XV4002 and pressure reduction skid valve XV4480.
Scada system alarms showed ESD system operated due to PRS common hand switch operated, (PRS\ESD\UA4002) and ESD trip from CDC control room (PRS\ESD\HS4002C) receipt of this alarm would indicate that the operator himself had activated the PRS trip by pushing the emergency trip button in the plant MCR This cannot of been the cause of the PRS trip due to the operator not pressing the push button in the MCR, this was witnessed by gas operations as they were present in the control room when the ESD system tripped. whilst the gas pressure supply to CDC did fall the cause of the unit trip was from combustion instability (humming). it is recognised  that the low gas pressure would have tripped the GT by activation of the low gas pressure trip signals however on this occasion 'Humming' occurred operating the MAX 3 protection trip before the low gas pressure trip signals were received. The load at the time of the trip was 414MWgen (full load in 'OTC operation).
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: STL contacted to establish his condition and personal safety.  Generating systems made operationally safe (Boiler, Steam Turbine, Feed & condensate systems), Both GT & ST shafts brought to cooling turning speed. Engineering informed of incident.

TITLE: MUW DCS RIO Panel Wiring Discrepancies
CASE_DESCRIPTION: When reviewing loop diagram 755-TEL-XX-XX-DR-E-0215 for PAB80AA151 in comparison to the physical wiring inside the MUW DCS RIO panel, it became clear that there are multiple occurrences of disparity between the drawing and the actual wiring configuration within the panel. For example, the drawing states on terminal block X33 wiring should be X33-13 - Brown, X33-14 - Black, X33-15 - Blue, X33-16 - Green, but in reality it is X33-13 - Blue, X33-14 - Green, X33-15 - Brown, X33-16 - Black, and the wiring into AO card 1:5:0 should be wire 316 into terminal 3, 317 into terminal 6, but the reality is 317 into terminal 3 and 316 into terminal 6. These are just a couple of examples but several other discrepancies have been found (including in other drawings) suggesting the drawings cannot be relied upon to reflect the actual wiring configuration of the equipment.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: No immediate action taken. Recommend a full review of the entire wiring installation in comparison with the supplied drawings may be required as a limited review has already uncovered a significant number of errors.

TITLE: BP Engineer unfamiliar with site and Uniper work practices allowed on site without host being contacted.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A repair request was raised with BP for EV charger number 2.  Syed Ishrat was given a name by BP for the person coming out to investigate.  The BP engineer was booked on site through VMS with Syed's contacts details as the host.

On arrival, he was booked in by security and directed to the power station.  Syed wasn't contacted by the gatehouse, so wasn't aware the engineer had arrived.

The engineer then went to the charger, reset it with the external reset button and was then spotted by myself as I went to my car.   No intrusive work other than pressing the reset button was carried out so the risk was minimal, but as a new person to site, the BP engineer would've been unaware of our safety and working practices.

I have found recently that I am rarely contacted by security when a visitor comes to site and the first that I hear of their arrival is when they arrive in reception and reception call me.  9 times out of 10 this isn't an issue, but if someone doesn't know to go straight to reception or is unfamiliar with site, they might end up somewhere they're not supposed to with no one site knowing that person is on site.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: No injury occurred, but potential for injury if unsupervised work was carried out.

TITLE: U1 Burner front mulsifyre system return to service
CASE_DESCRIPTION: On the morning of the 6th July the outage commissioner was reinstating the U1 burner front mulsifyre protection system.  As the air was being charged up at the burner front, it caused a drop of pressure on the mulsifyre air system.  Connected into to the U1 burner front mulsifyre system are several road 5 mulsifyre systems including the OPC transformers, and the fuel oil heater house.  The drop in air pressure initiated the OPC and fuel oil heater mulsifyre deluge system.   This in itself is not a particular issue as these fire systems can operate at any time without warning as per the design; however a secondary issue was caused by the water issuing from the fuel oil heater house carrying an unknown amount of oil from the fuel oil heater bunds.  I understand that the oil entered the site drains and was contained at the oil separator and straw bale filters.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Shift Operations and Altrad attended road 5 directly in front of the fuel oil heater house.  A significant amount of water was issuing onto road 5 from the heater house, and an unknown amount of oil could be seen on top of the water.   The water was isolated to stop the water & local drains were bunded, any residual oil remaining outside of the heater house was cleaned using oil absorbent.   The plant was inspected to prove there was no plant oil leaks.  Any fugitive oil must have already been in the oil heater bunds / house.

Work may have to be delayed until a suitable period where the adjacent plant can be isolated and safety from the system can be assured.

TITLE: U1 A SSFP Oil Filter vent valve found slightly open.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
U1 A SSFP was being prepared for RTS ready for a test run, followed by pressure testing of HP heaters.

The SSFP was de-isolated & pre start checked by the commissioning operator.  The oil pump was put into service and the oil system checked for correct pressures, and checked over for leaks.  No leaks were observed following the oil pump going into service.  The Operator then walked the HP feed system to ensure a route was available for the SSFP's and de-isolated the remaining plant.  The Operator called the Authorised Person over the radio to make the HV breaker available for service.  As the AP was heading to the switchroom the Operator returned to the pump ready for the start; a period of approx 30 mins had passed.   On returning to the pump he observed a large pool of oil under the A SSFP oil filters.  On closer inspection the vent on the filter was found to be slightly open with a stream of oil running from it.  The filter vent was closed immediately to stop the flow.   The AP was called on the radio to divert straight to the pump.  Dresser Dry was deployed to dam the oil and to prevent entry to any turbine hall drains.   There is a 3" hole in the turbine hall floor adjacent to the A SSFP, and some of the oil had flowed down the hole which leads directly to the sub- basement.  Dresser dry was deployed in the sub-basement around the oil & the spill contained.

The oil mop in the reject tunnel was immediately put into service as a precautionary measure.  There was a very slight film of oil on the water before the weir, but nothing observed after the weir, or at either the station drains sump or Ash Fines Pit.

The filter vent is not operated as part of the RTS procedure,  and is only used to prove the filter off pressure during a filter change.  I suspect that at some point during U1 outage the vent cock handle has been knocked slightly, causing the vent to pass when the oil pump went into service which was missed on the initial inspection.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The oil mop in the reject tunnel was put into service. 
Dresser dry was applied to all areas of the spill.
Altrad boiler ops were called to assist in the clean up operation.  All dresser dry was cleaned up and bagged, both adjacent to the feed pump and in the sub basement.
A defect card was raised to top up A SSFP oil tank.

Services team will be informed on Monday (10/07) to highlight the dresser dry used from spill kits

Consider filling in the Hole in the turbine hall floor  (expanding foam would suffice).

TITLE: PSNH - Common ammonia plant toxic gas trip
CASE_DESCRIPTION: The Ammonia Plant South West Perimeter LOS (Line-of-Sight) toxic gas detected alarm was received and release of the deluge system operated. This was coincidental  with collection of the waste ammonia solution IBCs for environmental disposal. One possible cause being diesel engine emissions from the Services JCB all-terrain FLT.  The driver was in close proximity to the LOS beam at the west end of the offloading bay when the LOS gas detection was triggered. Another possible cause could have been ammonia vapour emanating from the IBCs themselves, however these have not caused a problem in the last 3-4 weeks that they have been stored in the offloading bay. On this occasion there was no generation taking place, hence no operational loss. However there is the potential for operational units to suffer immediate non-abatement due to loss of NH3 injection so a repeat scenario should be avoided.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Communicate event to (Services, Boiler Team, Doosan, C&I Team, Env and Chem Team)
•When carrying out FLT operations in close proximity to the ammonia plant LOS beams, avoid the use of the ‘older’ JCB all-terrain FLT and substitute for either a newer diesel or propane powered FLT.
•When planning the delivery or collection of any IBCs to consider scheduling when the Units are not running if feasible.

TITLE: Water surge into Oil interceptor pits after heavy storm.

The breaker remains in the cubicle.

TITLE: Striking Pipe Support with arm when Changing Duplex Filter
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During operational walkarounds, it was noticed that the Boiler Feed Pump drive end lubrication line was shaking and the pressure gauge at the bearing showed spikes in pressure associated with the shaking. 
The operator investigated the fault by checking the oil heater was in service and then contacted the control room and asked for the lube oil pumps to be changed over. 
This made no difference so the operator decided to change over the duplex lube oil filter. 
The handle was found to be stiff and while changing over the filters the operator's forearm caught the underside of a pipe support bracket with their arm. 

The changeover of the lube oil filters did resolve the lube oil problem.
HAZARD: Human Impact with a fixed object
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Area checked and discussion had with operator on method.
Arm checked and operator continued working.

TITLE:
Point of isolation interfered without consultation with SAP.
RB 26/07 - Case extended to 21/08 due to tech detail required for completion.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A Defib box was to be installed on the outside of the station switch house, requiring it to be connected into a distribution board in the station switch house cable way that had a spare fuse carrier available. 
That morning the SAP asked the Electrical Supervisor to show him said distribution board so he could clearly identify the point of isolation he was going to use.  The fuse carrier to be used was identified (the fuse holder+fuse was missing so the SAP didnt have to remove it). The plan was to connect into the outgoing side of the fuse carrier so the SAP physically covered the live side of the fuse carrier with a caution card and protected the area with caution tape. 
When the document was cancelled the CP informed the SAP that what was thought to be the outgoing side was in actual fact the live side which he discovered when he tested for dead. At this point instead of returning to the SAP the CP removed the isolation and connected into the true outgoing side of the fuse carrier and completed the job.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Permit for Work cancelled.

The SFT was cancelled and a new one issued which allowed the Gen TX Marshalling Kiosk AC supply isolators to be deisolated, it was then noted that we had power to the OLTC. It was then determined that the OLTC is fed from F04 415V MCB within the marshalling kiosk.

TITLE: Loose scaffolding components found on U61 chimney top platform and on the  HRSG roof.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On the morning of 15th March, Kaefer scaffolding inspectors  conducted a scaffold inspection on the scaffold at the top of Unit 61’s stack. This is a standard requirement following adverse weather conditions.
On arrival at the top gantry the inspector has observed that a one ton ‘Maxi’ style bag that had been secured into position holding the fittings and smaller materials had ripped, spilling the contents onto the grating.

The inspector secured these loose fittings in another bag on this level which is intact and has been temporarily secured to the scaffold / grating.  Arrangements for further securing has been implemented until such a time as ALL materials can be lifted down by the crane.
After these materials were initially made secure, all gantry's on every level were subjected to a thorough inspection.
During the course of this wider inspection, it was observed that several fittings had fallen onto the HRSG roof. Permission was sought, and granted ,to remove these loose items from the roof.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Items removed from gantry and HRSG roof. All other items secured until safe removal can be arranged. Investigation report to follow from Kaefer.

TITLE: Access Control System failing
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Roll-Call

Currently our electronic Muster is not working, as process dictates when this goes down we start a manual roll-call and so this is what we have been doing now since Thursday night, however with tomorrow being the first working day for a lot of new contractors coming to site and for visitors and deliveries it could be a very busy day, especially in the morning.

TITLE: U4 'Y' 3.3KV Switchboard
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A PFW safety document for U4 ‘Y’ 3.3KV SW/BRD maintenance was issued on Monday 16th May (AM) to one of the electrical CP’s.

The CP (Competent Person) proceeded to work on the 3.3KV ‘Y’ board during the coarse of the day, carrying out VCB maintenance, CCT spout maintenance and function checks as per his maintenance orders and maintenance procedures and PFW.  At the end of the working day the CP surrendered the PFW and explained to the duty SAP (Senior Authorised Person) the state of the works and progress made.  During the discussion the CP stated that the VCB’s had been returned to the Earth position.  
To allow the VCB’s to return to the CCT earth position, requires the 110v solenoid fuses to be available; but the duty SAP noted the fuses were quoted as a POI on the safety document.

In discussion with the SAP who prepared the safety document - During the preparation stage, he had read & understood that the electrical method, stated 110v supplies were needed to function check the VCB closing springs, & that the VCB’s should be returned to the as found position following cct spout maintenance.  

Because of this, the preparing SAP had made supplies available to the 110V solenoids for function checking, and to allow the VCB’s to be put back to the CCT earth position.  The Safety document was already pre-prepared on Nisoft quoting the Solenoid fuses as POI’s, and the Preparing SAP omitted to remove the isolation point from the POI’s list in Nisoft prior to printing.  

The safety document was cancelled and the POI on Nisoft quoting the Solenoid 110v fuses was removed.   The new Safety document was re-issued on the 17th May to continue the work.

The isolation point originally quoted – 
•	‘Y’ Unit SW/BRD 110v CONTROL FUSES & SOLENOID FUSES             WITHDRAWN & CAUTIONED

The isolation point was changed to  
•	‘Y’ Unit SW/BRD 110v CONTROL FUSES                                              
WITHDRAWN & CAUTIONED

The safety document had been pre-prepared so that an isolation list could be produced for the isolating AP.  This was a couple of weeks prior to the document being printed as the contractors were delayed in attending site.

The Solenoid isolation had been removed from the key safe, made available & crossed off of the AP sheet by the preparing SAP, but not removed from the PFW.

Please note that this Observation Synergy is being raised as a prompt to have a discussion regarding the importance of SAP's to ensure the  administrative preparation of the safety documents is given the SAP's full attention, and is prioritised, to ensure the SAP isn't distracted by non SFS procedures.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Immediate action is to discuss with the preparing SAP the importance of proof reading isolations on pre-prepared safety documents (especially ones with multiple continuation sheets as any ‘Free text’ isolation points always appear at the end of the list), and to ensure that the safety documents are updated in-line with the AP sheet.

TITLE: SC10/20 Generator Hydrogen Leak alarms.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
There have been multiple cases of low level hydrogen leaks detected on both SC10 and SC20 synchronous condensers during offline periods.

July 7th 2022

The synchronous condenser was shutdown due to the need for a Mod 2 400KV grid isolation for maintenance activities.

Whilst the SC20 Generator was at standstill a hydrogen leak alarm was received on the gas detector panel CYE01 in the Killingholme control room. Investigations at that time could not detect a genuine leak although the reading appeared to last for approximately 30 seconds and peaked at 20% LEL. This alarm was detected at both ends of the Generator on both HD005 and HD006. 

Later as the Hydrogen Purity Concentration procedure was being carried out these alarms were received again. This time a noticeable leak could be heard within the turbine hall also. These readings peaked at 40% LEL and the detection lasted for several minutes. 

To clarify the first alarm was received with the shaft at standstill and no work being carried out and the second alarm was received when the shaft was still at standstill but hydrogen filling was taking place.

A further leak alarm was detected when  SC20 was put on barring up to 200RPM using the oil system

Aug 21st 2022

Again a 400KV outage was required for maintenance activities on MOD1.

Again, Killingholme OPS took the opportunity to attempt to sweeten the generator hydrogen purity. There were similar leaks of hydrogen detected as there was on SC20 above but in slightly different.

* Whilst at standstill during the H2 sweetening process

* Whilst at standstill following completion of the sweetening process.

* Whilst on barring on the return to operation

19/12/2022

Leak alarms were once again raised when SC20 was stopped to carry out repairs on GT21 GCB.  Leaks stopped once the unit was put back on barring.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Generator returned to barring and Purity procedure stopped.

TITLE: 81BFT20 415V circuit breaker not opening on command
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Overnight, the duty operations shift were requested to change over the duty 415V unit auxilliary transformer in preparation for the engineering department to change some protection settings the following day. 81BFT10 11kv breaker was closed prior so that the transformer could soak. The BFA-BFB breaker was opened and the BFT10 415V breaker closed to supply the BFA board from the BFT10 transformer. This worked correctly. The BFB to BMA board breaker was opened starting the standby diesel generator which took the load on the BMA board. A back synch to BFA board was selected which functioned correctly. The BFA board / BFT10 transformer was then supplying the power to the BMA board. This was correct. An attempt was made to open the 81BFT20 415V incomer CB to BFB board. An open feedback failure alarm was received and the current on the breaker did not drop. BFT20 transformer remains supplying the BFB board awaiting engineering assistance.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Remains in a safe condition, in service. If a fault were to occur, the 11kV VCB protection would open to clear the fault.

TITLE: Grinding activity causing small burn to abdomen
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Location: HRSG 27M Level - LP Drum External - Northside Shell 
-	Altrad Grinder undertaking grinding activity (excavating 4mm to remove defect) on LP Drum external shell. Full PPE worn inc. full face mask and area set-up for Hot-Works. 
-	Whilst undertaking works, train of grinding sparks was directed to his body/abdomen.

-	Grinder patted out the burn/hole on his overall realised the burn seeped through his T-shirt and burnt his skin (first layer).
-	Grinder immediately vacated the area and contacted Site Manager.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
- Work Stopped 
- First Aid treatment issued 
- Grinder undertook a cold shower - 10-15mins - ensuring burnt area was cooled. 
- Advise to go hospital if the burn blisters - Grinder refused and confirmed he was okay
- All Hot-Works stopped on plant 
- All Hot-Works personnel checked overalls - as a minimum they required Flame Retardant overalls 
- Brief undertaken to Altrad personnel - TBT re Grinder techniques / Overalls PPE. 
- Escalation report issued to Altrad Fleet - for awareness 
- Altrad site team told to ensure investigation is carried out and controls put in place

TITLE: SC20 Seal Oil Pump Faulted - Alarms missed
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
At 15:19 on Monday 24th April SC20 experienced a fault on the Seal Oil system.

1.	Seal Oil pump 1 “Running” signal lost.
2.	No change in Seal Oil pump 1 discharge pressure, and no activation of the pump “Stopped” signal.  Seal Oil Pump 1 remains in service
3.	Seal Oil pump 2 is started by the DCO controller
4.	Seal Oil Pump DCO is faulted and forced into Manual
5.	2 pumps are now in operation until manual intervention to reset system

This is Synergi is to log that the Killingholme Operator was not in the control room when the alarms activated. Subsequently the CDC Control Room acknowledged the alarms but took no action.

TITLE: U6 PLST Feed Pump Trip On Forced Changeover
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Coming on to shift in the morning it was noted that U6 BFP No.2 had developed a discharge v/v gland leak, the unit was due to 2shift overnight and it was decided the safest way to carry out a forced changeover was offload overnight. Around 15:00 we had a phone call from UGC (energy trading) to advise that the unit would be running through overnight. With this new change in commercial running and the fact that the leak was deemed to be deteriorating, the decision was made to try a forced changeover of the feed pumps while the unit was onload but in a steady state. at around 16:10 the changeover was initiated placing BFP No. 2 in service, at which point both feed pumps tripped and the unit PLST'd .

TITLE:
Unit 7 Cold Reheat Assisted NRV re-assembled incorrectly.
29/09 LT - Extended for Emerson RCA 31/10/2023
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During the first Steam Turbine run up the cold re-heat NRV failed to open, on investigation it was found that the actuator and valve keyway had been assembled 90 degrees out.
The actuator, instead of releasing the valve plate to open on flow was trying to lift the valve plate open, this was held back by the steam pressure difference.
Under normal operation the actuator would remove the closing action and allow the plate to lift open when the pressure difference across the valve was sufficient.
In this state, had the actuator been powerful enough to force the NRV open, with positive DP down stream the flow would have reversed back to the HP turbine Exhaust.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Unit 7 was shut down and issue investigate, actuator has been correctly aligned and re-tested

TITLE: Instrumentation issues on cooling water discharge
CASE_DESCRIPTION: A review of the environmental data identified two occasions where the environment monitors had issues resulting in the recording of emissions values which breached permit requirements. On 13/9, a high temperature was recorded while purging for  period of 3 minutes. On 19/6, a low pH value was recorded for a period of 1-2 minutes, before recovering while the purge valve was still closing. In both cases, other monitors in the system showed no changes and the readings were determined to be the result of instrument error.  As compliance monitors are involved, these incidents have been notified to the Environment Agency.  No pollution is believed to occurred, however neither incident was reported to the production team leader or APM and systems to prevent purging do not seem to have reacted sufficiently quickly.
HAZARD: Legal, monitoring and reporting (Non-compliance of obligations)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The temperature probe in the environment kiosk has now been changed to a more reliable system, with further changes planned to mitigate the effects of ambient conditions. Performance will be monitored against other instruments during periods of warmer temperatures. 
The environment kiosk pH meter is currently be redesigned to mitigate any  potential impacts from suspended solids – this will return to being the duty compliance monitor once this work is complete.

TITLE: Unit 4 Goods Lift
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Concerns around lift functionality and safety.

Incident:
I used the lift on Saturday 15th July approx 09:45.  I pressed floor 3. The inner doors seemed to jolt before it started moving.  I opened the inner door (believing that the lift had stopped and I was at the desired floor - landing arrival alarm has been disabled!) to find the lift had not fully travelled to the correct floor.  It opened with very little resistance and opened enough to stop the lift dead and put it into fault mode. I closed the door again, pressed floor 3 and the lift seemed to try to carry on with its journey to floor 3.  It is not clear to me what happened next but lift then returned to ground floor with a slight jolt.  I assumed this was a braked fall but it was a hard stop when it got to the bottom.  I rang the alarm in the lift as it wasn’t clear whether the doors would now open at the ground floor.  They did open.  Ops isolated the lift power supply and I barriered off the entrance.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Power supply isolated and locked off. Entrance barriered off. Lift contractor to remedy faults and programs.

TITLE: U1 Return to service from Outage - Spray pump hand isolating valves found in incorrect position.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During the morning of the return of U1 from main outage, it was noted that superheat spray flow was not sufficient as load increased.  The duty AUO was despatched to investigate the issue, helped by the commissioning lead operator.  They found the spray pump hand isolating valves in the closed position.  The valves could not have been 100% closed as there was sufficient flow to achieve ~5kg/sec of flow at the sprays.

These valves are very large hand isolating valves that are not routinely operated (2 man job to open / close) and are not part of any outage isolations as they are left available for maintenance during the outage.  

The work lists from the PFW's show that the valves were worked on during the outage, and we suspect they were operated by the maintenance team to prove operation following maintenance, and hence left in the closed position.

The valves should have been picked up as closed during the initial commissioning phase, and then again on the pre start checks prior to RTS of the pump.

This is the first Main outage RTS since the change to the outage procedure of filling the DA with FFA and forward filling of the feed system with the SSFP's.  With the introduction of the new boiler filling dosing skid, it means we no longer carry out the above step.  Instead we hold the feed water at the HP heater outlets and then fill the boiler using the filling pump with pre dosed water.  Then during the boiler Hydraulic, we back fill the steam circuits through the spray bypass line.  This meant that during our commissioning phase the Spray pump system got missed and highlighted a gap in the new procedure.

The pre start checks were carried out by the duty AUO.  On interviewing the AUO he stated that he had carried out a pre-start check, but only checked the electric valves as per usual for a normal return from a 2-shift.  This was a relatively inexperienced AUO who had never seen the hand isolators operated before.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Valves returned to normal working position to provide sufficient spray flows.
The new outage filling procedure has been updated to include back filling & priming of the spray system to re-capture the entire spray system.
Inexperienced AUO has been briefed on the extra checks required when returning a unit from outage compared to a normal 2 shift.
Outage return to service checklist will be updated to include visual checks on any hand isolators that have been worked on during the outage period.  This will be based on the returned WAL's (Work Attachment Lists), and valve lists provided by the teams.
Maintenance teams to record (on the WAL's) the position hand isolators are left in following overhaul.

TITLE: GT Blow-off valve failed to operate
CASE_DESCRIPTION: During plant start-up, Gas Turbine compressor blow off valve 10MBA41AA051 failed to close on command causing GT controller to protection shut down the Gas Turbine. On investigation, solenoid coil pack had come adrift. The securing nut was found to be missing. The nut is component specific (non generic). A temporary repair was affected to secure the coil pack and the Gas Turbine returned to service.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Temporary repair affected to secure the coil pack until a permanent repair can be planned and executed. The required repair is quite simple although there is a high risk of trip, hence it would be most appropriate to carry out the repair when the Gas Turbine is not in service.

TITLE: Red Liquid In Local Drain Outside Altrad Babcock's Outage Workshop
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
When walking out from the Altrad Babcock outage workshop, one of the Altrad Babcock team member's noticed a bright red liquid in the drain. This was immediately reported to Uniper ERSHE, Uniper Environmental team and the Uniper Services Team. 
A sample of the liquid was taken and provided to the Environmental Team. 
Another drain cover local to the area was removed, confirming no further contamination of drainage.
The liquid was removed from the drain with a gulper - at this point it was clear that this was a local drain only. Approximately 5L of the liquid was removed from the drain.
It was unclear how long the liquid had been in there or how it got in the drain.

TITLE: SSOW - U4 AFCU Steam 2 Shut Off Valve - Notification & WOC with incorrect SAP FL
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Defect (21456557) and associated WOC (1180945297) have a SAP  FL of instrument air valve QEB10AA153. The intended SAP FL was actually a related ammonia valve HSJ10AA010. Although intended plant was worked upon, it appears that this FL discrepancy was not identified during initial defect entry, work order preparation & issue, permit issue and setting to work. This is suspected to be due to a poor/misleading SAP short description for valve QEB10AA153 which could easily be mistaken for HSJ10AA010.
QEB10AA153 Short Description: U4 A AFCU STRM 2 SHUTOFF ISOL VLV
QEB10AA153 Long Description: U4 A SIDE SCR AMMONIA FLOW CONTROL UNIT STREAM 2 SHUTOFF VALVE INSTRUMENT AIR SUPPLY ISOLATION VALVE

HSJ10AA010 Short Description: U4 A AFCU STRM 2 PNEU SOV 
HSJ10AA010 Long Description: A SIDE SCR AMMONIA FLOW CONTROL UNIT STREAM 2 PNEUMATIC SHUTOFF VALVE

The associated permit (already cancelled) 2022/2309/SP used a correct functional location description for the work intended although did not reference KKS HSJ10AA010 :
"U4 SCR A Ammonia Flow Control Skid Stream 2 shut off valve"
HAZARD: Exposure to gases, fumes and vapours
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Collate SSOW documentation
Check plant labelling
Check plant alarm descriptions
Check Nisoft/Eclipse FL descriptions for these valves
Check SAP FL Description for similar valves inc. other units
Propose improve SAP FL short descriptions for these valves
Check in SAP for other previous similar occurrences

TITLE: PSNH - U1 C16 Oil Burner hose leak
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
@ Approx 07:30 Sunday morning 04/12/22, a fuel oil leak was discovered on Unit 1 Burner Front.  The source of the leak was C16 oil burner inlet hose which had developed a leak.  The leak appears to be at the rear of the hose where it was touching the steel work.   The spray from the Leak was localised to C16 / C17 burner, but the excess has tracked down the pipework and steel work to the boiler basement.

It is unclear at what time the leak developed, but was not identified by the end of Saturday Day shift when the burner front was checked at approx 15:00hrs. 
The fuel oil had ran down the lower levels of the burner front, into the snake pit and Into the boiler basement adjacent 'C' pa fan.   As soon as the leak was discovered, the drain between 'C' PA fan and the ash hopper was plugged, and dresser dry applied to the immediate area.  Dresser dry was then applied to the higher levels where ever the oil had pooled.  Air heater wash sump, ash fines pits and ash crusher pits have showed no signs of oil as of 09:30 04/12/22.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Dresser dry applied to all pooled areas, and drain blocked off.
Services contacted to arrange clean-up crew to attend site.
Unit firing delayed until clean up completed and assessment can be made of lagging requirements.
Prior to firing unit, fire-fighting equipment to be set up and regular fire watch to be organised.

TITLE: Make-Up Water Redundant Pipe Removal
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
This Synergi has been raised on behalf of EDF by Asset Support & Outage Excellence UK 

Decommissioning of the CDC MUW supply pipework to include removal of the pipework, 10-PAR-20-CF001 flow meter and 10-PAR-20-AA151 Actuated Control valve.

Prior to the Safety document being written the SAP and the Uniper Project Engineer visited the point of work to discuss the exact works. The SAP had opened the drain valve on the redundant  MUW pipework and air could be heard rushing in there was no water from the drain proving the isolation of 10-PAS-72-AA002 of which separated the new MUW system form the old MUW system thus proving the integrity of the valve. A further discussion between the SAP and Uniper Project Engineer took place reference the status of the MUW pump booster station reference the HV cable disconnection and that he MUW booster pumps could not run as there was no power present.

A Safety document was issued by the Uniper SAP for the decommissioning works to proceed and at approximately 12:30 p.m., the Uniper Project Engineer received a phone call from Trant Works Manager responsible for the works to ask if an isolation had been applied at the EDF end of the MUW supply pipe to CDC.

An email was received at  12:37 from EDF Site Separation Lead Mechanical Engineer Decommissioning as follows:

I have just been to see the Trant guys doing the make up decommissioning work on CDC, I did a spot check on the safety document, and subsequently asked Nathan Pearson to stop works.
 
The only mechanical isolation in place is on valve 10-PAS-72-AA002, this valve separates the old system from the new system.
It appears no valves have been isolated upstream from the booster station end.
 
If EDF were to start one of it’s make up pumps, this could potentially feed water all the way to the CDC site, either causing harm when flanges are split, or flooding the CDC
 
Nathan is going to speak to Steve Nelson and the Ops team, could you please raise a Uniper synergy case for this.
 
The booster station may be electrically disconnected, but there is nothing to stop valves from being opened
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Work stopped immediately and SAP informed by Trant Engineering. Safety document  cancelled and locks and chains applied to the MUW booster pumps discharge manual isolation valves 10PAR11AA003 and 10PAR12AA003. New safety document issued and work completed.

TITLE:

RB - EXTENDED 30/05/2022 Centre led investigation.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:

The condition monitoring team at UTG were contacted by the STL and requested to analyse the plant data at the time of the incident, and to advice likely immediate causes and next steps. It was shortly reported back from UTG that early indications of the event were attributable to a likely loss of mass from the GT LPT stages.
UTG were mobilised to site to undertake a boroscope inspection which concluded liberation of blade and vane material across LPT stages 2-4.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Unit put onto forced cooling followed by planned shut down and isolation in readiness for boroscope inspection activities
