TITLE: No AGI alarms to the DCS during UPS failure/ESD trip
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
There were no DCS alarms from the AGI to the CCR to draw the operator's attention to the evolving issue at the AGI. This resulted in 2 hours of confusion/investigation and ultimately led to the unit being shutdown when it otherwise may have been able to stay on had the problem been highlighted. 

Operations are blind to any issue at the AGI due to the lack of CCTV and CCR alarms. The ESD had tripped shut while the unit was on and the UPS power back up was not adequate during the power cut but at no point was there anything to alert someone at Enfield. This is a process and safety issue.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Issue at the AGI was rectified and the ESD was re-opened.  The pipeline pressure was restored and all valves/alarms/trips returned to normal condition. Unit was shutdown and stabilised and due back on this morning.

TITLE: PSNH - Gypsum slurry overflowing from U1/U2 FGD absorber sump, sump pumps and agitator tripped
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Around 9am, it was reported by Ops to the FGD team that the U1/U2 absorber sump had filled to 100% level, was overflowing and the agitator and sump pumps had both tripped and could not be started. On investigation into what was causing the sump to continually overflow, it appeared to be a drain valve that was open on 'B' Gypsum extraction pump, even though this was the standby pump ('A' was in-service although was actually tripped by accident when trying to locally operate valves to ensure their position). The loss of the absorber sump (sump pumps and sump agitator unavailable) means there was no start permissive on U1 or U2 FGD therefore this immediately became a P1 notification.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Work was immediately progressed to pump out and unbog the sump agitator. The sump was returned to service by c. 4pm.
Recommendations for further actions:
A) Regardless of reason, whenever the sump is filled to 100%, the agitator and sump pumps trip and cannot be restarted until the sump level becomes within 'operable range' i.e. there needs to be manual intervention by using a temporary pump to pump out contents of the sump. This is a detriment and a plant mod should be considered that would allow the pumps and agitator to remain operable, even if the sump becomes 100% full and/or overflows. (FGD team)
B) The cause of the sump getting overwhelmed and hence overflowing needs to be investigated by the Operations team. First investigations into the probable cause of continual overflowing on the morning of 29/06 suggest the 'B' Gypsum extraction pump (was the standby pump) drain valve was open and slurry was flowing at high rate from this drain. When this valve was closed by the operator, the sump ceased to overflow.

TITLE: Main turbine hall waste oil tank
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The turbine waste oil tank high level alarm initiated at approx 1500hrs. The AUO was dispatched to check the level in the tank and he confirmed that the level was high but no chance of overflowing.
Considered transferring oil over the waste oil purification tank, however this tank was already full. 
Contacted Altrad to inform and check whether they were aware that the tank was full and needed emptying. Person responsible had left site but message was left for the following morning.
The wider shift team conducted further checks of the waste oil recovery tank systems to confirm that there was nothing draining such as oil cooler / coalescers etc. Nothing concerning was found across the four units.
At approx. 1930hrs it was observed that the turbine waste oil tank was overflowing.
Immediate action was taken to contain the oil within the local area and prevent ingress into the drains.
Altrad Boiler Ops were contacted to provide support with cleaning and responded quickly with a gulper. The oil spill and spill-dri was cleared.
The source of the problem was identified as a steam / water leak on  Unit 4 spray water booster pump which was causing the turbine waste oil tank to fill with water. This was balancing into the MBFP waste oil recovery tank, which in turn was being pumped into the turbine waste oil tank.
The unit 4 turbine waste oil tank was in a barriered area (associated with the leak causing the problem) and was consequently not checked as part of the operational check associated with the high level.
The turbine waste oil tank was covered with a tarpaulin to prevent further water ingress.
The site services team were contacted to arrange further support to assist the night shift with the follow up cleaning and lowering of the waste oil tank level below the high level alarm and monitoring / gulping of the main reject tunnel station water drainage of any carry over oil which was completed.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
U4 turbine waste oil tank covered with tarpaulin
Oil spill cleaned up and waste oil tank level lowered below high level alarm
Consider covering over the associated unit turbine waste oil tanks with some kind of liftable cover to prevent recurrence. The waste oil system is a supervised system for recovering oil when draining coolers and coalescers etc not for continually pumping leakage from other sources.
Consider some kind of bund arund around the main turbine hall waste oil tank and any options on alarms ie hi and hihi and bund alarm although this may not be feasable.

TITLE: Member of Public has advised site that very rare birds are nesting and breeding on one of the stack platforms.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Dear Uniper
> I am emailing you to let you know that a pair of Ravens have built a nest on the chimney at the buildings of your Enfield site and appear to now be incubating eggs there. I was viewing these birds from the River Lee towpath east of the chimney and from the pathway that runs from Brancroft Way to Prince of Wales Field.
> I suspected a pair of Ravens were breeding somewhere in this area and have been making weekly visits to find them, which were only successful last Thursday.

> The nest has been built on a platform on the outside stairs at the chimney, so the birds would probably be subject to disturbance whenever these stairs are used. I was hoping you might be able to avoid disturbance of these birds during the next few months until they have successfully reared any young that hatch.
> Helping to protect the breeding of these birds may be something you would wish to publicise, given the public concern for the environment and for green energy these days.
> If you need any further information, please let me know. If it would help, I am happy to meet someone on site to discuss this further.

TITLE: Unit 6 Steam Turbine High Vibrations on Run-Up.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
From Enerlytics alert dated 22/03/2023 @ 14:38
During routine OLVMS monitoring, UTG noticed higher than normal levels of vibration along the ST shaft line during the run up on 16th March. The highest levels were seen on the IP/LP Eccentricities where levels peaked at 290 um pk-pk with the unit at 842 rpm, during a normal run up a typical amplitude at this speed would be 25-50 um pk-pk. The change in vibration was 1/rev driven suggesting the unit had run up with a temporary bend.

A review of the barring file prior to this run up shows that the turbine remained stationary for approximately 1 hour following the previous run down on the evening of 15th March. The barring file shows the rotor straightening across the barring period, however the elevated vibration levels had not fully subsided before the start of the run up. If the unit was had remained on barring for a few more hours the rotor may had been able to fully straighten prior to starting.

Once the machine reached full speed and was loaded up, the vibration levels subsided as the machine straighten. Subsequent run ups and run downs have passed by without incident, comparing well to previous and giving no cause for concern.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Investigate the reasons for the turning gear not engaging at the correct time.

TITLE: Tailgate entry to site - poor attitude
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A Transit connect approached the site gate, buzzed the control room and after a conversation with the shift operator it was concluded that the person was at the wrong site and should be next door at the cement factory.

5 min later the Transit Connect appeared and parked to the side of the main gate. After approx 10 mins a contractor who is erecting a new fence arrived at site and drove to the barrier to card in. At this point the Transit drove immediately behind the fencing contractor and tail gated them into the site, by-passing security.

Uniper colleague immediately left the control room to challenge the driver of the transit connect who had followed the fencing contractor and parked close to them. The first person Uniper colleague saw was the fencing contractor leaving their vehicle. They were asked who the person was in the Transit connect and they said they didn't know.

Uniper colleague approached the driver to ask who they were, why they'd tailgated through and who they were here to see.

They told me their Manager had told them to do it. Asked who their manager was and who they were here to see. They didn't know either but said they were here to wok with the fencing contractor. The person was extremely aggressive and confrontational. They were asked to remain in their van whilst Uniper colleague spoke to the contractor. It transpired the individual was here to work with them and was an agency temp. Due to the poor attitude displayed from arriving at site when engaged and the security breach. Requested that the contract company removed the individual from site.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Contract company contacted and contractor prevented from commencing work.

Further investigation with the contract company will be sort.

TITLE: Op Loss - U3 turbine barring without jacking oil.
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Unit 3 AUO found jacking oil pumps to be out of service on routine checks, turbine was barring at the time.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
From the MCR unit 3 rear panel jacking oil pumps were showing in service but on the turbine oil page no amps were showing, the turbine was taken off barring and turbine team representatives informed. During investigation an outage isolator at the 39' level was found to be switched off (assumed to be in series between the contactors and motors), this was switched back on and the pumps ran, the barring motor amps were found not to have been high and in line with previous runs. 
The decision was made not to attempt barring until the turbine team were happy.
The turbine team representatives checked jacking oil pressure etc.. and gave the go ahead to return the machine onto barring.

Recommend reviewing the suitability and functionality barring gear interlocks.

TITLE: PSO - U3 HP Shaft Position Indication Found Reading Off Scale
CASE_DESCRIPTION: The EC&I team were Investigating an oil leak on U3 HP Shaft position Differential Expansion probe.  It is standard practice to look at the current reading and note any standing alarms before any work is done.  The module was reading -1.25mm hard off scale.  There were no plant alarms standing.  Trending the value on the Ovation DCS revealed that the HP Shaft position had been reading off scale since 22/10/2021, just over 1 year.  Since this date, the generating unit has run many times with no accurate visibility of the turbine shaft position.  It was found that the alarms were not enabled in the measurement module.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The HP shaft position recalibrated and returned to service.
Module alarms have been re-instated.

TITLE:
61BMA / BFB breaker closed when it shouldn't have.
Extended 31/05 see comments
CASE_DESCRIPTION: A fault on a separate CB required the 61BFB board to be switched out of service. This required changing the 61BMA board over from BFB board supply to BFA board supply. I opened the BFB / BMA circuit breaker and the BFA / BMA circuit breaker did not close on auto (as I believe it should have). Rather than close it, we awaited the standby diesel generator to cut in and take the board and back-sync the BMA board onto the BFA board. Once synchronised, the standby diesel generator shut down as expected. We were then just assessing what further actions were required on the BFB board, when the BFB / BMA circuit breaker closed automatically when it shouldn't have. This commoned up two supplies through the BMA board and two separate 11kv feeds which should not be allowed.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Understand why this has happened, enable a hazop to determine whether it should be allowed to happen and if not (which I'm pretty sure is the case), carry out modifications to ensure that it can't happen again. Photo attached.
text_features:
61BMA / BFB breaker closed when it shouldn't have.
Extended 31/05 see comments. A fault on a separate CB required the 61BFB board to be switched out of service. This required changing the 61BMA board over from BFB board supply to BFA board supply. I opened the BFB / BMA circuit breaker and the BFA / BMA circuit breaker did not close on auto (as I believe it should have). Rather than close it, we awaited the standby diesel generator to cut in and take the board and back-sync the BMA board onto the BFA board. Once synchronised, the standby diesel generator shut down as expected. We were then just assessing what further actions were required on the BFB board, when the BFB / BMA circuit breaker closed automatically when it shouldn't have. This commoned up two supplies through the BMA board and two separate 11kv feeds which should not be allowed.

TITLE: U6 CW pump 2 motor testing
CASE_DESCRIPTION:

No safety precautions were attached to the LWC to prevent the motor being energized prior to or during the test, where direct contact with HV conductors would have been required, well within the approved safety distance for 11KV apparatus.

TITLE: Removal of Waste from CDC site non-compliance
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Re-power project Trant Engineering additional work scope on behalf of EDF to remove old transformer bunds BHT03 and BHT05 waste.
EDF via email 24/03/2023 issued waste collection note to Uniper project team as documentary evidence to be added to project handover documentation of which was in addition to Hitachi (main contractor work scope).
On review of information project team had a meeting on the 04/04/2023 CDC Environmental officer to determine that project teams understanding was correct, the process had not been followed and that the documentation was non compliant for the reasons given below prior to issuing response to EDF.

Waste collection note issued is non-compliant for the following reasons: 
•	The collection and delivery addresses are to be in full including post codes
•	SIC code 3511 is missing
•	Producer (Uniper) has not signed the document and the declaration which has been ticked should be a declaration for the producer (Uniper) to sign (Appears that waste has been removed from CDC site without signed authorisation from Uniper representative as per agreed process).
•	Tonnage is not acceptable as 1 load as there are 2 EWC codes 17.01.01 and 17.05.04 in which Uniper require separate tonnage per code 

In addition Uniper have checked the waste carrier license 401 5100 30 and confirm license is still valid. Prior to waste being removed from Uniper CDC site Uniper should of received completed waste classification forms (WM3 assessments) for the 2 different wastes. As the EWC codes are mirror codes and have been deemed as non-hazardous by Trant Uniper require analysis data i.e. copy of test results to demonstrate non-hazardous waste. This information should have been provided to Uniper for review and acceptance prior to any waste being removed from site as per agreed process, this does not appear to have happened and a synergi case has been raised.

Response sent to EDF 04/04/2023 to provide the correct documentation and carry out an investigation with Trant Engineering and to provide an update to enable Uniper to complete the investigation.

Client was notified  immediately and all other notifications sent within the golden hour.  The IP was taken to the hospital where he was checked for concussion and glue applied to the laceration.  The IP has returned to work this morning.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Area cordoned off whilst Uniper Safety assessed the area.  Pictures taken and discussions with on site personnel.
IP transported to hospital
All notifications sent with all managers informed.
Discussion with Site manger regarding mitigation.
24hr Incident report requested
7 day incident report requested.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:

	Protection circuit tripped the Steam turbine / unit on Max 2 HP Steam Pressure

TITLE: Main Cooling Water Bar Screen Dropped from Height
CASE_DESCRIPTION: During Bar Screen Cleaning Routine Activities, the 4T Bar Screen was lifted using fixed hoist system and lifting device to walkway level. Whilst cleaning the screen it detached from lifting device falling 19m into the cooling water chamber along the guide rails. The working party where stood clear of the suspended load  - one of the team was cleaning the bar screens with a fork through the hand rail as per SSOW. When the gate dropped he quickly retracted the fork jolting his shoulder. The IP was taken to hospital as a precaution and returned to site the same day.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Work Stopped

IP taken to hospital as precaution and returned to site a few hours later

Golden hour and whiteness statements collected and Photos Taken

SSOW, MS and GSAF reviewed

Lifting Devise inspected by LOLER inspector and confirmed in good working order

Potential Causes identified and recovery plan presented to Exec

contractor HSSE representative mobilised to site

Gate Recovered with Lifting Device and confirmed the hook had not fully engaged on lifting eye during lifting operation - the gate lifting eye was balanced on the hook end which had not been identified during the lifting activities

Investigation wash up with on site team and Kaefer HSSE representative

Further Actions:

SSOW: Addition of hold point in method statement to verify fully engaged hook prior to cleaning works - to be added to Task List UGRC2070 Cr.01

Human Factors: Hook to be painted bright colour to easily identify its position when lifting from cooling water culvert

SSOW: Barnacles to be cleaned off lifting hook area as part of routine to give clear visibility and reduce any snagging risk

Human Factors: Local signage to be attached to handrail to remind personnel to check for hook engagement

Compliance: RIDDOR Reporting Requirement Assessment to be completed

TITLE: Blowdown Cooling System Control Panel Door Almost Fell Off Last Working Hinge
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The blowdown cooling system had stopped working during the heavy rain and is required to cool the blowdown before discharge to sea. The panel door for the control system has been broken since 2018 (21295453) and not repaired so assumed water ingress had caused the system to trip. The panel door is held shut with gaffer tape, but we assumed this was to try to keep the door shut and water-tight. The gaffer tape was cut to access the panel and upon opening the door it nearly fell off the 1 remaining hinge keeping the door in place. The other 2 hinges have clearly failed in the past as not fixed to the door anymore.
This is a heavy stainless-steel door and could have caused serious injury if it had fully detached.
There have been multiple defects raised for this door, yet it's not been fully repaired (21295453, 21312566, 21422651, 21452022)
HAZARD: Human Impact with a fixed object
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Immediate Action
1. Door secured as best as possible and gaffer tape reapplied to hold the door shut.

Recommendations
1. This door needs to be replaced asap before causing an injury to someone.

2. A survey of all broken panels and enclosure doors needs to be undertaken and a repair plan put in place as the site now has multiple doors held by gaffer tape which is unacceptable.

TITLE: PSNH - U3 A SSFP started unexpectedly
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Whilst de-earthing / de-isolating U3 A SSFP, the pump started unexpectedly. The 11kv breaker was first removed from earth by tripping the breaker mechanically. The 11kv breaker was then removed from earth position, de-isolated and placed back in the cubicle and racked into the service position. The breaker selector was then switched from the OFF position to the REMOTE position. The mechanical and LV isolations were de-isolated and pre start checks carried out. The liquid reg Lram was raised and lowered to ensure control, at the same time the oil pump was turned to remote in the switchroom and the oil pump started straight away. The operative made their way round to the A SSFP to leak check the oil system. When the operative got to the oil pump he found the SSFP was running and fully in service. Contact was made with the control room to find out who had started the pump, the reply was nobody. The pump was then taken out of service immediately. EC&I and Turbine team were both made aware so the cause of the unexpected start could be investigated.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
SSFP taken out of service. On Initial investigations by EC&I and Turbine teams it appears that there was a latched start command within the plc from 5 weeks previous when the 11Kv SSFP breaker was isolated and closed remotely to circuit earth position. Even though on de-isolation and de-earthing the breaker was tripped mechanically, this did not override the latched start command.  

EC&I to carry out 11Kv breaker interlock tests to confirm initial findings. (Planned 22/09)
A SSFP to be test run with Turbine Team in attendance following EC&I interlock checks.
Ops to review breaker isolation / de-isolation procedure based on EC&I findings.
EC&I to review breaker start latched command, to understand reason for start command duration.

TITLE: Excessive oil from drained pipework
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
ST Clutch Lube Oil supply pipe weld was commenced on Sunday morning 30th august 2020. 
On cutting the existing pipe the Doosan Tech saw more oil than he was expecting draining under head from the stub pipe he had cut, not under pressure just weiring over. 
He stopped work ,informed us and we went to investigate. 
There was quite a bit of oil in the gallery under the grating. We applied a spill kit and requested Wayne Chandler to assist cleaning it up with spill pads. 
There was about 10 litres of oil possibly that we mopped up and it stopped flowing from the stub.
We conducted a job stop and meeting with GE supervisor. jacking oil work was suspended while we established a cause.

 The reason for the oil draining from the pipework was the fact that the bearing pedestals had filled with oil because of the jacking oil being put into service constantly. The level would reach the supply pipework internally to the pedestal.
This then ran down the SUPPLY pipework, filling the blanked and previously drained line back to the tank.. 
It was drain under head only and a gentle weiring from the stub. It would drain and stop . when jacking oil back in service a little bit more would drain.

We fitted a drain hose to the cut stub pipe and this was placed into an IBC to collect any oil. Permit for Clutch supply pipe weld cancelled.
 Monday 31st August the line was drained at the supply blank and the blank removed . Lube oil pumps isolated and PFW issued to weld flange onto stub after line proved drained again..
 
 History;
Supply pipework drained and Lube oil blank fitted under PFW 2020/00819 on 01/08/2020 and entered into blanks register.
Drain /return lines back to tank remained available throughout.
This was the basis for our Clutch weld job.
Clutch weld job PFW2020/ 00945 issued 15/08/2020(proved drained) work allowed to commence 30/08/2020 (drained line now contained oil).
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
PFW cancelled and spill contained and cleared.
Alternative isolation method applied .
awareness of Oil retuning through supply pipework and alternative bearing isolation points to be considered.

TITLE: 400kV Trip
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During works to replace the Gen CB drive unit on GT12 a 'breaker failure protection' trip was instigated because the gen CB lost its position. This in turn sent an intertrip to GT11 and tripped the GT11 6.6kV incomer, excitation and common services feed. It would've done the same on GT12 as well but the 6.6kv board incomer and excitation CB were already locked open as part of the isolation. This would've also tripped the GT11 BFE (415v) board but this was being fed from GT21 as part of the works.

A 400kV trip was instigated as part of this, the DCS received the relevant alarms, however the 400kV did not trip.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Further investigation with National Grid, site and UTG have suggested that because the GT12 disconnector (X1093B) was open as part of the isolation, this prevented the 400kV CB (X1090) from operating.

TITLE: Spindle on isolation valve installed wrong way round
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
When performing isolation of the HP glycol pumps one of the isolation valves used for isolation did not isolate as expected, it was found in a closed position and opened for the isolation, it should have been the other way around. 

This was due to the spindle having been attached 90 degrees the wrong way to the valve, then when the handle was attached to the spindle although lined up correctly gave the appearance to the operator that the valve was open when really it was shut and vice versa.

This was picked up during the isolation process by the SAP, if this had not been identified it could have resulted in someone working on a pressurised system at around 3 bar. It also meant that during operations the equipment had been running without protection of the downstream pipework and lean glycol tank from over-pressurisation.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Spindle removed and fitted correct way round, other valves checked on HP glycol pumps 10 and 30. 

Recommend that list of other manual valves on site are identified and prioritised for action based on criticality.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:

This misunderstanding came about because the long text on the maintenance order only stated “Effluent Sump Pump “B” 415v Contactor”.

Due to the Long Text wording (associated with the functional location) being poorly described, the SAP was not directed to the correct item of plant to isolate.  The high level functional location description is however correct.

As the works preparer drilled down to the specific functional location, some of the preceding text disappears and leaves the Functional Location long text description information too generic, and in this case very open to interpretation.

The Craft Team member was unsure about the location of the source of supply quoted on their permit and rightly checked the location prior to starting work to find the isolation did not tie up with the works requested.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Works not started.  Recipient of safety document identified error and immediately reported to Permit Office.

TITLE: Drain valve on heating medium package boiler, drawing incorrect

Because of this uncertainty when the SAP was preparing the isolation and ensuring safety from the system, the flange on the drain valve was loosened in a controlled manner and some water wept out indicating it was connected to the wet side of the boiler. The boiler was offline at this point, containing a triethylene glycol water mixture which was at low pressure and cold.
HAZARD: Contact with hot liquids or gases
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: P&ID's have been updated with a red line amendment to make it clear that the drain valve is connected to the main boiler economiser (see attached documents).

TITLE: Lifting of a load without a tag line fitted.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A crane lift, of  sheeting panels onto U42 were witnessed without a tag line fitted. This caused the panels on both occasions to spin and bump into the side of the access platform and structure. No injury or damaged sustained.
Several staff members witnessed the incident and intervened.
The panel was blowing about and started to spin. The driver in the cherry picker moved his basket in to the panel to stop it spinning around so he could control it and place the panel where it needed to go. Whilst several of the witnesses set off  to speak to the working party, they started lifting another panel so they decided to let them finish. As the panel was being lifted they noticed that there wasn’t a tagline attached. Again, the panel started blowing about and was slammed in to the steel work of the enclosure, the panel struck the steel work another 2 times before the driver in the cherry picker could control it. Two of witnesses went and spoke to the rigging crew and supervisor on the ground who were stood watching the lift, they were asked to use a tag line, which was about 2m away. The lifting party were reminded that if it’s too windy, don’t carry out the lift.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The crane lift was witnessed and stopped (by Uniper) and the lift supervisor and his team were spoken to about the occurrence. Siemens and their sub-contractor's safety managers informed.
It was recommended by Uniper, that Siemens undertake a safety stand-down before work commence on the next working day and highlight the incident witnessed.

TITLE: Undertaking work on valve removal and replacement to the HCL line and storage tank within the bunded area.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The subject of LONE WORKING was brought to the attention of Carl Newcombe ( UNIPER ) by the Contractors (Phoenix) who had observed a UNIPER person lone working on an aspect of the HCL system which involved breaking into system within the confines of its Bund. 

I realise on initial review and discussion that:

•	He was wearing the correct PPE for the works.
•	Had a Safety Document issued by the SAP which had ensured safety from the system was in place, with WO and RAMS which apparently covered the work.
•	Person involved had a radio on the understanding that this was his means of communication with the Control Rm in the event of distress, injury or other problem.

Although all these points were in place on review of the RAMS; 

•	The RAMS generated by Eclipse on SAP did state No Lone Working at the very end of the Risk assessment.

What is the interpretation that should be followed when it states No Lone Working on the RAMS. 
My current thought is what passed without event on the day in question, next time might not and being reliant on a radio may not offer the timely response required.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Review of the work order and associated RAMs carried out, with a discussion with the person in question to understand his thought process and interpretation of Lone working. 
It was considered that the radio removed the lone working aspect by the person involved, the scope of work may have been small and straight forward but clarification of what is deemed as lone working and how this can be correctly managed at a site with minimal working hands available should be reviewed.

TITLE: Steam Turbine Trip on Run up
CASE_DESCRIPTION: On run up this morning the steam turbine tripped at 44Hz due to low reheat steam temperature. Steam turbine had to slowed using the E shaft vac valve. On re run off the steam turbine program the step sequence faulted at step 18,This has led to believe to be the start up device. This is infact the steam turbine program looking for X5 which is lost, the Start up device appears to be a red herring. We found that even if the steam turbine is selected to fast from a trip it still looks for X5 positive which is not the same criteria of a HOF start. Hence the start up device is not the issue. Defects have been entered for the reheat thermocouples reading low.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Alarm report printed and graphs studied. Report sent out by Operations with the findings. Defects entered in SAP as high priority.ET informed of operating parameter for HOF start.

TITLE: Main Gas Valve would not open.
CASE_DESCRIPTION: A recent Gas detection panel fault had closed the sites main Gas valve 10EKG70AA001 on protection. During the unit start up 3 attempts were made to start the GT for it’s DP run scheduled for 15:00 – 21:00. Each attempt failed due to time out of the fuel gas program as a result of 10EKG70AA001 not opening in time. On the 3rd start attempt, the valve was locally observed to see what was happening. It became apparent that the valve was trying to run open but not moving more than a fraction. Numerous attempts were made to drive the valve open, both electrically from the DCS, locally and manually using the handwheel. It was concluded the valve was either mechanically jammed or pressure locked. After some discussion, the decision was made to try and reduce the pressure upstream of the valve by venting off gas from the pre-heater. This was successful and allowed the valve to be re-opened.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Pressure reduced upstream of the valve to allow movement.

TITLE: U1 Boiler HP Sootblower Control Valve 255.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On Monday 27th September at approx 0830, a Permit For Work ROMP ( Restoration of Motive Power) was issued from the Outage permit for work office to allow the set-up of limits and stroking of pneumatic valve 255 following outage works.  At the time of issue the boiler was being set up for a Hydraulic test.  As per normal procedure and prior to the hydraulic, all issued docs were checked and any relevant safety documents that could affect the hydraulic were suspended.  Between the times of the check of the issued documents and start of the boiler hydraulic, the ROMP for valve 255 was issued without the issuing SAP making the connection to it being affected by the boiler hydraulic.  The CP who collected the Romp proceeded to his point of work, made the air supply available and started to stroke the valve from the local junction box.  As the valve opened there was a release of pressure within the process pipework, which was 'quite loud' and caused vibration within the pipework.  This startled the CP and he proceeded to shut the control air valve immediately.   The CP reported straight to the Outage duty SAP who attended the point of work and realised the ROMP should not have been in force during the boiler hydraulic test. TITLE: WTP Effluent Tank Leak in to Bund.
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Shift team received a radio message from Kaefer at approx. 15:00 11/10/21 reporting a very high level in WTP Effluent Tanks bund. Shift team immediately investigated and confirmed high level. No evidence to suggest the leak had breached the bund and no evidence of any release to ground. Effluent systems made unavailable and pumps electrically isolated. Area was then barriered off to restrict access. Potential leak source from flanged joint on 09SDATK080 identified, tank level  below level this joint at time of issue and leakage had stopped . Contents of bund sampled and were approx. 11pH. 09SXSUV001 and 002 closed as a precaution. Shift Team called Veolia Emergency response to arrange for tanker to empty bund contents. Shift team continuously monitored bund level using CCR cameras and carried out regular inspections of location to ensure no increase in level or leakage from bund until Ancorra attended site 10:30 12/10/21 to empty bund contents. Bund emptied of contents by 14:00 12/10/21.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Actions Taken:
- Effluent System isolated to ensure no further leakage in to bund.
- Area barriered off to restrict access to persons and continuously monitored.
- 09SXSUV001 and UV002 (Site road drains) shut as a precaution.
- Emergency response contractor contacted to arrange for tanker to remove contents.
Recommended Further actions:
- Investigate, confirm and understand failure mechanism that has allowed effluent to leak in to bund and mitigate. 
- Maintain continuous monitoring of area until failure understood.
- Review Veolia contract and expected performance as other contractor had to provide tanker.
- Provide high level alarm for Effluent bund.

TITLE: Activation of GPP EDP system
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Routine preventative maintenance on Motor Control Centers in the Holford LV Switch Room caused an unexpected coms error in the installation's Safety Instrumented System (SIS).  Upon detection of the coms error (and in line with its design), the SIS automatically activated a controlled de-pressurization of the Gas Processing Plant through the site vent stack.  Following identification of the cause of the coms error, the de-pressurization process was aborted within approximately five minutes. The vent stack is designed and located to ensure the safety of all personnel during venting.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
- The site team followed our existing emergency response procedures - ensuring that key parties were informed and actions and decisions were logged.
- The site team attempted to replicate the faults through a repeat of the preventative maintenance work completed prior to the coms issue.  The coms issue could not be replicated.
- There were no standing SIS faults on the Alarm log 
- The GPP process was assessed for areas of potential risk in returning to service. The 
majority of the plant did not see large pressure swings with the exception of the 
compressors whose pressure reduced to 0.5barg. 
- The installation was balanced and re-pressurized in a controlled manner, using agreed methods.
- MCC inspections were put on hold pending further investigation of the root cause
- While the root cause of  the coms issue had not been completely understood, the plant was considered safe for RTS based on the work above, the low likelihood of reoccurrence and the knowledge that the installation would fail safe as designed.
- Full investigation of the incident will follow

TITLE: Steam Turbine Trip, Following Trip Testing
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Gas turbine overspeeds, steam turbine overspeeds & steam turbine HP stop valve/governor valve tested successfully. Plant was stable and running at 400MW.
12:09hrs TST IP SV + CV Left FAIL 18MAB11EA121. Whereby, IP steam turbine governor valve closed fully, but the IP stop valve remained in intermediate mode (18MAB11AA001). Result was worsened vacuum >250mbar causing the steam turbine to trip (18MAX43EZ903_XU51). REMIT call submitted to Trading approximately 12:10hrs. Load dropped to SEL, drum levels controlled, air cooled condenser demin sprays put into service and sequencer selected to bypass. Grid were called to inform them of the situation.
By 12:17hrs, SEL was achieved. Due to standby to bypass being selected, gas turbine continued to deload.
At about 12:28hrs, Trading called requesting a REMIT update: 70MW from 12:30hrs to 13:30hrs. Then, between 13:30 and 13:43hrs increase load from 70 to 240MW. Remain at SEL until 15:00hrs.
Grid called and updated.
~ 13:34hrs programme device became disabled on the steam turbine and was manually given an ON command. Steam turbine became to ramp up from 70 to 240MW.
Steam turbine, at the time of writing is stable, and control valve stresses are improving (26 & 68% for HP and IP valves respectively.)

TITLE: U4 main coalescer vent found open causing small (10-20L) oil spill.
CASE_DESCRIPTION: On Friday morning, a report was received to the outage office that there was oil dripping from the Coalescer drain separator vessel.  On investigation it was found that the Coalescer vent valve had been opened slightly.  The oil issuing into the Coalscer drain had eventually overcome the drains separator, and spilled a small amount of oil onto the basement floor.  The vent was closed immediately upon discovery.  It is not known how long, when or for what reason the vent was opened, but it is presumed it had been unintentionally knocked by a person or object at some point that morning.  There was no operational reason to operate or move the valve, and no-one was in the vicinity of the Coalscer when the open vent was discovered and closed.   The jacking oil pumps, oil tank and Coalescer were all available for normal service and at NWP.
HAZARD: Oil (Inc. contamination of land or water)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The Vent was returned to its normal operational position of fully closed.
Dresser Dry was placed on the area in the basement and subbasement immediately below the separator vessel, and a notification raised for the clean up.
Operatives in the surrounding area were asked if they had seen anyone in the immediate vicinity of the Coalescer that morning, but no-one had been seen working in the area.

TITLE: U4 Kue grit blast waste, failure to segregate waste as per agreed method resulting in additional work to properly segregate waste.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Kue a sub contractor to Doosan undertook grit blast of the primary and secondary platens in U4 boiler. Agreed method was to sweep and bag waste and transport to 'duct bags' on pallets to be segregated on site, this was part of method statement and confirmed again just prior to work. Work was undertaken from Friday 20/5/22 to Sunday 22/5/22. Altrad provided resource to collect the waste on pallets and to remove and store onsite. The work area was inspected at the end of the job, the main focus was the prep, however it was noted that the scaffold was clean, free of waste grit and the when asked if the plastic sheeting had been removed we were told "yes" Kue also made a point to say that the Altrad resource had been very helpful, as the Altrad resource had been set up specifically to remove the waste it was assumed that this therefore had gone well. Based on inspection of the work area, the Kue paper work was signed by Chris Onions, both for completion of the shot blast areas and that the work area was clean and tidy. Kue left site on Sunday 22/5/22.  

On Monday 23/5/22 the Environmental team enquired where the waste was stored as it could not be found. On enquiring with the Altrad resource, they confirmed that there had been no waste generated. It was at this point that it was realised that Kue had not followed the agreed method for waste removal and had undertaken a different method. On inspection of the ash hopper it became apparent that it contained the waste shot.

An enquiry with Kue via Doosan, it was confirmed that not waste was collected and bagged, it instead was swept off the sheeted scaffold directly into the ash hopper. No waste had left site, no waste had entered any other skip/bin and the total amount of waste was 4 tonnes. The waste is therefore contained in the ash hopper and will be removed by shovel and bag and disposed of as per original plan.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Identified where waste was, confirmed non had left site or placed in any other location. Agreed method to collect waste and store correctly.

TITLE:
Enfield issued with an SIR from National Grid. 
UTG & ABB concluding technical investigation EXTENDED 28/02/2022
CASE_DESCRIPTION: An incident occurred during the transformer testing which led to a huge MVAR swing of +160 to -78. This caused the grid voltage to drop from 136KV to 122KV. National Grid have now issued us with a Significant Incident Report to investigate and provide information on what happened and what went wrong.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
On the 18th November 2021 while carrying out Grid Code Compliance testing and with the unit operating at approximately 410MW and +220MVAr (lagging region) at the generator terminals (400MW and 120Mvar at the connection point) it was unexpectedly found during these planned tests, while the unit was settling after a tap of the the generator step up transformer was performed from taps 3 to 2, the Stator Current Limiter (SIL) within ABB Unitrol P excitation system became active and pulled the reactive power back to 0MVAr with a subsequent overshoot into the leading region (up until -70MVAr as shown as the orange signal in the below high speed recording). The reasoning for the large overshot is thought to be because of the high gain control of the SIL function. 

As a resultant of the SIL activation the effect unfortunately reduced both generator terminal and station board voltages by approximately 13% of nominal ( i.e. 21kV) and consequently reduced the 132kV system network voltage suddenly from 137kV down to 122kV. To counter act the effect of the SIL, the generator step up transformer was progressively tapped via controlled instructions from myself to our control room from taps 2 to 5 to increase the voltage back to as close to nominal and thus removing the unit from the SIL operating action. 

This counter action brought both the generator terminal and station board voltages relatively close nominal voltage and brought the 132kV system network voltage steadily back to 136kV, and the unit was left at position after NG Central Control Room (CCR) instructed Enfield not to carry out any further tapings. We inform NG CCR at this point that we would like to tap the unit back further towards unity power factor (i.e. tap 5 to 13) as there was a concern that the SIL could operate again if the system voltage were to alter thus moving the position of the reactive power at the generator terminals back towards the lagging region, however we were informed by NG CCR not to do this until all customers had been contacted and therefore the unit was left and no further tapping performed again until approximately 1 and half hours later.

TITLE: PSO - U3 MBFP Oil Cooler redundant pipework leak.
CASE_DESCRIPTION: While emptying U3 Main Lube Oil tank into the service oil tank for outage works, an oil leak was discovered at the MBFP oil coolers on an old redundant open ended pipe.  This pipe is linked to the oil transfer main which was under head pressure from the Main Lube Oil tank.  A small amount of oil leaked from the pipe into the reject tunnel, this was contained and cleaned within day.  The same pipe has a valve and blank in place on the other 3 other units.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:

Oil at oil coolers contained and cleaned, Reject tunnel oil mop in service with regular checks being carried out. Oil contained at reject tunnel sump and cleaned. Station drains, Sluice pumps and ash fines pumps all taken out of service as a precaution within 10 minutes of incident report. 
Further actions - 1) Investigate why U3 MBFP coolers redundant oil leg does not have a valve and blank in place as per other units, and why / when it was removed. Fit new valve / blank @ U3 and add signage. 2) Shut, lock and add signage to any other valves on the MBFP cooler redundant pipework legs across all units. 3) Look at the need to have all redundant valves and pipework removed and pipework permanently blanked.

TITLE: U1 61 Sootblower.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Whilst carrying out scaffolding to the full length of U1 No61 Sootblower, the opposing Sootblower on U2 (No62) went into service.  The operatives were scaffolding around the drive end of U1 61, so were in close proximity to U2 No62.  This particular style of Sootblower (of which there are at least 8 on section 2 per unit) have a section of unguarded shaft on the side of the drive end.  The Operatives were in close proximity to the unguarded rotating shaft and were installing supports directly below it.  The operative immediately reported this to their supervisor and the working party withdrew from the area.
There has been an assessment of the same design of Sootblower across unit 1 & 2 and all Sootblowers of this type have an approx 30" section of exposed shaft, of which at least 4 are at an accessible height on a walkway adjacent to a main stairwell.
The shafts do spin relatively slowly
Please note these are original design Sootblowers that have been installed and used for the station life, and I understand they have never been guarded.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
With immediate effect - All works on this design of Sootblower shall be carried out under a PFW (inc non intrusive scaffold and cleaning) with consideration being given to adjacent Sootblowers on the same unit and opposing Sootblowers on other units being isolated; if in close proximity to the exposed drive shaft.
Altrad supervisor to give a tool box talk to their team members and get them to inform the unit operator on both the unit they are working on and the adjacent unit if in close proximity.
Boiler team / Boiler contractor to assess the need to guard the section of sootblower exposed drive shaft.

TITLE: U7 HPB Steam Leak critical at drum level effecting WSC chemistry control
CASE_DESCRIPTION: U7 HPB steam leak at drum level on the continuous blow down valve, upon deisolation steam was whisping from the lagging and defected 08.11.  Today 23.11 steam leak is worse.
HAZARD: Temperature Extreme (Inc. Hot or cold surfaces, gases and environments)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
U7 HPB continuous blowdown isolators were closed and keys placed on IHC with permit office.  Shift TL heightened priority on defect again.  Exclusion zone erected. 

PEM109 - Ammonia dosing currently in manually operational mode - chemist asking for auto mode initiation.  Ref due to no phosphate dosing as no sample to HPB therefore, no auto sequence cut in.      Consequence is FAC.  More inspections on outage and more outage repairs.  

For Ammonia PEM109 use Feed conductivity and auto dose simulation cut in at 9 and cut out 10.     Note; this can only be for short term use.

Must ensure that the phosphate dosing for HPB is off on the dosing panel so as not to over dose as the conductivity is reading incorrectly as there is no sample to it. 

Continuous blowdown valve - there is an auto seq for operating this valve for two shifting mode and a running through mode.   The valve is isolated due to the steam leak therefore, auto sequence will not function.    There is also no access to any sample of the HPB therefore, process critical to get this system back online.  (Note; have been told by operations that if intermittent is used to blowdown they lose drum level and trip.

TITLE: Hire Car Loss of Acceleration when moving on to A1 carriageway with traffic
CASE_DESCRIPTION: While I was pulling out of a layby in a company provided hire car (supplied via Hertz) I attempted to accelerate to join the traffic in a safe manner.  I had waited for a suitable gap in the traffic and then proceeded to accelerate.  The car initially accelerated normally to 20mph and then accelerated at a significantly reduced level. Suggest a detailed inspection be carried out of the remaining air hoses and fittings and possible replacement during next plant outage.

When checking the A-site fire system @ ~09:30 the drain on the fire system manifold adjacent to block house 3a was found open.
This valve had not been open overnight and no permission had been given for the valve to be opened.
Taking into account the amount of water around the drain valve it is thought that it was opened at around the time the electric fire pump cut in.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Management teams informed.
All accessible valves locked off.

TITLE: Station and Unit Auxiliary steam header over pressurisation.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Unit 1 desync 2025hrs, Unit 4 sync 2207hrs, Unit 2 desync 2255hrs.
At 2254hrs Aux Boilers 210, 240 & 250 tripped due to a fleeting gas detector (Steam Generator 2 Gas Detector).
Until the Boiler system and gas slam shut valve could be reset the aux steam header was supplemented from Units 1 & 2, manually,  via SVAPCV019. This initially resulted in an momentary over pressurisation of the Auxiliary Steam Headers up to18Bar, (0*-SVA-025-PT).  Unit 3 Auxiliary Steam Header was isolated and depressurised for outage and so unaffected.
The Aux Steam header then dropped to 2 Bar before Aux Boilers 220 and 230 began loading enough to raise the pressure.
This resulted in the condenser pressures of Unit 1 reaching 165mBar and Unit 2 301mBar due to low gland steam pressures. Unit 4 vacuum was unaffected.
The Gas Treatment Plant was being started at the time of the trip, which required some venting of the compressor HP suction drum V403, and the wind was from the west (this may or may not relate to the gas detector trip).

The Unit Auxiliary Steam Header Safety Valves PSV003 are rated to lift at 18Bar according to the P&ID.

TITLE: Compressor 30 loss of comms from the Siemens Anti-Surge control system to the ABB 800xA DCS
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Compressor suction and discharge pressure, temperature and flow values freeze. Compressor still running until 18/06/22 09:00 

Compressor is then started again at 18/06 10:30, values come back at 18/06 12:30 values freeze again at 18/6 20:30 and compressor continued to run until 23:00. The values do not come back.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The Siemens UCP (Anti-surge control) and USS (Compressor safety) both have CP341 cards that handle serial RS485 Modbus comms back to the DCS through an RS485 convertor to RS232. 

The card was checked and found to have failed. The first incident of freezing of data could have been an early sign it was failing, but too soon before total failure to have done any pro-active maintenance. 

This incident has highlighted an issue that the failure of comms did not warn the operator, put the readings into fault, or stop the compressor and this allowed them to continue running the compressor.

Requires a mod to loss of comms that makes the compressor unavailable and faults out any IO that is linked to it

I went through the process of clearing documents with associated worklists and I am happy that this person understands his responsibility for the role of CP/NS for this process. 

I do not feel that any further action is required at this time.

TITLE: Unanticipated effect from altered Operator set point
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
An initial problem was detected with the GRUs where they were quickly dumping >6m3 hour of cold teg into the regen units on start up, which if wet could lead to a pressure trip. A modification was prepared for tuning out some poor control on the flow limiter on the stripping column.  However, it was not implemented because on closer inspection, the Rich TEG buffer vessel level Operator-adjustable set point was sitting at a low level.  Increasing the set point from 380 mm to 500 mm smoothed the start up process and prevented the pressure trips.

After a period of time, Operators detected that during the shut down of the GRUs, the TEG HP pumps were repeatedly turning on and off.  Investigation identified that this was because the auto-changeover setpoint of 1m3/hr was now being matched by the flow of Rich TEG from the buffer tank due to the changed setpoint (as described above).

There was no safety consequence to the pumps repeatedly changing over.  However, there was a potential plant damage risk.  Hence, this observation has been raised to determine any additional learning relating to the sites control of modification set points, including operator adjustable set points.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: No further immediate action required.  Further investigation of the installations control of set point modifications will be conducted by the Lead Process Engineer, DCS Engineer and Production Manager.

TITLE: Wrongly prioritised alarm
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
An alarm was discovered on unit 6 DCS linked to the Tantronic gas detection system. We often receive a lot of nuisance annunciations of this particular alarm due to low sample flows. On this occasion it was investigated and the same alarm was showing that there was a fault on the system (sample pump failure). This meant that there was no EV or SEV combustion ring gas detection and the alarm received was the same priority 3 alarm that you would receive for a low sample flow on one sample point.
A failure of a part of the gas detection system should give a more significant alarm.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
P1 notification raised and fault fixed immediately.
Alarm prioritisation for gas detection system needs to be looked at to make more robust.

TITLE: Underrated cutting/grinding disc for grinder
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A dip check by Kaefer & Uniper of Salko revealed that the speed rating of their cutting and grinding discs were not compatible with the speed rating of their angle grinder.
• 150mm Cutting/Grinding discs rated at 10,200 rpm Max.
• 125mm Angle grinder rated at11,000 rpm
The five inch angle grinders had been fitted with six inch guards, enabling incorrect discs to be fitted. Make sure the machine's speed is at or below the maximum operating speed of the wheel. Surpassing this rating risks not just wheel breakage but also the safety of the operative and adjacent personnel.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Identified angle grinders were taken out of service.
Briefing at CDM meeting.
TBT with working party and also at next outage briefing meeting.

TITLE: Nuts on compressor 10 floor
CASE_DESCRIPTION: On walkaround technician spotted several nuts on the floor of compressor 10 enclosure. On further investigation the nuts are from pipe supports at a height of approx. 3-4m and appear to have vibrated loose. Although the area is not a regular walkway they potentially could have struck someone.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Nuts have been replaced and the corresponding pipe supports on compressors 20 and 30 checked, these were found to be slightly loose. 

The area is not regularly accessed and only on very rare occasions when plant is running, so limited potential for nuts to vibrate loose when personnel in area.

Although not possible to fully understand root cause, likelihood is that this was due to poor installation. There is a vibration study for the compressors and associated piping completed by Southwest Research Institute (SWRI) whose recommendations have been followed. From anecdotal reports the area is not known to suffer from excessive vibration.

Next time maintenance is conducted on the compressors, whilst scaffold is erected checking these nuts will be also completed.

TITLE: GRU 30 incomplete combustion event and reboiler low pressure trip
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On the 28th February noticed puffs of black smoke being emitted from GRU 30 stack, not long after the Rich TEG feed had been introduced and on the following day the unit tripped on low reboiler pressure, again as the Rich TEG feed was being established.

The PI trend for the low pressure trip on the 1st March follows a very similar pattern to the trips observed in February & March 2020 and at the time wetter than normal Rich TEG was put forward as a possible explanation for a large spike in the reboiler pressure. However, the upstream GDU moisture analyser EKC10CQ001 wasn’t operating at the time which made this quite speculative.

One possible explanation for this could be the residual wetter than normal TEG held up in the contactors (approximately 14 m3) which would be transferred to the Rich Buffer tank in the subsequent withdrawals during which time it would be made partially drier by the incoming TEG although this would still have quite a high moisture content.

While the wet TEG theory remains far from conclusive it now has more credibility and GRU 30 was operated on the 2nd March with a Rich TEG feed which probably contained a more normal moisture content and no operating issues were observed.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Synergi 9408 from 30th March 2020 was last time we saw a similar trip. At the time there was one main theory that the trip was caused by high moisture levels in the gas. The plant was currently being operated in dual feed mode when moisture levels are high to double amount of glycol and therefore reduce moisture content of the gas. Since operating like this there had been no reoccurrences of the trip. 

Believed that the best course of action is to revert to dual feed mode on the contactors if the water content of the gas leaving the caverns increases significantly above the norm.

TITLE: SIS trip GRU20 reboiler high pressure QCA20ZP004
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Regen 20 was up and running and the cooling air pressure to the combustion chamber (QCA20ZP004) had started to drop off. 
Caused by ice forming over the cooling fan vent mesh which requires removal by technician. 

On this occasion though, it was an unusually freezing cold wet night and when technician went to remove the ice from the mesh they inadvertently made it worse as they wiped water across the mesh and it instantly froze blocking off all the air flow which resulted in the trip.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
This last occurred in January 2019 (Synergi: 3211).

The main action taken was to raise an MoC (235) to add a ‘smart’ DCS low pressure pre-alarm to QCA20ZP004 and QCA30ZP004 on GRU 20 and GRU 30 cooling air streams. 

To avoid the generation of nuisance or standing alarms this alarm will only be enabled after the associated cooling air fan running signal has been active for 300 seconds and the alarm will be disabled as soon as the fan running signal is lost.

This worked in this instance to allow the site team to respond, unfortunately the response exacerbated the issue in this instance.

TITLE: Ammonia Plant Trip
CASE_DESCRIPTION: At 17:05hrs B ammonia vaporiser tripped on low low level (61.25%) which caused the ammonia plant to trip. The first alarm received in the MCR was B vaporiser low low at 17:05hrs followed by the ammonia plant ESD at 17:06hrs.  Fortunately the plant was returned quickly avoiding high NOX levels, if a quick return had not been so forthcoming and NOX levels had breached the stations limits could have resulted in units being shut down.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Re-set ammonia plant trip, re-started C Vaporiser and returned plant to operational service.

TITLE: PSO - Ammonia plant trip after delivery
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
When disconnecting the vapour return hose at the tanker end there was a small release of ammonia vapour, causing the east side line-of-sight gas detector to initiate a SIS ammonia plant trip. The ammonia plant was forwarding to U3 at the time of the trip and NOx injection was lost for c.40 minutes, until ammonia plant was re-established.
To clarify both the tanker chiksan arm and vapour return hose were off-pressure. The chiksan arm had been successfully disconnected. Conclusion is that there must of been a small amount of liquid ammonia within the vapour return hose that was not evident (zero pressure & no frosting), which gassed off during disconnection.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
1. Ammonia Plant reset and returned to service.
2. Consider using steam lance or similar to heat tanker chiksan arm & vapour return hose to assist venting down prior to disconnection during cold ambient temperatures.

TITLE: Coronavirus Close Contact Assessment breach of EGTL COVID-19 Procedure.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On Friday 17th September it was reported that a GE/Fieldcore operative could not smell the wd40 he was using, as a precaution he took a LFT which proved positive, he left site in a controlled manner and the area sanitised, a close contact assessment completed. (He was a few days later confirmed positive by the official PCR).
3 operatives where identified and each had a LFT which all proved negative, they all had been double jabbed and were assessed able to carry on working as per Government advice.
However this against EGTL site procedure and against the instruction of the Grain Safety Team Leader who was contacted on A/L. The EGTL procedure insists that all Close Contacts should have been isolated until such time that the EGTL Appendix 9 RTW for Close Contacts had been completed. 
The Safety Team Leader did not find out until Tuesday 21st that the Close Contacts had been allowed to stay at work.
LFT have been conducted daily on the Close Contacts and surveillance and controls in place and negative results recorded.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
It has been 5 days since the event, an assessment has now been complete and concluded, as lateral flow tests have been conducted, all double jabbed and no symptoms have been observed that the risk of transmission and to Business Continuity has passed.
The fact that Government procedure has been followed is a mitigating factor due to the time passed, however the fact that our procedure has been breached and put at risk our Business Continuity warrants this investigation.

drains flushed with sea water from condenser to clear.
continual monitoring until issue cleared, and repeat monitoring to ensure no re- occurrence. Dosing point changed from condensate to feed tank.
Dosing lines and all condensate drains checked for leaks.

TITLE: Operational Loss - Pressurisation Fan Tripping - Fire Nearly Lost.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Unit 1 B Pressurisation Fan VSD tripped and two minutes later the mills in-service with dynamic classifiers tripped.
A Pressureisation Fan failed to start even though it was selected to remote and had no alarm standing. A Fan started in local and mills returned to service.

Unit MEL reduced to 230 MWs from 2030 until 2111.  Further in-balance losses incurred as Unit load drifted to 220 MWs sent out whilst furnace was brought under control.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
When alarm received for B Fan tripping Unit Operator started all oil burners whilst instructing the AUO to investigate why the A Fan would not start.
After 2 minutes and with the standby fan not in service, the following  classifiers tipped on Mills A/B / and C. Tripping the whole mill group. With oil burners in furnace remained stable but boiler pressure began to fall away and load followed.
Once A Fan was put into service, standby mill groups were put in-service and then the tripped mills were returned to service to remove any coal remaining in them.
Unit returned to full load. Defects were raised for the faults on both classifier air fans - 21383292 (A) & 21383293 (B).

TITLE: Gas Receiving Station Compound - Gas Inlet Isolating V/V.
CASE_DESCRIPTION: On arrival to Site, I heard an abnormal noise from the GRS. Upon investigation, I observed that the Gas Inlet Isolating V/V appears to have been affected by a drop in overnight temperature and caused the inlet seal face to let a small flow of gas through and into the interspace of the V/V. The safety document was rehashed to include the extra isolations and extra control measures due to the gas release in the area. All existing maintenance orders were reassigned to the new PFW and all relevant parties were informed of the reason for the change. Defect has been raised for V/V investigations (21350294)

TITLE: Review management of work system between Ops and Engineering and between the 5 Ops Shift Teams, with the aim of achieving consistency across the shift teams when assessing MO's and preparation of documents. In addition, investigate how to achieve a consistent standard of MO presented by engineering before placing on the weekly plan.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The following is an example of detail found on an MO and is an example that should never be allowed to happen: -

"While going through the plan today I noticed the above MO number already had a SAP decision on it, looking in enhancement it also had a Permit assigned to it – 2020/00406. 

As it looked like an older number I checked nisoft and this permit was “Not Issued” on 15/05/2020. 

I am concerned that we have received a MO on the plan that already has a safety decision applied along with a permit that is not ‘live’. I think the possibility of being able to re-using old MO’s needs investigating. I thought this was not possible. If it is then this has potentially serious consequences.

In this case the system has stopped any potential accidents as the MO could not be used with a cancelled/not issued document, however, If the original safety decision was at lower level such as a FWI and that MO was regurgitated but the plant/apparatus condition has since changed (therefore requiring precautions) it could prove to be more serious. As SAP’s we do not and can not check through every SAP decision that has already been made, some don’t even see this as they use GWOZ and only look at MO’s on the plan that are set to SRDR."

Questions I feel need answering are:
1. Who is capturing the volume of gaps in the standard of MO as there is no log book or day SAP in position.
2. What was captured in previous audits, regarding SAP MO's and documents, were any actions identified and carried out?
3. Discussion surrounding who and when a Safety Decision should be made to a MO and when is it suitable to place a document in 'mod' is being held across members of the Ops Team - should there be clarity from the management team so there is consistency?

TITLE: Rich buffer vessel pressure increase
CASE_DESCRIPTION: The rich glycol buffer vessel is pressure controlled by bleeding off excess gas via cascade flow control to an online glycol regeneration unit. The operator noticed a rising trend on the vessel pressure during a large withdrawal nomination . The gas flow control valve on the online regen was found to have a fixed output, and was not increasing the flowrate as the pressure overshot it's control setpoint. There was no obvious signs on the faceplates that there was an issue.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Second glycol regeneration unit was brought online to bring pressure correctly down to setpoint before any SIS trip or relief was activated. Upon investigating the control system, a variable in the background that toggles the cascade control on and off was found to be off. With this off the flow controller was set to a minimum flow rate. Although the regeneration unit had been off for a long period of time for maintenance, there is no mechanism where by this could have been accidently turned off from the faceplate. It was turned back on and is now working correctly. 

Further investigation will take place to try and identify how and why this was off.

TITLE: GT vibration trip setting
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During a run up to FSNL. 
21:22 Bearing 2 vib > max 1 alarm. DCS showed 20mm/s but this is the max of its range. GE suggested the GT should have tripped automatically but it didn't. 
21:23 GT reached FSNL and vibration has dropped

The reason for the GT not tripping on high vibration was investigated. The Bentley Nevada set points were checked and the trip levels are set at 14.7 when the GT trip matrix says they should be 11.8. With the 1.5x mulitplier on start up the 14.7 became 22.05 which was above the range of the instrument (20mm/s) so the GT did not trip. Once at FSNL the multipliers are not in effect so the trip limit was back to 14.7. 

Further investigation required.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: UTG contacted and they confirmed vibration had dropped to acceptable levels.

TITLE: PSNH  - U3 re-heater Intercept valve tripping leading to r/htr safety valve 166 to lift.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On unit 3 run-up A1 Re-heater Intercept valve tripped and went undetected. The unit was synchronised and proceeded to load up, at approx. 440MW Hot Re-heater safety valve 166 lifted as a result of the intercept valve being tripped. Although the HP exhaust pressure was only 40 bar, indicating the safety valve had lifted “light” (there are also 4 other R/htr safety valves passing on this unit).
The unit load was reduced to 230MW initially thus reducing R/htr pressure and enable a gag to be installed, unsuccessful the load had to be reduced further to 20MW allowing successful fitting of the gag. Unit load was then returned back to full capacity. 
The problem of the tripping intercept valves on fast (5 minute) run-ups has been highlighted several times in the past and a previous OIT raised. Also, the turbine valve tripping isn’t highlighted significantly enough, meaning operators can miss this crucial problem.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Unit load reduction to reduce r/htr pressure which allowed a gag to be fitted.
A plant SIM as been introduced from 19/01/2021 to "soften" to change over of turbine valves from ESV to governor thus preventing the tripping of the intercept valves. 

All turbine valve mal-function alarms should be transferred to the emergency alarm system on the unit.

All hot & cold r/htr safety valves should be inspected due to the amount that are passing on this unit and 166 lifting at a lower pressure.

TITLE: Operational Loss - U2 MBFP off barring
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Whilst off load the MBFP tripped off barring and would not restart. The turbine proved to be tight and would not hand barr. The unit came off load at 23:00, MBFP on barring at 23:30. At 01:30 the bottom belt temperature suddenly dropped from 284 to 187 Oc , 5 minutes later the turbine tripped, no other operational activity was taking place at the time. The temperature continued to fall down to 95 Oc at 3:30 with the turbine still stationary. In an attempt to rectify the situation the condenser level was reduced and loop pipe drains opened. This increased the bottom belt temperature back up to 180 Oc at 05:00 and enabled the turbine to be hand barred half a turn. It appears a build up of condensate occurred within the bottom belt however investigations could not identify the cause of this . The turbine was shut down correctly, all drains checked in the correct position.

TITLE: U3 B side 50ft furnace gantry unexpected movement
CASE_DESCRIPTION: U3 B side 50ft furnace gantry unexpectedly dropped approximately 1-2inches when being walked on.  Reported to control room who found that the gantry was 'wobbly' and not as secure as normal. Area was barriered off and notification raised (21388914).
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Person who reported the gantry movement worked for Altrad, they contacted Centre Desk to report the issue. Centre Desk investigated and barriered off the area. Altrad submitted a HSEQ Observation from and a notification was raised (21388914).

Friday (28/5/21) Inspection by boiler team found that the gantry had moved from off it lateral guide lugs and was found secure but wobbly. The plate that the gantry rests on visually was in good condition. The chains installed to stop the gantry falling if the plate fails were attached and visually in good condition. The kick plate bracket which is is the final safeguard of the gantry dropping was also found in good condition. It was therefore agreed that the gantry had not moved significantly vertically, but had moved slightly laterally.  Doosan attended to assist with the review and lifted the gantry back onto the lateral guide lugs by hand. This stopped the wobbly nature of the gantry. 

The Altrad HSEQ form stated the gantry had dropped 2 feet, this was of concern so until the person who reported could be spoken to confirm location and nature of movement in the afternoon it was decided that the gantry should be barriered off with scaffold and left so it could not be used. The other gantries on the unit were visually inspected also and no issued found. 

Altrad were spoken to in the PM and confirmed that it was a typo and the gantry had not dropped 2ft and instead dropped between what felt like 1-2inches and therefore was on a concern as the gantries do not normally move as much. Altrad had done the correct thing in reporting.

Barriers to be left up until an additional visual inspection can be conducted next week to confirm if the thermal movement of the boiler is causing the gantry to move out of the lateral guide lugs. Unit was hot during all inspections today, and would have been hot when the gantry moved.

It should be noted also that the gantry is local to the U3 furnace external tube leak failure in on 6th of November 2020 and required repair to the handrails. This may be of no consequence to this  synergi, but worth noting.

TITLE: U6 IP Bypass system Safety Valves Lifting
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
U6 PN off time 23:59hrs. At 23:57hrs the IP bypass Function Group deactivated (event message received), IP bypass SOV & CV and Warming Line V/v all Shut and Process Safety interlock activated. 
IP steam system Safety Valves lifted. (ST out of service, HP bypass valve Open).
At the DCS the IP bypass system spray water Valve recorded 90% Open but with little or no flow. 
At -3MW Generated Load a GT Trip was initiated from the Unit Desk.
The IP Safety Valves closed almost immediately.
On investigation it was determined the Condenser neck temperature had recorded a >Max 2 Temperature, which had deactivated the IP Bypass Function Group. At the IP bypass system spraywater Valve, the valve / positioner linkage was found not set correctly, the linkage cone was not in the correct position. The positioner output was asking for 90% but the valve was physically shut. The linkage cone was refitted, the valve was stroked from the CCR to confirm correct operation.
A notification was raised to check valve positioner linkage at next opportunity.
HAZARD: Environmental noise & vibration (Inc. complaints, technical breaches or affecting ecosystems)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: see case description above

Better communications are required.

TITLE: Gas Detection Panel failure.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
At approximately 13.29 the G as panel in control room failed initiating a GT protection level 1 & 2 trip.
It was assumed that voltage fluctuations from the SFC had possibly caused a supply MCB to the panel to trip. (Running the SFC has been known to play havoc with some actuators on site, in particular ones associated with the aux boiler). Initial investigations revealed the power source for the gas panel (415v switchboard 10GMA06) had not tripped but further investigation within the gas panel were made which ascertained there was no 240v power to it’s internal power supply. A small fast blow anti surge fuse was found blown in the 240v supply line to the power supply unit. A new one was sourced and fitted. 240v power was now restored to the power supply unit, but there was no 27v DC output from the unit. Although the DC supply healthy light was lit on the front of the panel (from the back up batteries), there was no functionality from the gas panel at all.
Members of the Engineering team were called to site and the power supply unit was removed and dismantled to reveal it was badly burnt out inside. An alternative 24v DC power supply unit was obtained and temporarily installed which allowed the gas panel to be reinstated.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Temporary 24v power supply unit installed.

TITLE: CO2 cylinder, uncontrolled discharge
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Planned replacement of Control room void CO2 bottles. Whilst connecting the activation solenoid the engineers noticed there was a slight leak, when trying to stop the leak the cylinders started to discharge. The control room was notified and sent to investigate they reported that CO2 was being vented.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Two calls were put out to evacuate the Turbine hall until further notice. Barriers were put in place and entrances either end of the turbine hall were manned to prevent access. Turbine hall doors were opened and the atmosphere monitored which showed local concentrations of CO2 only, depleted O2. 20.9 at barriers.
Both pits are now restricted but show normal O2 levels.
Isolations for this work were correct and did not contribute to this event.
A Call to return to work was put out when it was decided it was safe to do so.
The Cylinder continues to vent in a barriered off area with adequate ventilation.
