TITLE: U4 Fire Suppression CO2 Tank low level
CASE_DESCRIPTION: On 1st August 2020 CO2 in the fire suppression tank warmed and increased in pressure sufficiently to lift the pressure safety valve at 25 Bar and -12OC. On investigation the cooling compressor and fan were found not running. Various electrical and mechanical checks were performed to identify the reason for the non-running cooling system, finally a reset button on the compressor control pressure switch rectified the fault and the CO2 began to cool again. At 16:00 on the same day a subsequent check found that although the pressure and temperature had dropped to -15OC and 22 Bar, ice formed under the safety valve seat during its lifting had caused the valve to not correctly seat and loose further CO2 to a mass of 7.2 tonnes. The minimum mass required to protect the unit during operation is 8.0 tonnes so the unit was broken down until a delivery could be arranged.

TITLE: Like for like actuator issue
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Up until 2014 site had a problem in the Winter with the wellheads tripping on low temperature when the wellhead flow control valve was closed, usually when the DCS Stop or Adjustable Setpoint were reached at Pmin or Pmax. 

This trapped the gas between the wellhead and the control valve stopping the normal convection flows of warmer gas between the caverns. 

If the ambient temperature was below zero this static gas would cool to 0 degrees and activate the low temperature wellhead trip which is only intended to prevent low gas temperatures in the cavern and production tubing caused by a large, prolonged withdrawal.

To remedy this problem the trip was made ‘smart’ and was only activated if the flow control valve was open and it was deactivated when the valve was closed and no withdrawal could be occurring but this required a closed limit indication adding to the actuators. (see attached)

Since then 8 replacement actuator controllers were ordered that don’t come with the limits as standard and they have been in the stores for some time until one was fitted on H403 and were identified that the limits (there may have been an open limit fitted too) were missing.

The absence of the closed limit switch would not create a hazard and it would just generate the potential for an unnecessary trip.

This has been recorded as it is a case of a like for like replacement that isn’t.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Replacement actuator controllers ordered with correct limits set.

Process safety committee meeting to be organised with subject of tagging all equipment that has been subjected to a modification as discussion point.

TITLE: Ratcliffe 2020 EU ETS Gas Turbine Oil CO2 error
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Following submission of the 2020 verified Annual Emissions Report on 23rd March 2021 to the Environment Agency, an error was identified on the report. The error relates to the permitted fuel, F7 Gas Oil.  Activity data is taken from the turbine flow measurement system (GO FM1 and FM2) recording gas oil consumption to each gas turbine. The units of measure are recorded  in gallons, gallons are then subsequently converted to litres and finally converted to tonnes.  For the 2020 annual submission on 23rd March 2021 the  conversion factor of 4.54609 from gallons to litres was omitted from the calculation.  This resulted in an un-intentional under report of 664.04 tonnes of CO2.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The Annual Emissions Report was corrected, returned to the verifier for re-verification and subsequently submitted to the Environment Agency on 28th April 2021 (in advance of the deadline - 30th April 2021).  The additional EU Allowances were transferred to the registry account.  The additional EU Allowances were surrendered by the deadline of 30th April 2021.

To prevent a re-occurrence of an inaccurate gas turbine oil CO2 calculation, the spreadsheet used for calculating CO2 at Ratcliffe was revised to make the calculation steps of gas turbine oil more transparent and automated by avoiding the need for manual entry.

Being unable to enter the reduced MEL and UGC being unable to enter the MEL or reduce the PN for us, we incurred Significant Incidents from NGC for being 100Mw adrift of our PN and MEL. Eventually Siemens entered the MEL for us but not until 10:30hrs, with the EDL system down we had to receive telephone instructions for load drops to 350MW on Unit 1 and Unit 4, on EDL these will be seen as both units being 150Mw from their PN’s. As well as incurring significant incidents from NGC, there would have been significant imbalance across both unit’s and the loss of potential BOA’s or ancillary services costing us potential income.
The EDL system returned to us at 10:50 hrs when UGC informed us that their system had returned. For the record, the Nisoft system failed at the same time, this significantly impacted on us producing safety documents for the works to be carried out on the returning units, especially Unit 4 ‘A’ Coal Feeder.

TITLE: Ratcliffe Confined Space Procedures
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
I went to Ratcliffe Power Station to carry out internal visual inspection of the U3 main steam drum (part of the 2020 Statutory outage works).  This pressure vessel is classed as a “confined space”.

Prior to entry, we were informed by staff from the mechanical contractor that there was no requirement to wear any gas monitoring / detection equipment.  The mechanical contracting staff were working in the vessel when we arrived, however they exited the vessel to enable us to carry out our inspection work.

Before commencing work, we confirmed the lack of gas monitor requirement with a visit to the permit office / control room.

However, because a gas monitor is specified in our RAMS, we sourced a gas monitor from the Station Chemist and conducted our work as usual with a gas monitor attached.

This appeared to be an apparent change to the sites procedures.  Personal gas monitoring / detection equipment has been considered mandatory in confined spaces of this nature in previous years and at every other site UTG work on.   

We believe the Station has conducted a full investigation, therefore this is more for UTG learning.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Discuss with Station and understand learnings.

TITLE: Visitor Car Reversing Over Camera Cable
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A visitor to site was driving a car towards the gatehouse to enter the station. 
On approaching the station gatehouse barrier the visitor attempted to use their swipe card to raise the barrier.
When this did not work, after several attempts, they were instructed to return to the station gatehouse to check their access rights. 
On this instruction the visitor became frustrated, reversing their car quite quickly and clipping the metal cover that protected the power cable to the thermal monitoring camera. 
There did not appear to be any damage to the cable and the camera was still working, the security officer on duty reported the incident and the team responsible for this equipment were informed. 
The visitor returned to site about 30 minutes later with a visitor pass in a calmer manner and apologised for the incident.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: On finding out about the incident (~2 days after event occurred), the engineer who invited the visitor to site spoke to the visitor over their actions on the day and asked them to proceed calmer and with more care in the future. The reasons behind their pass not working were also discussed, and the engineer will ensure to confirm whether there is any history of site passes not working prior to other visitors arrival.

TITLE: Glycol Regeneration Unit 30 Low Pressure Trip
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Glycol Regeneration Unit 30 (GRU) tripped on Low Low Reboiler pressure when starting to process Rich Glycol. It appears QCA30AA101 Regen / Boil Off Gas Control Valve over shot when trying to balance the Reboiler pressure. On further investigation this follows similar trips on the 6th and 8th February.

This occurs as the Rich Triethylene Glycol (TEG) feed flow is increasing to close to the normal rate of around 6 m3/h. 

There is a spike in the reboiler pressure and in response the boil-off gas pressure control valve QCA30AA101 rapidly opens. This effectively controls the pressure rise which then rapidly reduces as the reboiler is vented through to the combustion chamber.

It would then appear that when a trips occurs QCA30AA101 cannot close quickly enough to maintain the reboiler pressure above the QCA30ZP005 low trip setpoint.

This trend pattern is common to all start ups but usually the pressure reduction is halted at around 30 mbarg. 

Worst case this could lead to air ingress into the reboiler from the combustion chamber creating a potentially flammable atmosphere.
HAZARD: Build up of an explosive atmosphere
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
There is no evidence to suggest that QCA30AA101 is not performing, as it opens and closes rapidly on demand and the valve was stroke checked twice, with no obvious issues revealed, after the February trips. It should be noted in all cases that the plant tripped to a safe state.

There is one main theory that the trip was caused by high moisture levels in the gas. The plant is currently being operated in dual feed mode when moisture levels are high to double amount of glycol and therefore reduce moisture content of the gas. Since operating like this there have been no reoccurrences of the trip. The situation will continue to be monitored and an action added to the sites action tracker to ensure this is closed out.

There is also an action to investigate whether these trips on the burner management system (not a SIS) can be added to the SIS activation log.

This incident has been closed and both actions above added to sites register.

The solution is non-conductive so there is not considered to be any safety implications.

TITLE: Leak on isolation valve
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Returning the heating medium boiler 10 to service following an outage, a leaking double block and bleed (DBB) isolation valve on the gas supply was identified. The valve is located outside in a cabinet at the top of the stairs and the KKS is EKT10AA010. Initially both the valves on the DBB arrangement were leaking from their stems, with the upstream valve leaking at a rate where you could hear and smell the leak. The valves have been backed off slightly and the glands nipped up. This has sealed the leak on the downstream valve and the upstream gland leak to the point where it is no longer audible and can’t be detected by odour, or a gas monitor. They will be changed out as a matter of priority.
HAZARD: Build up of an explosive atmosphere
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The cabinet has an open back so is not fully enclosed, it is located outside at the top of the heating medium package stairs and the door is currently open, the system is low pressure at around 3.6 bar. 

The valve is being monitored for signs of any degradation by shift technicians, a defect has been raised in SAP and replacement valves have been ordered.

When contractors are in to carry out annual checks of the regulators on the off gas skid they will be asked to double check these valves in future. This will mean they are inspected annually for leaks. 

When the valve is taken out, it will be inspected and this may raise further actions depending on its condition.

TITLE: Operational loss - U2 MBFPT Overspeed test
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Whilst carrying out the MBFPT overspeed bolt injection the MBFP tripped causing a loss of 170MW. Tripped at 20:37 unit MEL to 330 MW from 20:53 to 21:10. The correct operational procedure was followed, with the trip bypass securely held down the manual trip was tested followed by No.1 bolt injection. Whilst selecting No.2 bolt and resetting the trip plunger the trip occurred. 

The cause is unknown, suspect an issue in the overspeed head that reduced the oil pressure which tripped the ESV and Governor valves. A successful retest was carried out when the unit dropped load before desynchronising. When discussing this with colleagues it appears the same issue has happened previously with a successful retest on that occasion
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: A successful retest was carried out when the unit dropped load before desynchronising. P1 defect 21350843.

It was also noted that the down movement of the crane has been temperamental and sometimes with the lever put in fast position it only creeps down whereas on other occasions it will function normally. 
 
This incident would have a potential for causing an injury and damaging equipment if continued to be used. It was immediately taken out of service, pending inspection/repair by the engineer.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Following this incident chain blocks were used to lower the diaphragms, with the down lever used only when the crane had all lifting tackle disconnected from the diaphragms.
The crane was isolated pending examination from the Cane Company Engineers PLS.

Unit 07 was loading up from 183MW to 410 MW following a cold start. At 11:03 a FWT Level MAX2 was received causing the emergency drain to open. Condensate control valve had opened from 50% to 69% during loading up period (to be expected) but did not close in upon receipt of high level, or when dump valve opened, therefore continued to feed the condenser at the same rate. Dump valve also had to be closed manually by the operator. Turbine hall has a lot of water deposited on to the floor as the current drain system cannot cope with this volume of water.
HP drum level feed was increasing, IP was steady and LP drum feed was decreasing.
Please could you investigate the logic, and if the dump closes on clearance of a drop in level (if at all) and if the control valve should react better to a high FW tank level.  This is becoming a more frequent occurrence on all the units.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Water hazard cleared up. 
Please can DCS team confirm how logic works regards to controlling feedwater tank level and the actions on a high level.
1, The FW tank emergency drain opens on a Max 2 alarm, does it close automatically on clearance of Max 2/Max 1 alarm or is manual intervention the only way to close it.
2, There is no alarm to indicate the dump valve has opened, Can we have a priority 1 alarm to warn the operator it has opened?
3, Can the logic be altered so that the dump valve auto closes on clearance of Max 2 alarm?
4, can the Max 2 alarm be changed from a priority 2 alarm (yellow) to a red priority 1 alarm?

TITLE: Lack of progress with IT connections that has now created a significant operational risk associated with the HE project at Enfield
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Following escalation of the issues associated with the installation of IT infrastructure and connectivity ahead of the Enfield HE upgrade Outage, it was agreed with Uniper IT to raise a case within Synergi Life to ensure that this matter is formally investigated to determine a root cause and measures to prevent re-occurrence. Keys points for consideration as follows:
• HE Project Team engaged IT last year on the scope and delivery requirements.
• The original agreed completion date for all IT works was w/c 23 March.
• The project team were informed on the day the IT project should have been delivered that it is now 2 months late (potentially 3 to full completion)
•  An order for a dedicated 100mb BT broadband line with a 60d ay lead time had not been processed.
•  IT were engaging a 3 person family contract business
• The late delivery leaves operations with a contract claims risk. 
• The operations team is now having to organise elements on the installation to get things moving.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Recovery plan developed and presented to HE Project Team, temporary solution agreed whilst full requirement is continued to be progressed.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:

Second attempt 850 bar. 
Third attempt 900 bar tool failed. 
Maximum DRS 83 operating pressure of 942 bar. 
The operatives have been trained in the use of ITH tools and have been on site working with this equipment since the start of the outage. 
Field core operating procedures were followed and the tool was secured in place to stop any items falling.

TITLE: Displacement of load whilst lifting with overhead crane
CASE_DESCRIPTION: A rotor had to be lifted off a lorry trailer for storage in the PES workshop. The rotor was already attached to the customer built lifting cradle. A drawing supplied by the customer highlighted the total weight, CoG and the lifting points. A local lifting plan was produced in line with PES procedure. The plan was to lift the load clear of the trailer, remove the trailer and lower the load 1.5mts to the ground. This procedure was adhered to but whilst lowering the load, it suddenly shifted forward slightly, causing the CoG to move thus resulting in an unbalanced load. Following a quick re-assessment the load was safely lower to the ground. No person was in any danger at any time as all lifting team members remained outside of the lift exclusion zone.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: The load was carefully lower to the floor and secured. A investigation will be undertaken to identify the reasons the load shifted. The load has to be placed into another storage location but no further lifting of this load will be possible until all the causes are identified.

TITLE: High pressure at pressure reduction valve manifold
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During an injection nomination at around 00:00, high pressure seen at pressure reduction valve (PRV) manifold (cavern pressure). On investigation no differential pressure was seen across the equalisation valve to the heat exchangers. Technician went to investigate and the equalisation gas bypass valve was open, despite showing closed on the plant control system (DCS). The valve was isolated at the time and then subsequently the limits were reset, during investigation at the time it appears to have lost it limits. Difficult to determine exactly why the limits were not correct as this occurred during the middle of the night. 

Believed a contributing factor could have been that the inlet separator valves may also have been passing and an increased pressure was observed at Inlet Separator 20 by the operator.

If the pressure had carried on increasing the plant would have tripped on high pressure.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Subsequently the Inlet Separator valves were therefore checked and no fault was found. During testing both of the inlet valves to Inlet Separators 20 & 30 were tight (i.e. no leaks) and travelled smoothly with no issues. 

The slight increase in pressure that was observed in Inlet Separators 10 & 30 could be put down to temperature (initial venting down plus an overall increase in ambient temperature over the course of the day), rather than the valves genuinely passing.

From testing it does not appear that the pressure increase at Inlet Separator 20 was a mechanical one associated with the valve (given that it operated smoothly and was leak tight when tested). It is possible that the valve was not 100% seated in it’s closed position when the original issue was observed, but given that during testing nothing was observed of concern with the valve directly, it may have been an issue with the actuator. However during testing there was relatively little additional movement in the actuator between the limits and the mechanical stop, and consequently, it was not considered necessary to adjust or reset the limits. 

It may have been that exercising the valve a few times enabled it to travel and fully hit the limit, whereas perhaps there had been a very slight drift and whilst the actuator had hit its limit, maybe it was just ‘on the edge’ of that limit and as a result, the valve wasn’t 100% tight on the seats, allowing it to pass.

On further investigation conclusion is that the bypass valve limits (EKC10AA110) were on the balance of probabilities incorrectly set last time they were adjusted. This is believed to be due to the fiddly nature of the Rotork settings screen and the ease of accidentally pressing wrong button, or missing a step in the sequence. On review not all technicians have attended a Rotork training course so one will be identified for attendance once COVID-19 restrictions have been lifted.

TITLE: Emergency Stop button activated on 5t overhead crane following the "up  control" button becoming stuck.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The task was to lower the 15mts fabric slings into a storage crate after lifting the generator rotor onto a flatbed lorry. The 5t hoist was selected for this task. The slings were to be lifted so they are fully extended and then lowered into the crate. Whilst extending the slings, the banksman signalled a stop sign to the crane operator after noticing the close proximity of a sling to the cantilever scaffolding. The crane driver immediately reacted and depressed the up button but unfortunately the hoist didn't stop and the hook continued to rise. Almost immediately, the sling caught a scaffold pole and the operator reacted by hitting the emergency stop button. After a quick assessment, the crane was repositioned and the slings lowered into the storage box.
No other working party was in the vicinity during the activity.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The slings were lowered into the storage box, to ensure no suspended load was left unattended. The scaffold structure was checked by PES staff and appeared stable.
The Project Manager was informed and a decision taken to ask the scaffold company to undertake an examination the following morning as the CDM area would be closed from 19:00hrs. An examination was undertaken by the scaffold company as planned, and the scaffold returned to service after changing a slightly bent tube.

CNC-02-JPH-HV -076 is the discharge isolation valve for Zone 5 which provides water deluge fire protection for Bearings 4, 5, 6 & 7.
The fire valves had been checked in the corrected position during the previous months routine carried out on 10/12/2018.

A LWC for the Activation of Deluge & Visual checks had been issued to TYCO on 17/12/18.
The work carried out under this LWC allowed for the operation of the above valve.
It is a possibility that the CNC-02-JPH-HV -076 was inadvertently left in the closed position following the deluge test.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Valve opened and relocked using a Plant Padlock.

TITLE: Review of alarm arrangements in compressors
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A HGSL Operator is developing a simulator of the control system.  This work requires systematic review of the alarm arrangements across the installation.  When reviewing smoke and gas detection within the compressor enclosures, the Operator noticed that the code for the compressor to "fail safe" in the event of detector power-loss did not reflect the arrangement elsewhere on the site.  Hence, based on the operators concern that the detectors were not "fail safe", testing was undertaken on the same day to isolate the power and review the function of the code.  The test identified that the detectors were fail safe, but used a slightly different code - most likely due to the automatic EDP function found on the compressors but not elsewhere on the plant.

This report has been raised to document both the findings of the test and to note the potential benefit in such proactive alarm reviews.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Test conducted and no issues found.

TITLE: No 2 Air Compressor failure
CASE_DESCRIPTION: 03:11 Main station air compressor 2 tripped. Compressor 1 cut in ok. Local investigation showed no display on local screen and compressor appeared dead. Did not want to reset compressor until some electrical fault finding has taken place. Placed on holding document and defect raised.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Compressor electrically isolated and placed on holding isolation
Engineers report after attending site
 
Just a summery of the call out received and attended on Saturday 20th July (@8am).

I was called out to Enfield Power Station to their ZT90VSD serial number APF204398, as shut down and completely dead.

Upon arrival I found the compressor without power, and upon investigation found that the incoming power was missing completely. 
I was advised by the customer that inverter fans were replaced a week ago due to failure.

Upon further investigation (see attached pictures) it appears that the inverter cabinet had experienced a MASSIVE heat issue, enough to burn/melt the cabinet filters in their holders, at the time I wasn’t sure if this was an historic fault as the inverter had obviously been overheating due to the faulty fans, and the new parts may well have already been on order….THIS WAS NOT THE CASE, Paul and Keith confirmed the filters were replaced when the inverter fans were renewed a week or so ago.

This leads me to believe the inverter has indeed failed taking out the customers breaker/main fuse….But as no electricians were available until Monday the power supply issue could not be rectified to identify this for sure.

But on inspection into the inverter (Through the cooling ducts located on the front) it can be observed that there is a lot of chemical/acid erosion to the PCB and its components, (the room the compressors are located in, EVERYTHING metal has a visible sign of chemical erosion and degradation of some type or another. NOT THE IDEAL ENVIROMENT FOR COMPRESSORS AND ELECTRICAL ITEMS TO BE LOCATED…In my opinion.

I also cant work out why one of the cabinet filter vent holes in the main door was blocked by cardboard? (see picture attached)

I removed Elektonikon and took it into the control room to try and power it up with a separate 24v supply to gain access to the event history, but this proved fruitless as it wouldn’t operate without the expansion module also….Replaced Elektonikon back into compressor and advised to call us again once the main supply issue had been rectified on Monday 22nd.

(@Kelly Stirling can you please raise me a breakdown job for this please.)

TITLE: Hazardous Substance Chemical/Material - exposure to carcinogens
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
DMW Analyst was carrying out the routine personal dust monitoring on the Altrad stripping team when they noticed an amount of dust in the atmosphere inside the asbestos tent.
The pump was worn for a duration of 40 minutes at 2 litres per min. The limit of detection for this personal was 0.06 fibres per ml, the calculated result was 0.31 fibres per ml after a reading of 100.5 fibres on the slide in 33 fields. This is a fail by a large margin.
After speaking to the ALTRAD supervisors, they have informed me their limit of detection is 0.50 fibres per ml, so the result for them is not a fail, but they have acknowledged the reading is unsatisfactory, so a tool box talk will be conducted with Altrad staff.
A second personal test was run on the same operative which passed and was well below my limit of detection of 0.06 fibres per ml.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Altrad working party spoken to about sufficiently wetting the asbestos prior to trying to strip the asbestos off. 
Working party supervisor informed of concerns.
Services team informed of incident and actions taken.

TITLE: U8 No.1 Boiler Feed Pump
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Unit Off Load and running down. Excessive vibrations experienced, witnessed at DCS and Locally.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
•	MBFP No.1 experienced excessive vibrations during a Unit shut down.
•	The vibration was witnessed as genuine locally to the pump and the pump was shut down.
•	Engineering inspected the pump exterior, pipework and associated hangers and found nothing untoward.
•	C&I inspected the fixing and connections of the vibration probes and no issues were found.
•	UTG Vibration Monitoring were contacted but unfortunately the Beran measurement system has had a long term issue and they could not analyse any historical data.
•	It was noted that at the time of the vibrations, there was a substantial disturbance in the suction strainer differential, possibly going out of range of the dP Transmitter.
•	On a cursory investigation of the logic it seems the Trip Logic for the strainer dP has not been configured and therefore did not trip the pump.
•	No.2 MBFP was run to ensure it was not a system issue. This was proved to be OK.
•	No.1 MBFP was run under close supervision by Engineering and appeared to run with no issues.
•	The FRV were manually closed in to all three drums to simulate full leak off.
•	The decision was made, based on recommendations from Engineering, to isolate MBFP No.1 ready for a strainer inspection in the morning. (pending a successful isolation.) PFW(I) 14/08/19
•	Notifications were raised for “Strainer Inspection” and “Investigate Strainer dP Trip Logic” and “Calibrate Strainer dP Transmitter” as requested.
•	These are all P1 Notifications due to No.2 MBFP having issues associated with pipe hangers - 2 x Hanger Shoes not connected

For clarity the pump is available for RTS & there are no restrictions as such. 
However whilst we have an outstanding defect and investigations are ongoing it would help Engineering if OPS could avoid/reduce operation of this pump by having No1 pump duty, avoid doing routine pump changeovers as an example.
Extract of email dated July 2019.

•	No.2 MBFP is now the Duty Pump.

TITLE: Missed GC A Validation check therefore 14 months between validations (should be max 12 months)
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Under EU ETS regulations the Gas Chromograph (GC) should be validated by Effectech every 12 months. GC A was validated in January 2017 and then not validated again until April 2018.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
GC B data was used in the stage 2 EU ETS submission covering the period that GC A was out validation i.e. Jan 2018 to April 2018 for the 2018 submission year. This approach was agreed by the LRQA verifier Graeme Clayton.

Metering Validation Strategy was changed (improved) from annual validations to the following process:-

Metering Stream 1 Validation
Gas Chromatograph A Validation + 3 months from Metering Stream 1 Validation.
Metering Stream 2 Validation + 3 months from Chromatograph A Validation.
Gas Chromatograph B Validation + 3 months from Metering Stream 2 Validation.

This loop continues at infinitum via SAP PM and current 3 year contract with Effectech.

The problem was enhanced due to the fact the length of time taken by procurement to transfer a PO to a contract for the new alignment of the work and the fact once site was attended for the validation, tracking had been lost as to which GC required validation, consequently the "in date" validated GC was revalidated.
It is believed with completion of the Live Log in a timely manner this occurrence should not be repeated.

TITLE: IP CV North loss of control
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
02:15 Plant loading up from 3356MW BOA to 410MW PN
02:50 Prior to the event there was a rise in 18MAD20CY022 to 172um (which also happened on Sunday when there was a similar IP CV issue). This dropped right off once the plant load was stable
02:50 ST sequencer alarms received.
02:57 IP CV north started to open and close erratically.
Local observations were unable to prove that the valve was physically moving, however:
the IP drum level started to rise, 
the LP system pressure increased to alarm value, 
the plant load had become unstable,  
the IP CV south started to move in response to the IP CV norths position,
18MAB10CP001 pressure of steam IP inlet was unstable,
LP by-pass opening and LP drum level falling,
The Vickers card panel was displaying a intermittent flashing red light,
Decided to drop load to 230MW to stabilise the plant and avoid possible trip.

03:26 Called Trading to REMIT MEL down to 230MW until 06:00
03:29 Called CH
03:48 Plant at 230MW and stable - Both IP CV's open at 100% and IP and LP by-passes closed.
03:56 Called Trading to REMIT MEL to 230MW until 12:00.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: MEL down to 230MW to stabilise the plant. Maintenance called for assistance.

TITLE: Operational loss (not process safety) - U1 Boiler recirc pump tripped / came out of service
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
U1 Boiler Recirc pump tripped/came out of service on Sat 07/03 @ 08:20 hrs with no abnormal alarms received, we were unable to restart the pump because when the pump was found out of service on a panel check, we were just outside of the 2.5hr window where we allowed restart it.
We have done some preliminary investigations and it appears the pump shut down around the time we were carrying out our routine weekend checks.
The particular checks in question involve us pressing the A & B side drum hydrastep level check alarm test buttons that are located on the Unit ESD panel, to confirm the alarm works.
We have carried out a controlled test and it appears that if both A & B side hydrasteps level buttons are tested at the same time, or in quick succession (both alarms up at the same time) this then takes the pump out of service on a drum low level (drum level low should trip the pump under normal conditions), however if the hydrasteps are tested one at a time then the pump remains in service. No alarms are received to indicate the recirc pump has tripped.

TITLE: Acid leak in acid bund
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During a routine water treatment plant stream regeneration it was found that acid had leaked from the system into the acid bund. The process was immediately stopped, and isolation valves closed. The acid within the bund was fuming off at this point making it difficult to approach the area, but estimations of level was about 3-4mm. Personnel withdraw from the area and opened exterior doors to provide some ventilation.
Email sent to all members of staff advising of the situation and asking them to cascade this to their direct reports and contractors.
After some discussion on the way forward and a Dynamic risk assessment had been carried out, an Operation Technician donned suitable PPE and respirator and re-entered the WTP room and pumped out the bund into the main sump. The bund was then washed down and pumped into the main sump, ready to be sent to the neutralisation tank.
The cause of the leak is suspected to be vent from the double block and bleed valve. There was no evidence of wet on the motor support plate or surrounding pipework.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Personnel withdraw from the area and opened exterior doors to provide some ventilation.
Email sent to all members of staff advising of the situation and asking them to cascade this to their direct reports and contractors.
Barriers put up at all access points.

Acid leak in acid bund. During a routine water treatment plant stream regeneration it was found that acid had leaked from the system into the acid bund. The process was immediately stopped, and isolation valves closed. The acid within the bund was fuming off at this point making it difficult to approach the area, but estimations of level was about 3-4mm. Personnel withdraw from the area and opened exterior doors to provide some ventilation.
Email sent to all members of staff advising of the situation and asking them to cascade this to their direct reports and contractors.
After some discussion on the way forward and a Dynamic risk assessment had been carried out, an Operation Technician donned suitable PPE and respirator and re-entered the WTP room and pumped out the bund into the main sump. The bund was then washed down and pumped into the main sump, ready to be sent to the neutralisation tank.
The cause of the leak is suspected to be vent from the double block and bleed valve. There was no evidence of wet on the motor support plate or surrounding pipework.

TITLE: Operational Loss (not process safety)- CW system
CASE_DESCRIPTION:

Upon immediate investigation it was found that the flow to the cell of the instrument had been interrupted by "slime" but the constant head device was still flowing so there wasn't and alarm indicting loss of flow. 
On the night shift 11/09/19 when dosing again the same situation occurred and again dosing was stopped as soon as the alarm
initiated and the purge flow adjusted accordingly. 
The C & I team investigated as soon as they arrived on the following day shift to confirm that the cell had blocked again. Although this was not a breach of our permit there are still implications and reporting required.

TITLE: Operational loss - U3 high extraction pump conductivities
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On the 24/10 U3 was fired and steam to set occurred, it was showing high extraction pump conductivities >5uS before and after column. on the return to service unit 3 boiler chemistry deviated from target conditions. The extraction pump chemistry went into alarm state 3 (>1.0uS after column conductivity) during its on load run and the boiler water chemistry followed with the after column conductivity peaking at 51uS (alarm state 3). 
Due to the unit being ran to increase pressure for trevi testing there was no caustic dosing in the boiler water therefore no
boiler water protection. The pH of the feed flow and boiler water remained beneath the required level for the duration. LP dosing only occurred whilst the unit was generating. 
The boiler was dosed on the morning of 26/10 with a firing dose after discussions with a boiler team representative and the trevi continued after the dose had been added. The boiler was fired for 3hours after the trevi test was completed to facilitate blowdown and dosing of the boiler water. There was no steam sample available to assess the amount of sodium that has passed through the attemperator sprays into the superheaters. Both shells of the condenser had saw dust added to try and slow the ingress of contaminants and it was questioned if a condenser shell could be taken out of service to help to identify which shell the leak was in.

TITLE: Gas Turbine Combustion Chamber Flame Eye Failure.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
CDC module was at full load.
A large flame was witnessed on the control room CCTV coming from the west side of the top of the gas turbine.
A decision was made to manually trip the gas turbine from the control room  back panel emergency stop push button as simultaneously the fire alarm panel began to sound.
The above all proceeded within approximately 30 seconds of the flames being witnessed.
The site evacuation alarm was sounded along with a tannoy instruction to evacuate site.
The station MEL was redec'd to 0MW and remitted with energy trading.
The plant was observed as it was shutdown and the visible flames stopped on the tripping of the plant.  
The main gas valve 10EKG70AA001 was closed and gas vented to remove all gas from the building. The FGPH outlet valves were manually closed to 10EFG70AA001 passing.
Approximately 15 minutes after the GT being tripped a visual inspection was made of the GT which confirmed the dislodging of a flange thought to be that of the flame eye and lagging being emitted from the blow off pipework on the west side of the GT.
As there was no further risk to personnel the site evacuation was ended with the UMC remaining off limits and locked down.
Further inspection and repair planning commenced with the Engineering Team.
HAZARD: Presence of volatile fumes, gases and vapours
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Plant tripped and site evacuated as detailed above in the case description.

TITLE: Emergency shutdown of Gas Turbine due to suspected combustion air leak.
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Fire alarm received at 04:43 UMC duct sensor (No.56 on fire panel). No other DCS alarms received.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Immediate investigation of UMC found excessive noise so the module was de-loaded SEL.

Further investigation found evidence of disturbed lagging on the east side of the GT and what sounded like a GT combustion air leak.
GT shut down was initiated and a MEL profile and REMIT was put to 0MW until 17:00hrs.
On the GT camera a slight haze noticeable on the east side on close inspection. 
No further DCS alarms were received and all GT vibration and combustion related trends showed normal readings as the GT was closely monitored during it's emergency shutdown.

Further inspection was made when it was safe to do so and the GT was off load. This revealed a flange off the east side centre of the GT compressor had been exposed with its lagging blown off. Initial thoughts were the flange on the latter stages of the GT Compressor which is blanking a hole were a redundant blow off pipework had previously been removed was the source of an air leak or with it being in close vicinity to the GT burners one of them could of been the source of the leak.

The Maintenance and Production Team Leaders were informed.

TITLE: Fuel Gas Pre-Heater shutdown / tripped causing GT Humming.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Valve 10EKT25AA101 FG P/HTR CIRC CTRL-V faulted with ‘Trouble Alarm’ and ‘Status Discrepancy Not Closed’. The valve had to be put in local operation at the Fuel Gas Pre-heater location and then manually operated in the open and closed  directions, the ‘fault re-set’ was then operated to clear the fault.  Multiple notifications under 21347109 are available to view valve fault history.  
During the valve fault the flow rate on the heating water side dropped and shut down the fuel gas preheater program.
 When the fuel gas preheater shuts down cooler natural gas flows to the GT burners. During this transition from Hot Gas to cooler gas the Gas turbine suffers combustion instability and combustion chamber rumble occurs causing GT Humming protection systems to operate.  
On the morning of 29-03-2021 the GT Humming protection operated as a direct result of cooler natural gas temperatures causing 0.2s to be added to the humming counter, there was a slight drop in load as the GT setpoint controller was switched off causing a slight imbalance during a load transient.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Gas turbine load transient rate decreased from 35MW/min to 6MW/min until heating restored to natural gas system ensuring no further combustion instabilities (humming)

TITLE: Potential for Duplicate Swipe Card Numbers to be allocated with different Access Control Cards
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Recently at Ratcliffe we've taken delivery of 600 new HID access control cards.  As of last month our previously issued E.On access control cards ran out and we started issuing from the new batch.

After a few days a couple of users informed us that when setting up SecurePrint on their new cards, when scanning in on the printers instead of taking them through the registration process it logged them in as another user.

We believe that this is due to the stored numbers on the two active people's different cards being the same, and/or SecurePrint not using the site code portion of the access control cards.

This is a data protection risk as there is a chance that these users with duplicate card numbers could print sensitieve personal data off the SecurePrint queue from that account that they are incorrectly logged into.

I've attached a flow diagram to explain the problem.

Fundamentally we believe that the fragmented way that Access Control cards are issued across the company and having a company wide access control card swipe system for the printers is why the risk of duplicate numbers on Access control cards is a data protection risk.

There is also a potential that these duplicate cards could allow someone access to another site that they are not authorised, but we don't believe this risk is high as the access control systems should use the site codes as well, but this will need investigating.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
An MS Form has gone out to the UK sites to gather basic information about their Access Control Systems and ID cards to ascertain what level of risk each site has.  (see links)

IT Security, Printer Management and Data Protection have been informed and I've requested a call.

For the two users that this has occured with, we have re-issued them with new access control cards.

An IT incident ticket has been raised (INC1028153)

TITLE: Tech Centre HV Maintenance Findings (May 24)
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During the Tech Centre HV Maintenance a number of age / condition related hazards were identified on the HV electrical equipment that have the potential to cause harm / business interruption:

1. Partial discharge (PD) activity was identified on the PTB transformer circuit cable termination at the 11kV Scientific & Tech Centre Switchboard.

2. Fixed earth contact on one phase sheared during maintenance operation of the Winking Hill 11kV Circuit Earth Switch at the 11kV Scientific & Tech Centre Switchboard.

3. PTA Transformer Buchholz gas detection relay did not operate when initially tested.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
1. Partial discharge activity - Cable split and additional installation material added over visible areas of discharge. Recommendations - Warning notice / access restriction to switch room and regular online PD monitoring to be performed and trended (to be included in a maintenance management system).

2. Broken earth contact - Temporary repair installed and returned to service (Ductor and IR tested). Recommendations - Temporary repair to be replaced with OEM part(s) or reverse engineered substitute. Operational restriction + associated warning notice to be applied to switchgear (all outgoing circuits). Plant simulation to be recorded on Ratcliffe PS temporary simulation register. Increased frequency of inspection / maintenance of 11kV switchgear (to be included in a maintenance management system).

3. Buchholz gas detection relay - Relay exercised and repeat tested. Increased frequency of inspection / maintenance of Buchholz relay (to be included in a maintenance management system).

COMPANY: Uniper Group (70006651) - Siemens Power Generation UK
TITLE: Testing of HV cables associated with SC10 SFC
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The tests were conducted by ICS who had installed, glanded & terminated the cables on behalf of EMI.

The agreed test was a VLF test for 15 minutes at 19kV RMS (27kV peak) on three conductors simultaneously.

People present:-

Uniper – Dave Rowlands (SFT)
Siemens – Louis Bucholsky
ICS – Graham Sloan (Test Engineer)
ICS – John More

Sequence of events:-

•	C/O Panel – Fuse Panel & C/O Panel – SFC Panel cables tested successfully
•	SFC Transformer - SFC Panel (10CJN91) cables (9 off) confirmed disconnected both ends
•	Continuity test of all 9 cables completed
•	Transformer cable ends all well clear 
•	U1 cable ends (3 off) in SFC panel connected together and insulated boots positioned between cable lugs and busbar
•	V1 cable ends (3 off) in SFC panel connected together and to earth and booted
•	W1 cable ends (3 off) in SFC panel connected together and to earth
•	1kV DC insulation resistance test conducted successfully on U1 cables 
•	19kV VLF test started on U1 cables
•	Flashover was heard 2 maybe 3 times in quick succession before the test was terminated. It is assumed the flashover occurred between one of the U1 cable ends and the U1 busbar.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Following an inspection and review it was determined the root cause, was ICS didn’t place sufficient temporary insulation round the cable ends. 

To avoid any further issues the subsequent tests were conducted successfully from the transformer with SFC end booted & shrouded and SFC busbars earthed.

TITLE: U1 OUTAGE - FLT Transporting Generator Casing Steel Plate
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A near hit incident occurred involving a forklift and a stack of heavy steel plates. The incident took place at outside Unit 1 turbine hall at approximately 14:05

Details of the Incident:

Forklift Operator:  PES 
Equipment Involved, Steel Plates

Sequence of Events:
The forklift was transporting a stack of heavy steel plates.
As the forklift took a corner, the plates began to slide off the forks.
The sliding plates posed a significant risk of falling and potentially causing injury or damage.

Immediate Actions Taken:
The forklift operator immediately stopped the vehicle to prevent further movement of the plates.
The area was cordoned off to ensure safety until the situation was stabilized.
Additional personnel were called to assist in safely repositioning the plates.

Root Cause Analysis:
Load Securing: It was identified that the steel plates were not adequately secured before transport.
Forklift Speed: The speed at which the corner was taken may have contributed to the instability of the load.
Corner Handling: The angle and method of turning the corner were reviewed for safety compliance.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Provide additional training for forklift operators on safe handling practices, especially when transporting heavy and potentially unstable loads.
Emphasize the importance of reducing speed and careful maneuvering when taking corners.
Conduct regular safety inspections to ensure compliance with load securing protocols.

TITLE: Oil store flooding due to Mulsifyre system discharge
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During the electrical works conducted on weekend of 15th/16th Feb the supplies to the oil store were isolated.  The mulsifyre system was still live and the loss of supplies to the store included loss to the mulsifyre compressor which primes the air sensing lines.  When the pressure in the lines dropped the fire system was discharged in the oil storage area.  This deluge caused damage to several boxes of grease cartridges and also allowed oil drip trays to overflow.  The contents of which went down the station drains.

Oily water also proceeded to pass through to the office area and into the switchroom and down a cable tunnel.

This was not discovered properly until Tuesday 18th Feb as the Altrad oil supervisor was working in the main stores on Monday 17th Feb and didn't go in to the oil stores.  Legacy issues with the fire alarm system prevented the Operation teams from identifying where the mulsifyre system had been discharged and led them to believe there was a significant leak.

TITLE: PSO - Main Control Block Fire Alarm
CASE_DESCRIPTION: The control block fire alarm sounded at 07.48hrs. A full sweep of the building commenced and the various fire panels were checked to identify the source of the alarm. The area identified was zone 1 ground floor. A burning smell was evident on entry to the area. When opening the Inverter Room switchroom door thick smoke and burning smell was evident. The switchroom was ventilated and checks of adjacent areas of the switchroom annex confirmed that the source of the smoke was from the Inverter Room. As the smoke cleared, on inspection none of the equipment in the associated switchroom appeared to be in distress! With the support of the electrical team each panel was inspected and it was believed that EML4 lighting inverter was the most likely source although it was still operating apparently normally.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Fire watch set up. Further discussions with the electrical team as to what further actions required. EML4 put on hard bypass and isolated for inspection by the OEM and routines on EML's 1, 2 & 3 also planned. Consider thorough inspections of all apparatus within the Inverter Room

TITLE: Humber Oil Refinery (P66) Condensate Valve ESD Trip
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The pressure of the steam to the Uniper heat exchanger rose to 4 bar and this caused the condensate ESD valve trip to shutting off the return line to HOR. HOR provide the steam for this system.
The system is designed to protect the steam pipework from gas infiltration caused by a tube break in the heat exchanger. However due to system design the pressure monitoring is on the steam side of the heat exchanger and is set at 4 bar, the system normally runs at approx 3 .5 bar.
The issue would be cold gas to the refinery which should be supplied at above 0 Deg C  ,with the valve shutoff the gas temperature remained above that.
HAZARD: Temperature Extreme (Inc. Hot or cold surfaces, gases and environments)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: The system was reset then it tripped again after 1/2 hr ,, therefore contact was made with HOR who provide the steam to our system and we advised them to lower the steam pressure. They looked at how this could be done but decided for there current process the benefits of a slightly higher LP steam pressure out weighed the negatives from colder gas.

TITLE: Failure of level transmitter during test
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During routine testing of the liquid level still chamber.
The “Control” level transmitter was found to have values entered the upper and lower ranges, that were different to the identical safety transmitter and identical control level transmitters on the two other identical vessels. 

It was also observed that the amplitude of the waveform seemed to be significantly lower than on the same device at other positions. 

The still well was filled with water and the level increase – immediately an issue with the “0” position was obvious the water level continued to be increased and no response was given from the transmitter.

The correct parameters were entered, and the waveform threshold retuned. 
The liquid level test then recommenced. 
The transmitter performed as expected at 
0 ,25,50,75,100% points. 

As the still well drained, the Transmitter registered the 75% point, however after that the reading froze despite the still chamber being totally empty. 

Should this have happened in normal operation the control valve could have opened despite the liquid level not being present. 

This would have likely put a demand on the SIF responsible for this protection.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
•	Survey and test remaining level transmitters on site and form a database of expected settings. 
•	Review stock holdings as replacement parts on site are not correct. 
•	Temporary MOC to cover isolation of transmitter for vessel RTS – TRA scheduled 26/10/23.

Ultimately the test was to see if level was working. It was not and action has been taken.

TITLE: Fire in waste laydown area.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Quote from duty TL email:
"There was a report of a fire from Richard Hanter of HBS at the contractors amenities at approx. 12:30 today.
The Ops team immediately responded to co-ordinate a tactical response. 
Upon reaching the contractors amenities it was clear that the fire was coming from the recycling area.
At the contractor cabin side of the recycling area we found Richard in a safe location where he raise our attention to the fire.

We quickly made an assessment of the fire and the resources to hand
(Flames 20/30cm, not spreading quickly – 2 water 2 dry powder and a water supply from the contractor amenities) 
The initial response was with the extinguishers to suppress 5 mins and then water hose left on to dampen down 45-50mins. (Until 13:45)

Further observations were such that the source of heat was associated with the brindle dry wood used to store the spare Titanium Condenser Tubes and 
the heat radiated from the metal work. There was no evidence of cigarette ends and or other third party source of ignition."
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Further investigation revealed some cutting work had been carried out in the area that day. The work had a hot work assessment. Discussed with work issuer - any further works all cutting is to be made by removing the material away from the area and removal of any combustible material.

TITLE: Sync Comp 400kV Alarms
CASE_DESCRIPTION: At 00:11 on 28/7/24 we received a 400kV interposing relay 110V DC MCB Trip alarm. This was raised as a P1 notification and communicated via email, although it did not cause any issues with the sync comp but it was a worrying alarm when added to other alarms that had been standing. A further alarm, 400kV CP 1 relay inoperative initiated at 11:15 and at 12:26 all indication was lost on X490, X493A, X493B & X493C, this prompted a discussion with TNCC and a request was made for the on call NGET SAP to attend site. On arrival, as expected from a previous alarm, the 110v battery charger was in fault and the output volts had dropped to 50V DC. This was the reason for the faults and it transpired, we had lost the fast acting trip capability.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
After further investigation it was determined that the 110V stand-by supplies could be applied by the installation of links in the X490 supply pillar and inserting fuses into the stand-by fuse holders at the top of the battery charger. This immediately brought the output voltage up to >120V. The unit on the HV Connection panel rebooted and the indication was restored to the switchgear graphics on the DCS and the alarm cleared.
All alarms have cleared down except the original 110V battery fault and the 400kV CBU Fault recorder alarms. Further investigations will have to be carried out on the battery charger unit under NF 21528133.

This transmitter is part of the Steam Turbine SIL rated (Safety Integrity Level)  protection functions. 
The modification process should ensure the new transmitters meet the reliability calculations required of the attached Safety Manual and therefore maintain the integrity of the protective function.
There is a risk that the integrity of the safety system has been compromised without due diligence.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Immediate Action
1. Reported situation to C&I Strategy Engineer who wasn't aware of change and agreed to raise modification.
2. Discussed situation with C&I Delivery Engineers to ascertain awareness of SIS system.

Recommendations:
1. Raise modification to cover the change.
2. Seek advice from Ansaldo / GE / ABB as to a suitable replacement transmitter to meet the requirement of the protection system.
3. Plan & Deliver Safety Instrument Systems awareness training to all engineers and operators.
4. Decide the best way to physically identify on plant all components of each Safety Related System so that people are aware at the point of work.

Note - Further actions covered in subsequent A1 41002143 SL Case. 49019 - Can be found in connected cases section.

TITLE: Maxum Hazardous Area Classification Pressurization / Purge
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Purge system on the analyser- the pressure gauge on the front of the analyser Purge air has always read “0”- confirmed by site documentation dating back to 2011. 

The Hazardous area code on the analyser contains a  “p” for pressurisation.

The Purge air regulator is connected directly into a monitoring system inside the analyser electronics enclosure ( this system is currently disabled) 

The analyser is installed in a zone 2 area. 

So the equipment has been operating in a zone 2 area without the protection system operational.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The idea of the purge monitoring system is to maintain a positive pressure differential inside the electrical enclosure as it is full of uncertified electrical equipment, such as valves, power supplies etc. 

The protection concept for this appears to be “p” (pressurisation)  and is stated in the Siemens manual as being a requirement if the analyser is installed in a zone 1 or zone 2 area. (it is in a zone 2) 

The regulator has been set at 5 psi for now, for the short term until we can commission the protection system, (if it is found that this should be enabled).

TITLE: Loss of Containment while returning U42 Sync Comp Cooling Pump 2 To Service
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
When returning to service a closed cooling circulation pump following maintenance, the operator didn't see the vent valve on the discharge pipe had been left open and process fluid was released into the area. The operator managed to shut the valve and minimise the release of fluid.
Following the incident it was also realised that the closed cooling system had lost system pressure and was in alarm. No-one on the shift had been trained to repressurise the system and there are no operator procedures are in place for the Sync Comp units to refer to. The location of the O&M manuals are also unknown.
The Uniper commissioning Engineer was contacted for advice on how to repressurise the system but the equipment didn't work.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Immediate Action
1.An email was sent to all SAP's to request that when vents and drains are left open and not part of the isolation, a note is left within the Key Safe to alert the person returning the plant to operational state.

Recommendations
1. As above, circulate best practice guidance to SAP's for logging of drains and vents not part of the isolation
2. Produce operational procedures for Sync Comp units
3. Ensure Sync Comp O&M manuals are accessible for both operations and engineering personnel.

TITLE: ENV - Ash Lagoon water level high

TITLE: Maintenance Order discrepancy between operational line description and PRT.
CASE_DESCRIPTION: I was looking to assess a Maintenance Order for set up actuator unit 4 FSR-UV -051. The operational line is for setting up the actuator and the long text stated set up actuator and adjust limits and torque settings. There is no safe system of work in the long text so i had a look at the PRT which is for generic Kaefer actuator stroke check fault find which allows them to carry out a full range of jobs including IR and balance checks,replacement of components and boards etc. If I had assessed this job on the long text the competent person would have had a Safety Document that i thought was for stroke checking the actuator but the method of work allows them to possibly do much more work. In my opinion there should be something written in to GMI SHE 003 which makes it clear that the work scope and method of work that an SAP assesses for the job from the long text needs to match any PRT.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Maintenance Order operational line rejected.

TITLE: Excavation above 33kV feeders
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Came across an unsupervised and unauthorised excavation carried out above our 33kV feeders, just as it was finishing (on public property by third party organisation).

The contractors read our marker posts around October time last year and using number on marker posts called the control room, they provided Engineering Manager's number and someone from their organisation contacted them.
A SAP was sent down to meet them and they described to them their plans. Our SAP instructed them to contact Engineering Manager with details on what they intended to do near our feeders and when.

They sent an email, but with what appears to have unfortunately been to the wrong email address. Therefore it was never identified by any Uniper personnel, so they never received a reply.

It appears that they took that as a green light to carry on with the work with no input from Uniper.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Discussions are ongoing with the contractor and their client as to how this occurred.

From initial discussions appears that the contractor followed safe working practices, but don't know at this stage if these align to Uniper standards.

There was no risk to Uniper personnel. The risk was to third party workers and also causing loss of power to site.

The process is we would issue a safety document for any work over or close to our feeders, which would include Uniper supervision. This did not happen in this instance.

Despite repeated efforts to contact contractor they have not responded. Action to be send letter via legal.

TITLE: FGD Ops Van Rear Light Cluster Damaged
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The CPO was asked to check the status of the towns water tank inlet pipework which had previously been identified as leaking, the CPO drove the van up Redhill tanks on  the  track, which was muddy. When the CPO arrived he parked the van and went to check the leaking pipework.  After the check was completed the CPO had to turn the van around to go back to the the track, upon reversing the van he slid on the mud into the undergrowth and damaged the rear drivers side light cluster.

The CPO used his mirrors (as the reversing camera didn't initiate - see below) but because he'd slid on the mud he couldn't avoid the 'bushes'. A point to note was that the reversing camera did not initiate whilst in reverse gear and it appears that if you are below a couple of mph then it doesn`t initiate the reversing camera.

TITLE: Forklift Truck Transporting Generator Steel Casing Plates
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Forklift Operator: PES

Equipment Involved: Forklift, Steel Plates

Sequence of Events:
The forklift was transporting a stack of heavy steel plates from the turbine hall on U1.
As the forklift took a corner whilst reversing backwards, the plates began to slide off the forks.
The sliding plates posed a significant risk of falling and potentially causing injury or damage.

Immediate Actions Taken:

The forklift operator immediately stopped the vehicle to prevent further movement of the plates.
Additional personnel were called to assist in safely repositioning the plates.

Root Cause Analysis:

Load Securing: It was identified that the steel plates were not adequately secured before transport.
Forklift Speed: The speed at which the corner was taken may have contributed to the instability of the load.
Corner Handling: The angle and method of turning the corner were reviewed for safety compliance.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Supervisor informed
No further lifting with fork lift truck. 
Movement operations between turbine halls
Correct mobile plant
Banks man

TITLE: Personnel Stuck in Alimak Lift
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Two embedded contractors entered the Alimak lift on the HRSG building, closed the doors as normal and pressed the '2' button to ascend. The usual drive mechanism engagement noise was heard but the lift did not move from its original position. After approximately fifteen seconds, the noise stopped, at which point the embedded contractors attempted to open the doors to exit the lift, but the doors were locked shut. MCR was contacted by radio and informed of the situation, at which point one of the shift operatives attended the scene. The doors could not be opened from the outside or the inside until the emergency door release handle was used inside the lift vehicle which released the doors and allowed the contractors to exit the lift.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: The lift has subsequently been isolated and locked off by the duty control person until further notice.

TITLE: GT Fire detection trigger
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
GT Fire operated at approx. 08:30 today. 
Investigations identified that a Smoke detector within the Turbine Hall HVAC extraction ducts had triggered the alarm.
The associated filter on the detector was today identified with what appeared to be oil residue The other 2 detectors in the ducting’s also where in a similar condition however still functioning. 
On external visual inspection of the GT it was identified that some browning around the turbine bearing vents at the 11 and 2 o’clock positions and this has caused lacquer formation This is believed to have been gradually increasing since 2022.
Some of this material was removed for analysis and to determine if it was as suspected oil or charring. -  from this it was determined that the residue appeared to be a mixture of oil vapor and dust . Not charring
Checks where made on the GT start bearing rodding point which appeared to be clear from Coking.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The fire detector filters in the HVAC ducting were cleaned and put back in service, the original operating one still showing a fault but functioning
Siemens have been contacted for advice on the issue which they have referred to engineering . The fire detection contractor is due to service the units next week
The cause and effects matrix for the fire detection system is being checked to ensure does not trigger the GT protection system.An area was cleaned on blow offline to determine future fouling rate.

TITLE: U4 Upsurge Control Valve No515 Control Air Valve missing isolation lock
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The safety isolation key for the Upsurge Control Valve No.515 Control Air valve was released from the T3B cascade key safe following the return of the T3B PFW.  The release of this key (safety key No 9727) allowed us to prepare for the PFW ROMP (Permit For Work with Restoration Of Motive Power), for the re-connection of the valve 515 and setting of the valve limits.   Following release of the key on the morning of the 13/07, the Outage Commissioning operative was asked to attach a ROMP notice to the valve in preparation for the issue of the safety document.  On getting to the valve location it was noted that there was no isolation lock on the valve as expected.  The chain that was used to isolate the valve was still attached to the valve body / pipework but there was no sign of the isolation lock.
The control valve and actuator had both been removed & replaced during the Outage period.  The air pipework and the valve spindle had both been disconnected to allow the removal / replacement of the valve / actuator.  The air isolation valve was not directly local to the valve, it was the master isolator approx 6ft away on the adjacent wall.
The Authorised Persons Isolation sheet was checked, and the isolation point had been double checked and double signed for at the start of the Outage period when the T3B cascade box was established; on release of the safety key from the key safe the signatures were crossed off of the AP sheet.  The immediate area was searched for any sign of a broken / damaged lock, but nothing could be found.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Valve No.515 local control air isolation valve has been isolated & pipework vented.

An investigation is required to understand the sequence of work carried out on the Control valve, and to understand what other works happened in that immediate area over the outage period.

TITLE: Misuse of 'Man Down' feature on Site Radios
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On the evening of 16th July 2024 around 20:00, the night security guard set off the ‘Man Down’ alert on his site radio, which was subsequently reset. Later, whilst undertaking the 22:00 site tour, the security guard failed to take the Gatehouse radio & site security mobile phone.
The Gatehouse radio was left in the Gatehouse and set to ‘Man Down On’ and thus activated an alert on the Gatehouse, CDC & KPS Control Room radio base stations.
Operations personnel in the CDC Control Room attempted to contact the security guard on the radio & site security mobile phone, to no avail.
Fortunately, operations personnel in the CDC Control Room were able to spot the security guard walking around site, which negated the need to escalate the matter. Operations personnel in the CDC Control Room were able to speak to the security guard on his return to the Gatehouse and instigated additional contact protocols to ensure there were no repeat occurrences that night.
The following morning, upon his arrival to site, the day security guard reset the Gatehouse radio base station which was still in alarm. The night security guard simply turned off the Gatehouse radio and turned down the volume on the Gatehouse radio base station to silence the audible alert, as he did not know how to reset it.

On the evening of 22nd July 2024, the same security guard once again set off the ‘Man Down’ radio alert and was given instruction on how to reset it by Killingholme operations personnel. However, at the start of the morning shift on 23rd July 2024, Killingholme operations personnel found the KPS Control Room radio base station in alert, so it would appear the security guard had triggered the alert again at some point during the night.

These are serious matters of concern, which highlight the security guard’s lack of understanding and discipline, repeatedly creating unnecessary work for numerous Uniper personnel.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The security guard has been instructed to take with him the Gatehouse site radio and security mobile phone each time he leaves the Gatehouse to perform a site tour. He has also been instructed several times on how to use the 'Man Down' feature on the site radios.
A meeting has been arranged on 14th August 2024 with his regional manager to ensure there are no more 'Man Down' incidents which are concerning and extremely disruptive to Uniper operations personnel.

TITLE: Poor electrical installation
CASE_DESCRIPTION: During commissioning work for the Ambient Air Injection project, the drawings supplied by Schneider for the two new HMC1172 6.6kV VCB control panels were found to be roughly 75% accurate. There was also a suspicion that the motor heaters were remaining live, despite the fuses being pulled from the circuit. Work was put together, to validate the drawings and produce an as built drawing. During this work, it was found that the outgoing heater connections for both the new 6.6kV motors had been linked together, and then fed from the next closest HMC panel with motor heater connections. This meant that, if any of the three panels heater fuses were in place, all three motor heater circuits would be live.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Link cables were removed from all three outgoing heater connections. Heater circuits for each panel were proved for correct operation.

TITLE: Fall off bicycle near storage rack area
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Whilst approaching the bike storage area, the cyclist rounded a corner and encountered two oncoming walkers on the path near the bike racks.  
In the process of slowing down/taking evasive action the cycle front wheel slipped and the cyclist lost control of the bike and fell to the ground. 
No injuries were sustained. 
Initial conclusion is that the sudden change of direction and braking caused the wheel to lose grip on the slimy/slippery paving slabs.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
As Integral FM personnel were present at the time of the incident, they advised that a task to clean the slippery concrete slab would be entered on the buildings job ticket system.
Cyclists/walkers have been aware of the hazard of the slippery slabs – but none had raised a ticket for cleaning.

TITLE: Crane contact with podium (platform)
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A podium (platform) was erected on top of the crane beam for an assessment of its suitability to be used as a working platform to remove redundant florescent light fitting. 

The crane was tested in the long travel direction to ensure there was no collision points, however, it was not tested in the cross-travel direction. At this point it was assumed that the cross travel would not come into contact with the podium as it was within the safety wires.

An individual used the crane in a cross-travel direction, at this point a section of the crab unit that protrudes beyond the safety wires came into contact with the podium.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Workshop crane isolated and podium made safe.  Appropriate Management team members informed.

TITLE: Paint spillage Tech Centre
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Paint was being removed from the COSHH cabinet in the Integral engineer area in the rig bay roof, to be relocated to the COSHH cabinet in the shed. 

We had made the decision to do this, following the issuance of the FRA and comments made concerning the rig bay roof. 

Office Essentials loaded the paints onto a rolling cage and took them to the goods lift, where they were moved to the ground floor and out of the external door into the carpark. 

As they moved the cage down the slope into the car park, the door came undone and a tin of paint fell onto the floor, the lid came off and a small amount of emulsion paint spilled onto the tarmac surface. 

This was highlighted to David Gray and Cassie Hall who cleaned up the spill with absorbent pads and blue roll from the spill kit. 

There was a thin residue left on the floor that could not be wiped up further with pads / wipes. 

David Gray decided to wash down the area with water to dilute what was left of the paint, after no more could be removed by the absorbent pads.

TITLE: Gas leak from faulty isolation valve
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Whilst carrying our flushing and greasing activities on Inlet Separator 10 inlet valve, there was an unexpected gas leak due to a faulty isolation valve. 

The capped screw has a drilled tell-tail to allow for any pressure behind to vent before the cap can be fully removed to prevent any potential injury due to build up of pressure.

As the cap was unscrewed, the pressure was released from the tell-tail and instead of it being a short sharp hiss, it was continuous indicating the fitting had failed.  It has a non-return valve and a ball valve but on this occasion both were passing. The same isolation valve was used yesterday with no issues.

TITLE: Ammonia dosing leak
CASE_DESCRIPTION: At 08:20, the Operations Team began preparing the Unit for start-up and entered the boiler house to conduct their routine pre-start checks. They discovered the ammonia dosing tank overflowing into the bund. The operator immediately inspected all valves supplying water or ammonia to the dosing tank, confirming they were closed. The outlet valve from the ammonia storage tank was closed but the leak continued. An attempt was made to close the demin water supply to the boiler house, but this valve was unfortunately seized open (a defect has been raised). The only remaining possibility was backflow from the LP drum dosing line, both discharge valves were closed, and eventually the leak stopped. When the discharge valve from the main storage tank was reopened, the leak did not return. The discharge valves on the LP drum dosing line remain closed. The leak was contained within the bund and caught early, resulting in only a small amount of fluid accumulating there.

•	Manway door by LP Int Blowdown Actuator does not look like it has been fitted properly and most of the nuts are hand tight or missing.

TITLE: PEM120 - GRA-61-MBM-10 - U6 EV COMBUSTOR
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During the U61 A07 Inspection the EV LHS split line insulation was found internally damaged during removal. This was first evidence of hot air leakage in this area. At this time Ansaldo and UTL supported an opportunity based reinspect and monitor strategy which was implemented.

Upon visual inspection during the U61 B03 Inspection the insulation was found further deteriorated in the local area. GE were now involved and they took images and feeler gauge measurements of the area. It measures 0.05mm gap across approx. 200mm length which confirmed the leakage path.

There is currently only localised signs of heat around the area, particularly on insulation blanket directly on top of the leak area. GT enclosure temperature is currently steady. Based on this the leakage is assumed to be minor currently. But the confirmation of leakage gap and length checks has initiated this exclusion zone assessment to manage any further deterioration.
