TITLE: Confined-space atmospheric hazard – CO alarm triggered; controlled evacuation of CQ U3 IP Drum
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During an internal inspection of the CQ Unit 3 HRSG IP drum  the entrants’ personal multi-gas monitor alarmed for elevated CO. 2 entrants were inside and the designated attendant (top-man) waited outside. Top-man immediately exercised stop-work authority, instructed a controlled evacuation, and managed the egress. From a safe position outside the vessel, the atmosphere was re-tested using the gas monitor on an extension probe to exclude instrument fault; readings confirmed elevated CO within the drum. The job was paused, the permit suspended, and the area isolated, with escalation to the Supervisor/HSSE.
Actual outcome: Near miss, no injury or illness.
Potential consequence: Asphyxiation/physiological effects due to CO displacement of O₂.
Immediate actions: Stop-work initiated; entrants evacuated; atmosphere verified; re-entry prohibited pending review of ventilation/purging and controls.
Preliminary factors for investigation: Effectiveness of purge/ventilation; possible CO ingress/accumulation pathway; confirmation of gas-monitor calibration and bump-test records.
Positive observation: The attendant’s prompt, calm response exemplified our Beyond Zero behaviours and prevented potential exposure.
HAZARD: Gases / Fumes / Vapours (Release of SOx, NOx, SF6, NH3, CH4, CO and CO2 into the atmosphere)

TITLE: Site Radios safety concern
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
There are significant safety concerns regarding the new site radios currently in use at Grain.

Issue Summary:

Dead Spots: There are areas across the site where radios fail to receive or transmit messages, leading to critical communication blackouts.

Encryption Hindrance: The newly introduced encryption has notably disrupted communication flow across the site. The additional delay and complexity—especially with the double-tap function—has led to repeated miscommunications, which could prove dangerous in emergency situations.

Man Down Feature Reliability: While we’ve seen a decrease in false alarms reaching the control room, this has come at the cost of reliability. During upcoming outages, the influx of contractors unfamiliar with the equipment will likely lead to increased spurious alarms and confusion.

Incident Simulation & Findings:

During a recent test of the “man down” function:

The CCR responded to the alarm by attempting contact via the emergency channel, which should have automatically connected. However, this communication was overridden by the radio’s repeating alarm signal.

The CCR received no indication from the base station that the message had failed.

Upon failure, the CCR attempted to reset the alarm via the base station. While it appeared to reset, the alarm remained active on the radio, creating a false impression that the situation was resolved.

No follow-up response was initiated, as the incident was mistakenly assumed to be a false alarm.

Safety Concern:

This exposes a critical flaw in both the communication and alarm systems. The man down function, in its current implementation, cannot be relied upon to trigger an appropriate emergency response. Furthermore, the system provides no clear feedback loop to confirm whether a situation is genuine or resolved.

Request for Action:

We strongly recommend the following actions:

Review and audit the coverage and communication integrity of the current radio system across site.

Evaluate the effectiveness of the man down feature—consider disabling it until it can reliably support life-critical incidents.

Provide clear training for all personnel and contractors on radio functionality and limitations.

Establish a failsafe protocol for verifying and responding to emergency alarms that includes manual confirmation.

The safety of personnel on-site depends on reliable communication. The current radio setup undermines this, and we urge a review before an incident highlights these flaws with serious consequences.

TITLE: Archaeological dig happening in the same field as the Uniper Cot Pipeline without Uniper being informed.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
An archaeological excavation was identified in a farmer's field near Stow by the Uniper aerial patrol on 14/07/2025. A Uniper engineer attended the site on 15/07/2025 to speak with the ground workers present.

The excavation is being conducted by CFA Archaeology. While the workers were aware of the presence of a Uniper asset in the area, they were unsure of its exact location. They believed this did not pose a risk due to the wide working boundaries from the pipeline.

The Uniper engineer advised that pipelines do not always follow a perfectly straight path between markers and emphasized the importance of accurately locating and marking the pipeline before any groundworks commence. This is considered best practice to ensure safety and prevent potential asset strikes.

TITLE: Emerson Product Safety Notice - MAL Drains Fasteners
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
IMPORTANT PRODUCT SAFETY NOTICE
Incorrect Fastener Plating Impacting High Temperature Applications
Shipment Date Range: September 2021 – December 2024

This Important Product Safety Notice (“Notice”) is to advise you that Sempell GmbH (“Sempell”) has confirmed that fasteners used in a limited quantity of valve assemblies and also sold as replacement parts did not meet Sempell plating requirements. The bolting supplier’s EN 10204 3.1 and 3.2 inspection certificates incorrectly stated the components were zinc-plated, however, it was recently discovered that cadmium-plating was used instead. If installed in a high temperature application, the cadmium-plating could cause the fastener to embrittle and fracture. The cadmium plating may also be transferred to components in direct contact with the fastener. IF OPERATED IN APPLICATION CONDITIONS THAT CAUSE THE BOLTING TO EXCEED 232°C (450°F), THE BOLTING COULD FRACTURE RESULTING IN PROCESS LEAKAGE, SERIOUS INJURY OR PROPERTY DAMAGE. TITLE: Non-Compliance with Respiratory Protective Equipment Requirements - GMI SHE 021
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
An initial review of our Compliance with GMI SHE 021 subsequent to a question being raised in regards to WSC Ammonia Dosing Procedure for Units 6 7 8 has been conducted by myself. 

Within the above GMI it highlights the requirement for RPE to be worn in accordance with the aforementioned procedure and the MSDS. It highlights a number of statutory requirements in regards to RPE:

Requires employers to provide and maintain suitable, CE/UKCA-marked RPE for employees exposed to hazards. 

Employers must conduct risk assessments to ensure RPE is adequate, carry out fit-testing for tight-fitting masks, train users on proper selection, use, and maintenance, and store equipment correctly

However, the following gaps have been identified via documentation review, discussion with staff and process review on our wider Respiratory Protective Equipment Compliance, which is a statutory bound duty under the PPE Regs & the COSHH Regs :

There is currently no reference to RPE Within our Skills Matrix – thereby no face fit testing or  practical general training on how to wear RPE. Nor, how to maintain RPE

No Face Fit Testing Conducted in 5 years (It is required by the RPE ACOP to be conducted every 2 years)

RPE not officially inspected in the past 5 years (Should be inspected on a monthly basis) PM hasn't been completed since March 2020 

Inappropriate storage of RPE / Filters – filters are all out of date

Individuals whom have not been face fit tested have conducted tasks requiring RPE to be worn
HAZARD: Toxic substance or CMR substance (carcinogenic, mutagenic, reproduction toxic)

From these findings Chloride working party instructed not to use out of date equipment on site.

TITLE: Manifold left in wrong state
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During commissioning activities the GT failed to come online due to a manifold for a pressure transmitter being left in the wrong state following calibration.

The GT sequencer test opens the gas SOV valve (GRA-71-MBP-43-AA003) and looks for a pressure spike on the outlet pressure transmitter (GRA-71-MBP-43-CP001) before reopening the SOV. The pressure transmitter's manifold was left with the isolator shut and the vent open post calibration, due to this the sequencer did not see the pressure spike and therefore did not reopen the SOV.

TITLE: Unsafe and unapproved electrical installation found on Safety walk.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During the HESAC inspection of the Fuel Oil Compound today, a member of the electrical team noticed a damaged 110v extension plug & socket on the floor. He followed the cable back to where he assumed it would be plugged in, and noticed that it went through a hole in the wall of the old Mill Workshop. 

The cable was then strewn between several fuseboards and terminated directly into the 110v fuseboard by the roller shutter door. It was noticed that the live (brown) wire was terminated into the fused neutral busbar and the neutral wire (blue) was terminated into the fused live busbar. The opposite end of the extension lead was left with a plug hanging over a cable tray at the top of the bund access stairs and dangling, submerged into oily water.

The fuses were removed and caution notices applied to make the extension lead electrically safe, before removing the plug from the water.

The extension lead will be planned to be removed fully from the supply, then disposed of accordingly.

TITLE: PEM120 - GRA-61-MBH-30-AC001 - U6 GT LP ONCE THROUGH COOLER
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Unit 61 had B Inspection scope carried out as per TIL2469R2 recommendation. The PAUT of Weld AIJ3 detected low amplitude embedded indication close to the bore with a 2 mm cross-section and 548 mm long. PEM120 access control protocols for Unit 71 LP OTC are extended to Unit 61 prior to return to service. The Unit 61 Weld AIJ3 should be re-inspected after no more than 4,000 hours or 90 starts, whichever is sooner, following return to service from the August 2025 outage. At that time, it would be prudent to re-inspect Welds AOJ2 and AOJ3 to confirm the stability of the defects detected in these welds.
U61 Indication detail:
• AIJ3 (Alloy 800 to P11 transition weld): FDPI – no recordable indications. PAUT detected low amplitude embedded indication close to the bore (probably bore emergent) with a 2 mm cross-section and 548 mm long, observed previously during the 2024 monitoring exercise, but now recordable due to a higher amplitude response.
• AOJ2 (P11 to Alloy 800 transition weld): FDPI - 4-off surface breaking intermittent circumferential weld defects detected. PAUT detected a 2.5 mm deep surface breaking response close to P11 fusion boundary intermittent full circ. NB: no defects detected during previous monitoring of this weld.
• AOJ3 (Alloy 800 to 304 SS transition weld): FDPI - 4-off surface breaking intermittent circumferential weld defects detected during FDPI. PAUT detected a 2 mm deep embedded response close to the 304 fusion boundary with a 2 mm cross-section intermittent fully circ. & located 3 mm below the external surface. NB: no defects detected during previous monitoring of this weld.
General - Unencrypted
Surface replicas have been obtained from the surface breaking defects detected during the FDPI of Welds AOJ2 and AOJ3. These defects were located wholly in the weld metal and appeared to be intergranular and are probably fabrication flaws, associated with shrinkage, due to micro-segregation during welding. The PAUT responses detected on Welds AOJ2 and AOJ3 were not entirely consistent with the FDPI report and it is also not understood why these flaws were not detected during the previous inspection of these welds last year. Currently, it is considered that these flaws are unlikely to developing in-service.
For Weld AIJ3, the location of the flaw, and the increasing amplitude response, is consistent with the initiation of creep cracking we believe to be responsible for the failure at Keppel and it is in a similar position to the defects we are monitoring in the equivalent welds on both Units 71 and 81.

TITLE: Environmental kiosk/ purge issue
CASE_DESCRIPTION:

TITLE: Shortcomings in general safety management found during task audit.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A task inspection on civil works highlighted a number of shortcomings:

1. **RA225 Compliance**: It was noted that RA225 was not adhered to during the operations. This issue has already been discussed with the working party.

2. **PPE Concerns**: One member of the working party was seen wearing short-sleeved work wear. Long-sleeved work wear has since been obtained to address this.

3. **Glove Standards**: The working party was not aware of the minimum glove standards required for the tasks at hand. This has been explained to them.

4. **Lifting Area Safety**: It is recommended that the lifting area be improved with brick guards.

4. **Lifting Equipment**: A general-purpose builder’s bucket was used as a lifting attachment to transport mix from ground level to the plinth over the guard rail using a gin wheel. This practice should be reviewed. And was not covered in the RAMS

5. **Tool Safety**: The use of a fixed blade knife to trim expanding foam was not included in the risk assessment. This point needs to be addressed to ensure compliance.

6. **Circular Saw Assessment**: I advise that the use of a circular saw be specifically assessed in the RAMS rather than a general guideline such as "only choose the correct tool for the task."

TITLE: Loss of DCS readings and control
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
At 02:23, a series of I&C alarms appeared on the DCS alarm page. Almost immediately, all DCS values were lost, signals turned bad, and no changes could be made, resulting in a complete loss of Unit control. This lasted approximately two minutes and at this time the Unit was operating at full load. Because we were unable to adjust the load, the unit was declared inflexible and SEL to MEL.
Once control was restored, a decision was made to deload the Unit to SEL and maintain its inflexible status until further guidance was received. The Production Day Team Leader and ROM's were contacted for support. Although the ROMs couldn’t access the system remotely, they provided assistance over the phone. Despite their efforts to diagnose the issue, they were unable to identify a cause, or determine if the issue might reoccur.
As a precaution, the decision was made to keep the unit inflexible at SEL until Engineering/ROM's could complete a thorough investigation.

TITLE: Oil loss
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Whilst walking through turbine hall 3 I noticed oil on top of the PT lub oil tank ('B' end) and some on the floor. I immediately put down absorbent pads and proceeded to mop up the oil. I also noticed that one of the vent cocks on the 'Auto-clean' package was not in the correct position so I put this right. After cleaning up the oil I started each lub oil pump in turn to try and identify where the oil loss was coming from. Whilst testing one of the lub oil pumps I cracked open one of the vent cocks to see if oil could come out whilst in the position I had initially found it, and yes oil did come out. After test running all three lub oil pumps I found no oil leaks evident.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Oil was mopped up and instant investigations started to find where the leak came from. When no leaks were found when the lub oil pumps were test run the conclusion was that the vent cock got inadvertently knocked open when a greasing operation was performed earlier in the day, the unit was shut down at this time. 
In the afternoon a test run on the unit was performed which switched on the lub oil pump hence oil came out of the vent cock.
The open pipes under the vent cocks have now been removed and plugs have been inserted to prevent future reoccurrence.

TITLE: Level instrument failure
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Level instrument failed during a nomination; GDU30 EB30ZL002. Not reading correctly, on investigation was reset and appeared to work correctly. As a precaution taken out of service until further testing can be completed.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Trip defeat has been put in place whilst a wet test on the instrument is planned in.

Work to wet check the level instrument EKB30ZL002 was carried out on Friday 27th November.

The level instrument is located in the upper part of Contactor 30’s KO pot and always reads 0mm.

A defeat was put in where a value of 4mA (0mm) was simulated to the DCS to enable the plant to be reset and run again. (At the time of putting the defeat in the level reading was full scale).

When, as part of venting the stillwell, removed the bottom blank flange (to which the test flange was to be bolted), observed foam dropping out, which would provide a false reading. The foam would inevitably appear as an obstacle in the way of the radar beam.

The wet test was then carried out by filling the stillwell in 25% increments to from 0 % to 100% (0-600mm) and then emptying it down to 25% also in 25% increments, where it was left for 1 ½ hours. On returning the level instrument remained at 25%. Proving a successful test.

The foaming is caused by TEG in the system and is often observed when venting down to atmospheric pressure, it is not believed to be a cause of the issue but a result of the test. Historically have investigated spiking issues on level transmitters elsewhere on plant and whether this is due to foaming, several actions were taken that didn't mitigate the spiking issue, in the end the transmitter was replaced.

So a spare has been ordered and this will be monitored closely.
text_features: Level instrument failure. Level instrument failed during a nomination; GDU30 EB30ZL002. Not reading correctly, on investigation was reset and appeared to work correctly. As a precaution taken out of service until further testing can be completed.

TITLE: Failure of Compressor Variable Speed Drive DC-link power capacitor
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Suffered a second drive failure on Gas Compressor 10. First occurred in December 2018 (synergi case no: 2661)

On investigation it was determined that the fault was again attributed to a fault 0.33µf snubber capacitor as per the initiating event on Compressor 20 only this time on an IGBT as opposed to a clamping diode. 

The capacitor in question was C1 on -G013A7 - MC2 IEGT Stack Phase W.

The drive didn’t trip and there were no signs of any further damage. The site fire & gas system detected smoke/heat and tripped the drive.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Investigation of the cause is on-going with the OEM, GE.  The failure occurred in a room with strictly controlled access.  The equipment has been electrically isolated.  Additional controls have been put in place to bar all access to the variable speed drive rooms of the other compressors.

TITLE: CNC Lathe chuck opening
CASE_DESCRIPTION:

IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: A physical barrier denying entry to none machine operators, is to be erected around the machine as a immediate precaution. A long term engineering solution has to be sought to remove the possibility of accidentally operating the chuck release foot pedals

TITLE: Transferring - Offshore wind turbine
CASE_DESCRIPTION: A Trainer was attending a customer site to complete apprentice observations. He arrived at site on 22nd September and completed a successful transfer to and from the wind turbine. The following day the waves were high and RWE were in a position where they were deciding whether or not to go off shore. A decision was made to go ahead. Later in the day the team at RWE were told they had to leave the turbine within an hour and a half because the waves were getting high. The team transferred and all made it back to site safely however, Jonathan has described it as a frightening experience. RWE state safe wave height should be 2.8m but the waves on this day were over 3m. When they returned to site all RWE staff were asked to complete near hits so that they could investigate the reasons someone had authorised transfer to the wind turbine that day. As the Trainer was part of the group on site and for his own safety we wanted to raise this as a near hit within Uniper too.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: I have spoken to the Trainer who has confirmed that he's OK now. The experience was frightening but it hasn't put him off wanting to assess wind apprentices. I've informed him that I would be putting this near hit together, have spoken to Steve Gilmore and have informed him that he may receive a call from H&S.

TITLE: 20% Caustic leak
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During routine inspections of plant equipment a shift technician noticed a small amount of 20% caustic on the floor (within a large metal storage container). The leak was on a small caustic dosing pump arrangement where 20% caustic from a 25 ltr drum is used to neutralise condensate drain water from a package boiler.

Upon inspection a plastic spigot that holds a flexible return pipe to the pump unit had failed, allowing a small amount of caustic to be released. Most caustic had run down the outside of the flexible hose into the container the 25 ltr caustic drum sits in. A small amount of caustic that had dropped onto the floor of the container was cleaned up by the shift technician.

There was a scaffold in the container at the time and as there was potential for caustic to be under the feet of the scaffold tubes the scaffolders were informed and made to wear PPE  to protect them from residual that the shift technician could not reach to clean. All scaffolding was washed down and PPE disposed of correctly. The floor was once again cleaned after scaffold removal.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The spigot was replaced with a spare and the other units on site were inspected for defects with none found. As there was scaffolding recently erected there may have been some unintentional damage that occurred during erection.

text_features:
20% Caustic leak. During routine inspections of plant equipment a shift technician noticed a small amount of 20% caustic on the floor (within a large metal storage container). The leak was on a small caustic dosing pump arrangement where 20% caustic from a 25 ltr drum is used to neutralise condensate drain water from a package boiler.

Upon inspection a plastic spigot that holds a flexible return pipe to the pump unit had failed, allowing a small amount of caustic to be released. Most caustic had run down the outside of the flexible hose into the container the 25 ltr caustic drum sits in. A small amount of caustic that had dropped onto the floor of the container was cleaned up by the shift technician.

There was a scaffold in the container at the time and as there was potential for caustic to be under the feet of the scaffold tubes the scaffolders were informed and made to wear PPE  to protect them from residual that the shift technician could not reach to clean. All scaffolding was washed down and PPE disposed of correctly. The floor was once again cleaned after scaffold removal.

TITLE: Piece of debris in person's eye.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Person received injury through getting debris in their right eye whilst working in the HRSG top dead space. The IP was wearing safety glasses but strong winds were causing a draft within the boiler house and boiler internals
The IP cleaned his eye using the Boiler House emergency shower eye wash. This alerted the control room via a DCS alarm.
On investigation the IP claimed their eye felt like the debris could still be in it.  
They were escorted to the First Aid Room and treated by a CDC first aider who washed out the eye to remove the debris.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The incident occurred at 14:30. All work was suspended in the HRSG top dead space and the issue discussed in the 15:00 CDM meeting. Actions from the meeting were to;
Close the HRSG Rain Damper - This reduced the draft blowing through the top dead space allowing work to continue. 
Close the external doors to the HRSG building - This again reduced the airflow through the building and the boiler
Use googles in exposed/windy area's

The IP's right eye was examined by a First Aider at the first aid room, there was a some dust found behind the lower lid in the right hand corner of the eye which was removed. There was a red mark/scratch running vertically down behind the upper lid. The eye was thoroughly irrigated using eye wash solution. The IP reported that it felt better. They were advised that should the eye become inflamed or irritated they should have it examined at their local hospital. The IP then returned to work for the remainder of the shift. They reported for work the following morning, their Supervisor checked in with them reporting the eye felt much better and had not needed any further treatment.

Communications had with the JCB operative about the proximity of Our Gas Pipeline to there excavation site.

Communications made with their management, They sent us copy of there RAMS and Drawings, Previous Linsearches had given Orsted ( Hornsea wind 2), our pipeline route,
I concluded that the were carrying out the Excavation safely, and that they were fully aware of our pipeline location, and I informed the JCB operative to continue the work.

I reiterated to there management that they MUST inform us of excavation work which is ongoing in the same field as our pipeline, even though they are away from our easement, as it is UNIPER's responsibility to ensure that their work-scope can't affect our asset.

TITLE: Boiler level switch faulty
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Heating medium boiler 10 was taken off line and drained for an upgrade project. As part of the recommissioning process, it was noted that the level switch was displaying as healthy, when the boiler had been completely drained down for the duration of the works.

The level switch exists to provide protection against low water level in the boiler and would trip the burner management system if a low water level is detected. It is part of the safety chain on the boilers which consists of the following; 3 pressure switches; 2 high, one low, 3 high temperature switches and the level switch.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
A proof test was carried out by pushing down the manual test plunger and it was found to be very stiff. Upon dismantling the level switch a circlip at the top of the float assembly had failed completely allowing the magnet to remain in the healthy position (through possible build up of corrosion). This prevented the magnet from being able to drop with the float assembly and activate the low level trip switch. 

Circlip was replaced, and corresponding level switch on boilers 20 and 30 checked. Same issue was identified on boiler 30, so the circlip has been replaced. Boiler 20 passed its test, but will be take out of service and checked as a precaution.

TITLE: Spare gas regulator failed upon fitting
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The glycol regeneration units have a an integrated regulator/slam shut valve on the Natural gas line to the combustion chamber. The slam shut valve had activated twice so the unit was made unavailable by the shift team. A site engineer and mechanical shift technician inspected the unit and were unable to set up the regulator correctly to stop the slam shut activating. 

A spare was in stores so the unit was changed out. The new unit was tested and the engineer and shift tech were unable to set up the unit to factory specifications. The original regulator & slam shut was re-installed and the regeneration unit left as a poor spare. Wales & West were called in to investigate.

On 24.1.20 Wales and West attended site and repaired the original regulator that was fitted. 

They also attempted to set up the spare unit but failed. The unit was stripped down and a port that had been drilled out at the factory was found to be blocked with possible swarf; the internal measuring line on the attached diagram. The hole will be re-drilled by a technician.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The spare has been removed from the stores until it has been cleared and tested as fit for duty.

Having competent persons fitting and testing the equipment meant we did not leave the equipment in an unsafe condition.

The blockage in the port (internal measuring line) could not be seen but it does highlight the importance of checking equipment before fitting, even when the equipment is brand new.

TITLE: PSNH - Ammonia level transmitters
CASE_DESCRIPTION:

One BPCS level transmitter HSJ01CL022 was found not to be indicating during the ammonia delivery and hence this signal
was deselected. The ammonia delivery continued using the second BPCS tank level transmitter. 
On completion of the ammonia delivery the tank level SIS overrides were removed, which resulted in an ammonia plant trip. 
On investigation it was discovered that all three SIS level transmitters, HSJ01CL004/005 & 018, had low level signals standing. The issue with all level transmitters was subsequently resolved on 29/01/20.

TITLE: HTA Top pass condenser flushing causing contamination.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Harm to asset via chloride pitting at GLNG SCVs (submerged combustion vaporisers.   
Top pass of U6 condenser only operationally flushed 'once' as auto sequence looking at conductivity meter and after column.  Then allowed seawater contamination into the HTA demin water circuit.  It was found that the conductivity meter 'cooler' had a leak therefore, the conductivity meter was looking at the wrong source of water for the flushing sequence.  The chloride that was found in the system is double the chemistry spec.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
1. Shift Team Leader questioned the Top pass flushing sequence.  It usually takes 'two flushes'.
2. Chemist sampled and analysed.  Found chloride over the spec limit for HTA.
3. Purging the system to decrease the chloride.  Exec informed and Day Shift Team Leader.
4. GLNG informed on behalf of Exec at Grain and advised for part drain and refill of SCVs as far as operationally possible.
5.Chemist re-sampled after 16 hours, slight decrease of chloride, but not within limits yet. Plan of sampling and analysing each day until back into spec.  Purge Forms to GLNG each day until system back in spec.  Exec do not wish for plant to be off line for draining and refilling as trading income costs issue.   
6. Defected via SAP the cooler.
7. Defected via SAP the 2 flushes of condenser as a minimum and then the auto sequence looks at the conductivity meter and after column  (PEM109 in the interim of mod).

TITLE: Overhead 5t crane failure to respond to stop signal sent from the remote control unit

During the removal of the drive plate from a rotor, using the high bay 5 t crane, the banksman indicated to the operator to stop. The crane was immediately taken out of service and placed in quarantine.

TITLE: Fuel gas flow signal failure
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Fuel gas flow signal channel fault/failure caused main gas slam shut valve to protection close which consequentially caused a protection trip of the Gas Turbine due to fuel gas pressure less than minimum. Station was de-loading at the time following PN plan profile and was generating circa 280mw at the time of unit trip.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Interrogated DCS and observed fuel gas pressure signal channel fault alarm occurred, followed 14 seconds later by fuel gas pressure less than minimum alarm (due to slam shut valve operating in P.R.S compound. Gas turbine trip followed immediately after. Pipelines on call engineer contacted, who attended site and established that failure of a U.P.S power supply unit had caused loss of 24v DC control supply to the control system, causing the loss of flow signal. Power was restored from an alternative source and gas system visually checked and restored to operational condition.

TITLE: Incorrect paper work detailing type of radioactive NDT source planned to be used on weld testing
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
NDT/Radiography has been completed on a number of shifts – the process involves completing the Appendix A documentation which details important information – one being the source type and size – the source decay certificate also states type and current size – the Appendix A is prepared by the FieldCore Mechanical contractor along with the decay certificate – this is checked/signed by the Uniper Engineer and distributed to relevant parties nominated on the Appendix A – the source nominated was Iridium - Ir192 23.7.
Iris the NDT company arrived at Enfield Power station at approx. 02:00 – after a review the Shift team leader found the source was a Selenium 75 Source with a strength of 32.8 Curies. (>20Curies) – The shift team leader has been on Nights since Wednesday, I was confident in the competence of the IRIS Engineers and decided this was admin error and not that IRIS had bought the wrong Source.
Once IRIS showed the shift team leader all the necessary paperwork for the Source, he allowed the Radiography to continue.
The fact that IRIS told him during the Saturday morning testing, that they were bringing a stronger Selenium Source for Sunday’s testing, was also taken in to account.
HAZARD: Exposure to an ionising radioactive source
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Review of Iris contractor competence - review of correct paper work - work allowed to continue

It is highly likely that this unit fell from its fixings some time ago and has not been identified due to its inaccessible nature (this fitting is not on any designated walkways etc.). The production team was alerted to the light fitting fall when investigating another 'non related' issue.
Although categorised as Personal Injury it is highly unlikely that this particular incident would have caused injury to persons.

TITLE: Transport of IGA Pressure Reduction Skid
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
AN IGA pressure reduction skid was being transported from the Gas Reception Centre at Killingholme to the PRS at CDC.  After travelling approx. 400m along the public road immediately outside of Killingholme Power Station, one end of a section of pipework on the left hand side of the trailer became detached from the skid hitting the road.  The driver immediately slowed and stopped in a safe location.
There were no injuries as a result of this incident.
The package of works to remove the skid and re-install it at the PRS had been contracted out  to Doosan.  As such they will be conducting the investigation in to the incident.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The lorry had a HIAB and so the driver deployed the stabilisers as a precautionary measure.  The trailer was partially blocking one side of the carriage way so vehicles with orange flashing lights were stationed to warn on coming traffic of the hazard.
The local council and then the police were contacted to enable a road closure to be put in place.  The crane company who conducted the lift at the Gas Reception Centre were contacted, they reviewed the situation, produced a lift plan and carried out the lifts allowing the load to be moved to a safe location.

TITLE: Discovery of Asbestos in SWPH No.2
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Whilst working on the preparation for blocking off of above ground apertures to SWPH No. 2 by our Estate Lockdown works Contractor Access Direct Site Services (ADSS), Operatives were breaking out mortar / putty to the apertures in readiness to be blocked up with air bricks. 

Notification was received by phone at 14:54 by Mark Carr (ADSS site manager) and John Dempsey attended site shortly after 3pm. MC raised concern over two locations with which there were potential ACM concerns, the SWPH No.2 and along the 11kV route south of Damhead Creek where suspicious material was observed underfoot.  

It was agreed that sampling would be organised and ADSS were to stand down and work elsewhere. Sampling was undertaken and the analysis report was received on Friday 6th at 11:58.  Two samples from SWPH No.2 were identified as positive and the four taken along the 11kV route were identified as negative.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: All work to area stood down.  Notifications made to Grain / Phoenix Team.  Requested Contractor to attend site and provide quote for removal at earliest opportunity.  Sampling to be arranged to SWPH No.1 as constructed at the same time to similar design.  Impact on ADSS Estate Lockdown works programme to be assessed.

TITLE: Unit 7 Safety Valve Lifting unintentionally
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
U7 Steam Turbine was tripped using the CCR Emergency Stop Button as per the recommissioning programme for the HP bypass works.
The HP bypass opened satisfactorily but the IP bypass tripped almost immediately after opening, it tripped on Condenser Inlet temperature >Max 2; the spraywater valve for the IP bypass failed to quench the steam temperature in sufficient time. The Operator was unable to reset the temperature trip and therefore was unable to reinstate the IP bypass valve.
Subsequently, the CRH / IP systems pressurised causing the safety valves to lift.
Owing to the IP bypass trip, the GT PLS(T), leading to desynch at 03:04hrs. The HP header pressure increased due to the GT EV burners remaining in service for cooldown. Turning Gear was selected but the fires remained in service. The HP system safety valves lifted @155barg, the GT ESB was pressed at the CCR to extinguish the burners and reduce the HP pressure.

The IP bypass spray valve was later investigated by the maintenance team, I'm not sure what was found and if any changes to the control system were made.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: See Case description above

TITLE: Excavation above 33kV feeders
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Site were contacted by Inovyn to assist with the positive identification of both of our 33kV feeders.

They had already undertaken some identification work and had identified one feeder. They were picking up both feeders on the power setting of their scanner but when applying a fixed frequency tone they could only identify the one feeder. 

On meeting Inovyn at the agreed site just off Hulse Lane it was clear that works had already taken place directly over our feeders. Six large fence posts had been driven into the ground in between feeder 1 & 2 to a depth of 450mm.

Inovyn explained that an Inovyn excavation permit was in place and the original intended method of work was to drive the fence posts in to a depth of 1200mm. After scanning by Inovyn that initial depth had reduced to 450mm.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The site was visited for a second time with Uniper HSSE manager and at this point the working party had returned and were continuing to install further fence posts using a hydraulic post driver. They were asked that no further fence posts were installed in the corridor containing our feeders until the situation could be clarified. 

Inovyn team who deal with excavation permits were contacted. Agreed that the process appeared not to have been followed.

Inovyn should have made Uniper aware of the intended works so that our own safe system of work could be enacted and employ appropriate controls as required.

This area of land also contains a competitor's 33KV feeders in an adjacent corridor. They had not been contacted at all concerning the work over their feeders as Inovyn did not have any contact details for them. Uniper have also made them aware.

An investigation will be launched by Inovyn which we will attend.

TITLE: Power loss to site
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The gas processing plant suffered from total power loss, which caused the uninterruptable power supply to start. Site was in compression injection mode at the time and was in the process of bringing on a third compressor. 

The issue was caused by a faulty protection relay on feeder 2, this did not take the site offline as feeder 1 was still operational. However when the third compressor was being bought online the demand exceeded the current settings and an undetected latent fault on voltage transformer (blown fuse) of feeder 1 caused it to trip, leading to a power failure at site.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: The UPS operated as it should but there were some issues identified with some systems not operating as expected such as the GPP access system, and there was no return to service procedure / checklist for responding to a power outage.

TITLE: SSoW - U4 pneumatic bled steam to DA valve 4002 permit for work ROMP
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On Sunday 23rd May 2021, a Competent person (CP) collected a safety document PFW ROMP (Restoration Of Motive Power) to work on bled steam to de-aerator valve 4002.   Following collection of the safety document, the CP proceeded to the point of work he knew as 4002 valve, but found that the safety key issued with the PFW ROMP did not match the isolation lock on the valve, and there wasn't a ROMP notice present.  
The CP contacted the duty Senior Authorised Person (SAP) immediately to report his findings.  The SAP attended the point of work and found the CP on what he believed to be the wrong valve.  The CP confirmed through his experience and knowledge that he believed he was on 4002 valve, and showed the SAP a handwritten sign on the pneumatic valve control box (approximately 12ft away from the valve it's self) stating it was valve 4002.  The duty SAP took the CP to the valve that was isolated for the ROMP, and showed him the local permanent plant ID label attached to the valve stating valve 4002.  After some discussion and consulting drawings, it was still not 100% clear which valve was 4002.  The Duty SAP cancelled the PFW ROMP and de-isolated both 4001 & 4002 valves, and asked a Unit Operator to operate the valves remotely from the ovation soft desk in the main control room.  On operation of the valves it was confirmed that the permanent plant ID label attached to U4 4002 valve was incorrect, and that the valve was actually 4001.  

After confirming that the identification on valve 4001 (stating 4002) was wrong, 4002 valve was inspected and there was no plant label attached to 4002 valve, apart from the hand written sign on the pneumatic control box which is not local to the valve. 

U4 is currently on an Interim outage, and the air supply valves for both 4001 and 4002 were isolated at the start of the outage period (approx. 2 weeks earlier).  Both valves have been worked on through the outage with 4002 requiring setting up under a PFW ROMP before being returned to service.

Information

Both 4001 and 4002 pneumatic bled steam valves are located on U4 De-aerator.  On Unit 4, 4001 valve is located on the 'B' side of the De-aerator, 4002 is located on the 'A' side.  The valves are approximately 10 meters apart, each on it's own platform.  The valves are the opposite way round on U1 & U2 compared to U3 & U4.
HAZARD: Contact with hot liquids or gases
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Wrong labelling removed from item of plant and replaced with temporary labels stating correct description.  Other units checked for ID and discrepancies corrected.

TITLE: Loss of process control resulting in plant trip
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Whilst withdrawing gas from the caverns and changing load from 700,000Sm3/hr to 900,000Sm3/hr by the pressure reduction valves (PRV’s) the plant suffered an unexpected Safety Instrumented System (SIS) trip on rate of change (falling <1bar/min) on the pipeline to the National transmission system (NTS).

In 2011 similar issues were experienced when certain plant conditions were met (approx. 8 bar dp between caverns and the National Transmission System [NTS] system). To prevent this from occurring a Management of Change (MoC) was implemented that allowed the shift operator control of the plant 'global gain'. This global gain effectively slows the plant control system down to prevent these large flow variances happening quickly and thus preventing demands on the SIS system. There is a standing operational instruction for the shift operator to manually change the global gain from 1 to 0.7 when in these pressure ranges.

On this occasion the operator had not reduced the global gain as when the withdrawal nomination commenced the conditions for the global gain to be reduced were not met, however, as these conditions are dynamic as the withdrawal nomination continued the conditions were met but the global gain was not adjusted.

Upon investigation of the DCS trend it appears this has been happening (to a lesser extent) for the past 16 months. This ties in with a rolling programme of overhauling each PRV, of which we have 3 off. It is thought that splitting the flow across two valves instead of three may have contributed to the issues described.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
The plant was reset and the nomination re-started with the global gain set to 0.7. The operators have been reminded of the importance of periodically checking the pressures and adjusting the global gain as necessary. 

An MoC will be raised to automate the process of the global when the correct plant process parameters are met and this shall be completed as a matter of priority. This will help remove the human error potential.

During the investigation issue was raised whether an MoC for the programme of overhauling the PRV’s should have been completed. Although the design flows have not been exceeded through each valve a material change has been made to the amount of equipment used to control the process. 

Discussion was held around what constitutes normal/abnormal maintenance and when an MoC should be raised, also whether an MoC would have identified this as a potential risk. 

This will be taken to the next process safety committee meeting for further discussion and formal agreement as when an MoC is required if removing a piece of equipment for maintenance.

TITLE: Uncontrolled Release of steam via safety valve.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
It appears that U6 Sequencers (HRSG/WSC and ST) stopped running(Disabled themselves) when restarting the unit from an SSD trip during unit start-up. 
It was not noticed that the sequencers were not running initially (no alarms) until the operator realised that the HP bypass had failed to open. Immediately the HP by-pass was manually switched on which resulted in the HP-pass opening to pressurise the cold re-heat line as designed. This had the result of pressurising the CRH line due to high pressure already in the HP steam line. this consequently led to the CRH safety valves lifting at their designed lift pressures. 
Just after the HP-bypass had been switched on it was then noticed that the HRSG/WSC and ST sequencers were not running, these were immediately re-started. Once the condenser vacuum had reached 300mbar, the CRH pressure was able to relieve to the condenser via the IP by-pass valve. The unit the ran up as designed.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: There is a requirement to ascertain as to why the sequencers failed to switch on after the initial SSD trip.
text_features:
Uncontrolled Release of steam via safety valve.. It appears that U6 Sequencers (HRSG/WSC and ST) stopped running(Disabled themselves) when restarting the unit from an SSD trip during unit start-up. 
It was not noticed that the sequencers were not running initially (no alarms) until the operator realised that the HP bypass had failed to open. Immediately the HP by-pass was manually switched on which resulted in the HP-pass opening to pressurise the cold re-heat line as designed. This had the result of pressurising the CRH line due to high pressure already in the HP steam line. this consequently led to the CRH safety valves lifting at their designed lift pressures. 
Just after the HP-bypass had been switched on it was then noticed that the HRSG/WSC and ST sequencers were not running, these were immediately re-started. - Further cleaning of residual in bund planned.
- Operation team to monitor drains and straw bails for signs of oil.
- All fuel oil heater works stopped.

TITLE: Faulty Hertz Hire Car - Again
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On Starting my journey to site, within half a mile of my journey start, a low tyre pressure warning light appeared on the dashboard display. I stopped the vehicle and checked the tyre to see if it was noticeably deflated. It was not. I reset the monitor and continued on the journey. 
I reported to Hertz at approx. 08:30, I stopped at the motorway services, checked the tyre again and contacted Hertz when their office was open that I suspected that the hire car had been supplied with a slow puncture. I also reported unrecorded rain damage to the door cards, door handles and dash boards.
I contacted the Uniper Central Support team to record this report of pre-existing damage.
When I arrived at site, I followed up the initial report with an email with photo's of the water damage.

Complaints were registered with Hertz 

On Wednesday morning, I started my journey from hotel to site and the same tyre pressure warning appeared. this time when the tyre was inspected a clear depletion of the tyre pressure was visible.

TITLE: Failure to adhere to PEM-225 High Temperature Threaded Fasteners
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Following a confirmed leak on the new ISDH spraybar flange joint U81 was brought offline for opportunity corrective maintenance. During disassembly of the flange assembly one of the fasteners 'picked up' resulting in having to be cut in order to break the flange and complete removal of the flexitallic gasket. A new joint had been reserved against the SAP MO and was free issued from the stores but there had been no requirement for spare bolting identified. On rebuild of the flange assembly standard stainless steel studding was used to replace the fastener that had previously been cut as opposed to T41 grade stainless suitable for high temperature applications
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: PEM-120 Temporary Exclusion zone remains in place. Replacement T41 studding has been procured and has been planned to be exchanged at the next earliest opportunity.

TITLE: When is a Zebra Crossing not a Zebra Crossing
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
There are two 'zebra crossings' marked on the approach road to UTG. Whilst one is associated with signage and orange beacons, the other comprises just the back and white road markings. This means that the pedestrian feels they have the right of way, but their safety is reliant upon drivers noting the road markings.

This was raised as an issue some 18 months ago and nothing appears to have progressed. I would suggest removing the makings, but keeping the drop kerb, In this way, the pedestrian knows to remain alert when crossing.

TITLE: Unsecure pallet load
CASE_DESCRIPTION: unloading 3 pallets (from James Walker) off a TNT articulated lorry just before 2pm today. The TNT drivers were using their pump truck to get the pallets to the rear of their vehicle so Kev could unload and place them in the workshop. The 2nd pallet was already in a broken state but the black shrink wrap was intact. As Kev reversed from the vehicle (with the load at height) the pallet started to tip sideways and fell to the ground. It transpired the pallet had been packed, in my opinion, quite dangerously as all the heavy nuts and bolts had been placed at the very top of the pallet. These had shifted during transit which caused the pallet to become unstable.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: A bag of nuts, bolts & washers split and a couple of plastic tool cases were smashed but the contents appear fine. We have placed all the loose items with the pallets in the workshop and swept up the mess; Gary Wilme has been made aware too as he raised the PR.

TITLE:
SSoW
Safety document not collected from Permit Office
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Contractor carried out inspection work to the intrusion tube to Unit 1 A inlet dust analyser
HAZARD: Exposure to gases, fumes and vapours
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
This incident was brought to the attention of C&I engineering 24 hours post work completion (5/8/20). No immediate actions were taken as engineer was not aware at that time that the permit had not been picked up. 

CEMS contractor did not follow own method statement which clearly states on line 1 of the pre start check that "ensure Permit to work or Limited Work Permit is in place and understood" 

Following a post incident interview the contractor stated that he was not told a permit was required although had signed on to the GSAF document declaring he understood the content of work order card and RAMS.

The engineer responsible for the work was working from home that day and had delegated the supervision of the work to another member of the C&I team. 

The job had been discussed by the engineer in charge of the work with the contractor two days prior to visit although the permit was not discussed specifically the engineer assumed the contactor would carry out the same work as they had 3 week previously on unit three, same individual was involved on both jobs. 

The main cause of the incident was the contractor being in an alpha state whilst carrying out routine work which led to the RAMS being read incorrectly. This could have been avoided by better handover between the two engineers in the C&I team, which would have resulted in a more thorough review of the safety requirements required for the work to be carried out. 

An underlying influencing factor that the responsible engineer was working from home due to Covid-19 implications (child care issues).

TITLE: Leak from pressure gauge vent valve
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Whilst conducting maintenance at Wellhead H406 a slight gas leak was detected coming from the direction of a pressure gauge (photos attached) which is located on the horizontal pipework between the master and the wing valve. This was clarified by the reading on the technicians personal gas monitor increasing in that location. 

On closer inspection it was found the vent valve was open slightly. The technician turned the valve clockwise slightly to close it and the escaping gas noise stopped. This was verified by applying snoop leak detector fluid to the valve and around other joints in that area and no further leaks were identified.
HAZARD: Presence of volatile fumes, gases and vapours
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: At the other wellheads the corresponding vent valves have been inspected and found to be all okay.

TITLE: 20mm vent line pipework found disconnected
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Each heating medium boiler on the Holford GPP is supplied with gas at ~280mbar. Each gas supply has a small PRV that vents to a safe location at height. During a site tour, a Uniper employee noticed that the vent pipework had been disconnected on the downstream side of one of the PRVs. Hence, had the PRV of lifted, approx. 300 mbar gas would have vented into a cabinet (within a dsear zone 2 location) for a short period (a slam-shut valve would activate if the pressure continued to rise - isolating the release).
HAZARD: Build up of an explosive atmosphere
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Initial investigation suggests that the near hit was most likely cause by an omission or error during works by a contractor to test the PRVs in September 2018. Pipework has been tightened up and checked on the corresponding heating medium boilers.

TITLE: Poor Area Control
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A rigger lowering gypsy chains from a chain block, proceeded without the area being secured and barriered off. The rigger had asked a guardian to keep the area totally clear, but the guardian had moved elsewhere during the operation.
The rigger continued, as he considered he had full view of the landing area.

IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Confirming no risk of re-ignition, Photographs taken and reported to shift team leader. Recommendations are to use a more suitable fire proof cigarette receptacle which separates cigarette ends from flammable general waste and notices displayed to enforce this.

TITLE: Damaged air hose repaired with electrical insulation tape.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
When setting up for Unit 3 LP ST blade inspection, which means use of pneumatic hand-barring equipment, found compressed air hose defect had been repaired with many wraps of insulation tape. Possibly twice! 
This equipment is fitted with bayonet fittings now which don't require the use of whip-arrestors, (air flow is blocked if hose is unintentionally released while at pressure) but if hose had detached from fitting completely this protective feature would not have worked. 
No opportunity to use alternative hose as this is a fixed installation with fittings not common with portable air hoses. 
Temporary repair such as this with unsuitable materials is storing up potential future injury.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Whip arrestor fitted around hose and restrained to adjacent steelwork out of range of any working personnel. Recorded on GSAF and work party made aware of risk.
SAP notification 21417118 raised.

TITLE: SIS Activation HAZID 83 - GRU 20 cooling air low pressure trip
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
There was a trip on GRU 20 caused by low cooling air pressure, < 10 mbarg on pressure transmitter QCA20ZP004 (HAZID 83).

The cooling gas is delivered by fan (QCA20AM050) via a control valve (QCA20AA116) which controls the GRU 20 combustion chamber temperature at around 910 degrees.

For over an hour before the trip the pressure downstream of the fan started to decline and the control valve opened to maintain the cooling gas flow / combustion chamber temperature.

The fan delivery pressure will reduce as the control valve opens and the back pressure declines. However, when the control valve is 100% open (during the start up pre-purge) the pressure normally reads about 20 mbarg.

This suggests that the control valve opened in response to a reduced fan delivery pressure (to control the combustion chamber temperature) rather than being the immediate cause of it.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
SIS activated as it should do to trip on low pressure. 

It is not immediately apparent why the fan flow / delivery pressure declined. 

The fan is direct drive and fixed speed and unlikely to be an electrical problem (the fan has operated without any obvious issues during subsequent nominations).

One possible explanation is a blockage gradually increasing in the fan inlet which subsequently cleared.

Further investigation has focussed on the ambient temperature conditions at the time of the trip. The cooling gas pressure starts to decline at about the same time that the aftercooler temperature (EKH10CT002) noticeably drops below 0 degrees, suggesting that ice build-up on the cooling air fan inlet could be a potential cause of the blockage and the fan delivery pressure reduction.

TITLE: Lack of indication in control room that continuous monitoring of purge sample has been lost.
CASE_DESCRIPTION: There is currently no indication in the control room that a loss of continuous sample has occurred. The pump shows running even if stopped and all measured values drop and thus will never alarm (as breach levels are high levels). Potential to run for the vast majority of the purge window with no sample and thus to have an environmental breach without our knowledge. System was designed originally with a flow switch to indicate loss of sample - suggest this is re-instated.
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM: Pumps have been tested to improve confidence of continuous running, and manual readings taken 10 mins into purge as per procedure. Operators warned to regularly monitor where possible.

TITLE: CDC CW Purge pH reading low whilst purging to river
CASE_DESCRIPTION: During unit start up the CW system was put back into service with the purge valve to river opened and dosing systems reinstated. After some hunting the CW Purge pH reduced sharply to below 6.7pH at which point the purge valve started closing. The pH continued to drop over the next 30 seconds to below the permit limit of 6.5 to 6.35 and then recovered before the purge valve had time to close.  During this period the other 2 pH measurements on the system (at different points) remained as expected. Once all 3 readings were consistent the purge was opened again and dosing put into service.
HAZARD: Legal, monitoring and reporting (Non-compliance of obligations)
IMM_ACTION_TAKEN_RECOM:
Purge valve closure initiation changed from <6.7pH to <6.9pH.
Schedule 5 raised within 24 hours of detection to inform the EA on temporary low reading of purge pH

TITLE: Scope of work changed during replacement of two faulty Mediatrix units.
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Scope of work changed during planned replacement of Mediatrix units GW/002 & GW/001.  GSD incident number INC1157301 created for the initial replacement of faulty components.  During the local installation at site, the remote team decided to consolidate 7, 24 port Mediatrix units down to 2 Mediatrix's units, and cancel the replacement of the GW/001 and GW/002.  No consultation happened between the local  site engineer and the Uniper engineer to discuss this change of work scope.  As a result of the changed works scope, stakeholders were not informed of the brief interruption to the telephone system at Killingholme and MOC and work planning was not followed.
